title: حِكَايَةُ الْأَحْدَبِ
titleEn: The Hunchback's Tale, continued: The Tailor's Wife, the Jewish Doctor, the Steward and the Christian Broker; the Christian's Tale begins
part: Night 25 · The Hunchback's Tale, continued / The Christian Broker's Tale begins
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 199–211 (Night 25, continuing directly from nights-24), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 25 carries on the Tale of the Hunchback. The tailor's wife and the tailor, to be rid of the dead hunchback, prop him at a Jewish doctor's door; the doctor trips over him and passes him on to the steward of the Sultan's kitchen, who in turn leaves him in the street, where a drunken Christian broker is taken for his killer. One after another the steward, the doctor and the tailor confess to the same death before the magistrate, and the Sultan, whose jester the hunchback was, has them all brought to court. There the Christian begins a tale of his own about a young man with a severed right hand, who tells how he came to Cairo and met a woman at a cloth-merchant's stall. The night breaks off as he enters her house. Verse is copied as printed, and pointed by us only where the print has no marks. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْخَامِسَةُ وَالْعِشْرُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-khāmisatu wa-al-ʿishrūna
sentences.l: And-when was the-night the-fifth and-the-twenty,
sentences.i: And when it was the twenty-fifth night,
sentences.n: The night number is spoken as an ordinal plus the units, as in the previous nights; the edition does not number it any other way.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ امْرَأَةُ الْخَيَّاطِ لَمَّا لَقَّمَتِ الْأَحْدَبَ جَزْلَةَ السَّمَكِ مَعَ انْقِضَاءِ أَجَلِهِ مَاتَ لِسَاعَتِهِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu imraʾatu al-khayyāṭi lammā laqqamat al-aḥdaba jazlata al-samaki maʿa inqiḍāʾi ajalihi māta li-sāʿatihi
sentences.l: She-said: It-reached-me, O-you the-king the-happy, the-woman-of the-tailor, when she-fed-a-morsel the-hunchback a-chunk-of the-fish, with the-ending-of his-appointed-term, he-died at-his-hour.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O happy king, that when the tailor's wife crammed a chunk of fish into the hunchback's mouth, just as his appointed time ran out, he died on the spot.
sentences.n: After بَلَغَنِي the edition leaves out the usual أَنَّ and runs straight into امْرَأَةُ الْخَيَّاطِ, so I point it as a nominative subject, the way the sentence sounds (Classical would put it in the accusative after أَنَّ). لَقَّمَ takes two objects: the person fed (الْأَحْدَبَ) and the morsel (جَزْلَةَ السَّمَكِ). لِسَاعَتِهِ is "at his hour", that is, on the spot.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَيَّاطُ لَاحَوْلَ وَلَاقُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ مِسْكِينٌ جَاءَ مَوْتُهُ إِلَّا هَكَذَا عَلَى أَيْدِينَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khayyāṭu lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi miskīnun jāʾa mawtuhu illā hākadhā ʿalā aydīnā
sentences.l: And-said the-tailor: No power and-no strength except with-God! A-poor-man! came his-death only thus, upon our-hands.
sentences.i: The tailor said: There is no power and no strength save in God. Poor man! His death had to come like this, at our hands.
sentences.n: The edition prints لَاحَوْلَ and وَلَاقُوَّةَ with the negative glued to the next word; I keep them as printed. This is the pious exclamation of dismay: power and strength belong to God alone (إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ, "except through God"). The edition prints جاء with its hamza on the line, so it is kept as printed. جَاءَ مَوْتُهُ إِلَّا هَكَذَا is "his death came only in this way".

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ وَمَا هَذَا التَّوَانِي أَمَاسَمِعْتَ قَوْلَ الْقَائِلِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-marʾatu wa-mā hādhā al-tawānī amā samiʿta qawla al-qāʾili
sentences.l: And-said the-woman: And-what (is) this the-dawdling? Have-you-not-heard the-saying-of the-sayer:
sentences.i: But the woman said: What is this dawdling? Have you not heard the words of the poet:
sentences.n: أَمَاسَمِعْتَ is printed as one word, أَمَا ("have you not") glued to سَمِعْتَ; I keep it as one token, as printed. الْقَائِلِ, "the sayer", is the usual way of introducing a quoted line of verse. The edition prints a dash after it, which is just the sign that verse follows.

sentences.t:
مَالِيْ اُسَلِّي نَفْسِيْ بِالْمُحَالِ اِلَى * لَمْ اَلْتَقِي مِنْ حَبِيبٍ يَحْمِلَ احْزَانِي
كَيْفَ الجُلُوسُ عَلَى نَارٍ وَلَا خَمَدَتْ * اِنَّ الجُلُوسَ عَلَى النِيرَانِ خُسْرَانُ
sentences.tr:
mālī usallī nafsī bi-al-muḥāli ilā * lam altaqī min ḥabībin yaḥmila aḥzānī
kayfa al-julūsu ʿalā nārin wa-lā khamadat * inna al-julūsa ʿalā al-nīrāni khusrānu
sentences.l:
What-(is)-to-me, I-console my-self with-the-impossible, until * I-have-not-met, from a-beloved, (one who) bears my-sorrows?
How (is) the-sitting upon a-fire, and-not it-has-died-down? * Indeed the-sitting upon the-fires (is) loss.
sentences.i: Why do I console myself with the impossible, until I find no beloved to carry my sorrows? How can one sit on a fire that has not died down? To sit upon flames is nothing but loss.
sentences.n: The verse is printed pointed and is copied as printed. The first line is hard: اِلَى stands alone at the end of the first half, and I take it as "until" with an understood أَنْ, so that the sense runs "I console myself with the impossible until I have no beloved left to carry my sorrows"; I give that reading with some doubt, because the line may be damaged. Printed vowels that a grammarian would correct are left as they are: اَلْتَقِي keeps its long ī where the jussive after لَمْ would drop it, and يَحْمِلَ is printed with a fatḥa. The point of the poem for the speaker is the second line: sitting still beside a fire that is still burning is folly, so do not sit and wait.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا زَوْجُهَا وَمَا أَفْعَلُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā zawjuhā wa-mā afʿaluhu
sentences.l: And-said to-her her-husband: And-what I-do-it?
sentences.i: Her husband said to her: And what am I to do?

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لَهُ قُمْ وَاحْمِلْهُ فِي حِضْنِكَ وَانْشُرْ عَلَيْهِ فُوطَةَ حَرِيرٍ وَاخْرُجْ أَنَا قُدَّامَكَ وَأَنْتَ وَرَائِي فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ
sentences.tr: qālat lahu qum wa-aḥmilhu fī ḥiḍnika wa-anshur ʿalayhi fūṭata ḥarīrin wa-ukhruj anā quddāmaka wa-anta warāʾī fī hādhihi al-laylati
sentences.l: She-said to-him: Rise, and-carry-him in your-lap, and-spread upon-him a-cloth-of silk, and-go-out: I (am) in-front-of-you and-you behind-me, in this the-night,
sentences.i: She said to him: Get up, carry him in your arms and spread a silk cloth over him, and go out. I will walk in front of you and you behind me, tonight,
sentences.n: فُوطَة is a cloth, a wrap or towel; here it is a silk covering to hide the dead man's face. قُدَّامَكَ is the everyday word for "in front of you" (Classical أَمَامَكَ). فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ, "in this night", is simply "tonight". The sentence has no main verb for "I" and "you": the two pronouns sit in front of and behind each other, which is the whole plan.

sentences.t: وَقُلْ هَذَا وَلَدِي وَهَذِهِ أُمُّهُ رَايِحِينَ بِهِ إِلَى الطَّبِيبِ يَرَاهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qul hādhā waladī wa-hādhihi ummuhu rāyiḥīna bihi ilā al-ṭabībi yarāhu
sentences.l: and-say: This (is) my-son, and-this (is) his-mother, going with-him to the-physician, he-sees-him.
sentences.i: and say: This is my son, and this is his mother, and we are taking him to the doctor to be seen.
sentences.n: رَايِحِينَ is the colloquial "going" (from رَاحَ), a plural active participle; it is the colloquial voice of the Nights and not Classical. يَرَاهُ follows with no particle at all (Classical would want لِيَرَاهُ or أَنْ يَرَاهُ), and means "so that he may see him". The wife is rehearsing a cover story: he is a sick child.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّاسَمِعَ الْخَيَّاطُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ قَامَ وَحَمَلَ الْأَحْدَبَ فِي حِضْنِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-khayyāṭu hādhā al-kalāma qāma wa-ḥamala al-aḥdaba fī ḥiḍnihi
sentences.l: And-when he-heard the-tailor this the-speech, he-rose and-carried the-hunchback in his-lap.
sentences.i: When the tailor heard this, he got up and took the hunchback in his arms.
sentences.n: فَلَمَّاسَمِعَ is printed as one word: فَلَمَّا ("and when") glued to سَمِعَ. I keep the one token as printed.

sentences.t: وَزَوْجَتُهُ تَقُولُ يَا وَلَدِي سَلَامَتَكَ أَيْشَ يُوجِعُكَ وَهَذَا الْجُدَرِيُّ كَانَ لَكَ فِي أَيِّ مَكَانٍ
sentences.tr: wa-zawjatuhu taqūlu yā waladī salāmataka aysh yūjiʿuka wa-hādhā al-judariyyu kāna laka fī ayyi makānin
sentences.l: And-his-wife she-says: O my-son, your-safety! what hurts-you? and-this the-pox, was to-you in what place?
sentences.i: while his wife went along saying: My child, may you be well! What hurts you? And this smallpox of yours, where did it break out on you?
sentences.n: سَلَامَتَكَ is the wish "your safety!", said to a sick person ("may you be well"). أَيْشَ is the colloquial "what?", worn down from أَيُّ شَيْءٍ "which thing". الْجُدَرِيّ is smallpox. All of this is staged loudly for anyone in the street who might be listening.

sentences.t: فَكُلُّ مَنْ رَآهُمْ يَقُولُ مَعَهُمْ طِفْلٌ طَارِحَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-kullu man raʾāhum yaqūlu maʿahum ṭiflun ṭāriḥāni
sentences.l: And-every who saw-them says: with-them a-child, two-laying-low (?).
sentences.i: And everyone who saw them said: They have a sick child with them.
sentences.n: طَارِحَانِ is the obscure word here. I read it as the dual active participle of طَرَحَ, "to lay down, throw down", with the couple as its subject, so that the child is one "laid low" with sickness by the two who carry him; but it may well be a corruption (طَرِيح, "laid low, bedridden", is the nearest ordinary word). The sense is clear either way: a sick child. The edition prints رآهم with its long ā already written as آ, so I keep it.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا سَائِرِينَ وَهُمْ يَسْأَلُونَ عَنْ مَنْزِلِ الطَّبِيبِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālū sāʾirīna wa-hum yasʾalūna ʿan manzili al-ṭabībi
sentences.l: And-not they-ceased walking, and-they they-ask about the-house-of the-physician;
sentences.i: They went on walking, asking the way to the doctor's house,
sentences.n: لَمْ يَزَالُوا سَائِرِينَ is "they did not cease walking" (the Arabic way of saying "they kept on"): زَالَ with a negative takes a predicate in the accusative.

sentences.t: فَدَلُّوهُمْ إِلَى بَيْتِ طَبِيبٍ يَهُودِيٍّ فَقَرَعُوا الْبَابَ
sentences.tr: fa-dallūhum ilā bayti ṭabībin yahūdiyyin fa-qaraʿū al-bāba
sentences.l: And-they-guided-them to a-house-of a-physician, Jewish; and-they-knocked the-door.
sentences.i: and were directed to the house of a Jewish doctor, where they knocked at the door.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَتْ لَهُمْ جَارِيَةٌ سَوْدَاءُ وَفَتَحَتِ الْبَابَ وَنَظَرَتْ وَإِذَا بِإِنْسَانٍ حَامِلٍ صَغِيرً وَامْرَأَةٍ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-nazalat lahum jāriyatun sawdāʾu wa-fataḥati al-bāba wa-naẓarat wa-idhā bi-insānin ḥāmilin ṣaghīran wa-imraʾatin maʿahu
sentences.l: And-came-down to-them a-slave-girl, black; and-she-opened the-door, and-looked, and-behold with-a-person carrying a-little-one and-a-woman with-him.
sentences.i: A black slave-girl came down to them and opened the door, and she looked, and there was a man carrying a little one, with a woman beside him.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِإِنْسَانٍ is the "and behold" construction: بِـ after إِذَا of surprise only marks what appears, here a man. جَارِيَة is a slave-girl or serving-girl; the edition describes her colour plainly, سَوْدَاءُ, and that is what is translated. وَامْرَأَةٍ is genitive because it is joined to the same بِـ. The edition prints سوداء and وامرأة with their hamzas written, so they are kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ مَاخَبَرُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-jāriyatu mā khabaruka
sentences.l: And-said the-slave-girl: What (is) your-news?
sentences.i: The girl said: What is your business?
sentences.n: مَاخَبَرُكَ is printed as one word: مَا ("what") glued to خَبَرُكَ ("your news"). I keep it as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ امْرَأَةُ الْخَيَّاطِ مَعَنَا صَغِيرٌ مُرَادُنَا يَنْظُرُهُ الطَّبِيبُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati imraʾatu al-khayyāṭi maʿanā ṣaghīrun murādunā yanẓuruhu al-ṭabību
sentences.l: And-said the-woman-of the-tailor: With-us (is) a-little-one; our-wish, he-looks-at-him the-physician;
sentences.i: The tailor's wife said: We have a little one with us, and we want the doctor to look at him,
sentences.n: مُرَادُنَا يَنْظُرُهُ is "our wish (is that) he look at him": the verb comes straight after the noun with no أَنْ, which is common in the colloquial register of the Nights. The edition prints امرأة with its hamza.

sentences.t: فَخُذِي هَذَا الرُّبْعَ دِينَارٍوَ أَعْطِيهِ لِسَيِّدِكِ وَخَلِّيهِ يَنْزِلُ يَرَى وَلَدِي فَقَدْ لَحِقَهُ ضَعْفٌ
sentences.tr: fa-khudhī hādhā al-rubʿa dīnārin wa- aʿṭīhi li-sayyidiki wa-khallīhi yanzilu yarā waladī fa-qad laḥiqahu ḍaʿfun
sentences.l: so-take this the-quarter-of a-dinar, and- give-it to-your-master, and-let-him he-come-down, he-see my-son, for indeed overtook-him weakness.
sentences.i: so take this quarter-dinar and give it to your master, and ask him to come down and see my son, for a weakness has come over him.
sentences.n: The edition runs the و ("and") on to the end of دِينَارٍ, and then spaces أَعْطِيهِ apart, so that the line reads دينارو اعطيه; I keep the spacing as printed and point the و as "and" attached to the preceding word. فَخُذِي, أَعْطِيهِ and وَخَلِّيهِ are all feminine imperatives, addressed to the slave-girl, and likewise لِسَيِّدِكِ "to your master" (feminine "your"). الرُّبْعَ دِينَارٍ with the article on the first word is colloquial for "a quarter-dinar". لِـ in لِسَيِّدِكِ marks the one who receives (give it to your master). خَلِّيهِ يَنْزِلُ is "let him come down", with no particle between the two verbs.

sentences.t: فَطَلَعَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭalaʿati al-jāriyatu
sentences.l: And-went-up the-slave-girl.
sentences.i: The slave-girl went up.
sentences.n: طَلَعَ is the everyday verb for "go up", where Classical would use صَعِدَ.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَتْ زَوْجَةُ الْخَيَّاطِ دَاخِلَ الْعَتَبَةِ وَقَالَتْ لِزَوْجِهَا اتْرُكِ الْأَحْدَبَ هُنَا وَخَلِّنَا نَفُوزُ بِأَنْفُسِنَا
sentences.tr: wa-dakhalat zawjatu al-khayyāṭi dākhila al-ʿatabati wa-qālat li-zawjihā utruki al-aḥdaba hunā wa-khallinā nafūzu bi-anfusinā
sentences.l: And-entered the-wife-of the-tailor inside-of the-threshold, and-said to-her-husband: Leave the-hunchback here, and-let-us we-win with-ourselves.
sentences.i: The tailor's wife stepped inside the doorway and said to her husband: Leave the hunchback here, and let us make off with our own skins.
sentences.n: فَازَ بِنَفْسِهِ is "to win through with one's own self", that is, to escape unharmed; here بِـ marks what one carries off with one (بِأَنْفُسِنَا, "with our selves"). خَلِّنَا نَفُوزُ is "let us (go and) win", again verb after verb with no particle.

sentences.t: فَأَوْقَفَهُ الْخَيَّاطُ وَأَسْنَدَهُ إِلَى الْحَائِطِ وَخَرَجَ هُوَ وَزَوْجَتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-awqafahu al-khayyāṭu wa-asnadahu ilā al-ḥāʾiṭi wa-kharaja huwa wa-zawjatuhu
sentences.l: And-stood-him-up the-tailor, and-propped-him against the-wall, and-went-out he and-his-wife.
sentences.i: So the tailor stood him up and propped him against the wall, and he and his wife went out.
sentences.n: The edition prints الحائط with its hamza (ئ), so it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الْجَارِيَةُ فَدَخَلَتْ لِلْيَهُودِيِّ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنَّ عَلَى الْبَابِ رَجُلً مَعَهُ وَاحِدٌ ضَعِيفٌ وَمَعَهُمْ حُرْمَةٌ وَقَدْ أَعْطَوْنِي رُبْعَ دِينَارٍ لَكَ تَنْزِلُ تَشُوفُهُ وَتَصِفُ لَهُمْ مَا يُوَافِقُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-jāriyatu fa-dakhalat li-al-yahūdiyyi wa-qālat lahu inna ʿalā al-bābi rajulan maʿahu wāḥidun ḍaʿīfun wa-maʿahum ḥurmatun wa-qad aʿṭawnī rubʿa dīnārin laka tanzilu tashūfuhu wa-taṣifu lahum mā yuwāfiquhu
sentences.l: And-as-for the-slave-girl, so-she-entered to-the-Jew and-said to-him: Indeed upon the-door (is) a-man, with-him one weak, and-with-them a-woman, and-indeed they-gave-me a-quarter-of a-dinar for-you: you-come-down, you-see-him, and-you-prescribe for-them what suits-him.
sentences.i: As for the slave-girl, she went in to the Jew and said to him: There is a man at the door with someone sick, and a woman with them, and they have given me a quarter-dinar for you, if you will come down and look at him and prescribe for them whatever suits him.
sentences.n: وَأَمَّا ... فَـ is the "as for ... then" frame, which marks a change of subject. دَخَلَتْ لِلْيَهُودِيِّ is "entered to the Jew"; the colloquial verb takes لِـ here (the Classical would be دَخَلَتْ عَلَى or إِلَى). وَاحِدٌ ضَعِيفٌ, "one weak", is "a sick person". حُرْمَة is the colloquial "woman" (properly "a thing held inviolable"; it is a polite word for a woman or a wife). لَكَ تَنْزِلُ is "for you (to) come down", compressed. تَشُوفُهُ is colloquial "you see him" (شَافَ, Classical رَأَى or نَظَرَ). رَجُلً and صَغِيرً (earlier) carry tanwīn without an alif because the edition prints no alif there; I add only the vowel.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْيَهُودِيُّ الرُّبْعَ دِينَارٍ فَرِحَ وَقَامَ عَاجِلًا وَنَزَلَ فِى الظَّلَامِ فَأَوَّلَ مَاحَطَّ رِجْلَهُ عَثَرَ بِالْأَحْدَبِ وَهُوَ مَيِّتٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā al-yahūdiyyu al-rubʿa dīnārin fariḥa wa-qāma ʿājilan wa-nazala fī al-ẓalāmi fa-awwala mā ḥaṭṭa rijlahu ʿathara bi-al-aḥdabi wa-huwa mayyitun
sentences.l: And-when he-saw the-Jew the-quarter-of a-dinar, he-rejoiced, and-rose quickly, and-went-down in the-darkness; and-first (thing) what he-set his-foot, he-stumbled on-the-hunchback, and-he (was) dead.
sentences.i: When the Jew saw the quarter-dinar he was delighted, and he got up quickly and went down in the dark; and the first time he set his foot down he stumbled over the hunchback, who was dead.
sentences.n: فَأَوَّلَ مَاحَطَّ is printed with مَا glued to حَطَّ: "the first (time) that he set (his foot)". عَثَرَ بِـ is "stumble over", where the verb chooses the preposition بِـ. The edition prints فى with ى here, and I keep it as printed. وَهُوَ مَيِّتٌ is a circumstantial clause: "he being dead".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا لَلْعُزَيْرِ يَا لَمُوسَى وَالْعَشْرِ كَلِمَاتٍ يَا لَهَا رُونَ وَيُوشَعَ بْنَ نُونٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā la-al-ʿUzayri yā la-Mūsā wa-al-ʿashri kalimātin yā la-hā Rūna wa-Yūshaʿa bna Nūnin
sentences.l: And-he-said: O! to-Ezra, O! to-Moses, and-the-ten words, O! to-Aaron, and-Joshua son-of Nun!
sentences.i: He cried: O Ezra! O Moses! By the Ten Words! O Aaron! And Joshua son of Nun!
sentences.n: يَا لَـ is the cry of appeal ("O ... help!"): the لَـ with fatḥa marks the one called on. يَا لَهَا رُونَ is printed as three words with the name Hārūn broken in two (لها + رون); it must be يَا لَهَارُونَ, "O Aaron", and I keep the split as printed. وَالْعَشْرِ كَلِمَاتٍ is "and (by) the Ten Words", the Ten Commandments, taken as an oath (wa- of oath, with the genitive), though it could also be a fourth name called on. The Jewish doctor swears by his own holy names. وَيُوشَعَ بْنَ نُونٍ is accusative as one more name in the appeal.

sentences.t: كَأَنِّي عَثَرْتُ فِي هَذَا الْمَرِيضِ فَوَقَعَ إِلَى أَسْفَلَ فَمَاتَ فَكَيْفَ أَخْرُجُ بِقَتِيلٍ مِنْ بَيْتِي
sentences.tr: ka-annī ʿatharttu fī hādhā al-marīḍi fa-waqaʿa ilā asfala fa-māta fa-kayfa akhruju bi-qatīlin min baytī
sentences.l: As-though-I stumbled in this the-sick-man, so-he-fell to below, so-he-died; so-how shall-I-go-out with-a-slain-man from my-house?
sentences.i: It seems I stumbled on this sick man, and he fell down below and died; so how am I to get a corpse out of my house?
sentences.n: كَأَنِّي is printed كاني, with the hamza left off the alif, which is why it is pointed with a hamza here. عَثَرْتُ فِي is "I stumbled upon" (a second preposition for the same verb, فِي here instead of بِـ). He thinks the patient fell down the stair when he stumbled and died of the fall. خَرَجَ بِـ is "to take out, to go out with (something)", where the verb chooses the preposition. قَتِيل is "one killed", a corpse, which is the word the doctor uses.

sentences.t: فَحَمَلَهُ وَطَلَعَ بِهِ الْبَيْتَ وَأَعْلَمَ زَوْجَتَهُ بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥamalahu wa-ṭalaʿa bihi al-bayta wa-aʿlama zawjatahu bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And-he-carried-him, and-went-up with-him (to) the-house, and-informed his-wife of-that.
sentences.i: He picked him up and carried him up into the house, and told his wife of it.
sentences.n: طَلَعَ بِهِ الْبَيْتَ is "he went up with him (to) the house", with the destination in the accusative and no preposition. أَعْلَمَ زَوْجَتَهُ بِذَلِكَ: here بِـ marks what she is told (أَعْلَمَ بِـ "inform of").

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ وَمَا قُعُودُكَ إِنْ قَعَدْتَ هُنَا إِلَى طُلُوعِ النَّهَارِ رَاحَتْ أَرْوَاحُنَا أَنَا وَأَنْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu wa-mā quʿūduka in qaʿadta hunā ilā ṭulūʿi al-nahāri rāḥat arwāḥunā anā wa-anta
sentences.l: And-she-said to-him: And-what (is) your-sitting? If you-sit here till the-rising-of the-day, will-go our-souls, I and-you.
sentences.i: She said to him: What are you sitting there for? If you stay here until daybreak, we are both dead, you and I.
sentences.n: رَاحَتْ أَرْوَاحُنَا, "our souls have gone", is the answer to the condition إِنْ قَعَدْتَ, and uses the perfect for a sure future outcome. The closing أَنَا وَأَنْتَ, "I and you", spells out who the "our" of أَرْوَاحُنَا is.

sentences.t: نَطْلَعُ بِهِ السَّطْحَ وَنَرْمِيهِ فِي بَيْتِ جَارِنَا الْمُسْلِمِ
sentences.tr: naṭlaʿu bihi al-saṭḥa wa-narmīhi fī bayti jārinā al-muslimi
sentences.l: We-go-up with-him (to) the-roof, and-we-throw-him into the-house-of our-neighbour the-Muslim.
sentences.i: Let us take him up to the roof and throw him down into our Muslim neighbour's house.
sentences.n: نَطْلَعُ and نَرْمِيهِ are in the indicative with the force of "let us"; the colloquial uses the plain present for an urging. جَارِنَا الْمُسْلِمِ, "our neighbour the Muslim", names his religion because the Jewish couple choose to pass the corpse to a house of another faith.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ جَارُهُ رَجُلًا شَاهِدًا مُشْرِفًا عَلَى مَطْبَخِ السُّلْطَانِ وَهُوَ كَثِيرٌ مَا يَأْتِي بِالدُّهْنِ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ وَتَأْكُلُ الْقِطَطُ وَالْفِيرَانُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna jāruhu rajulan shāhidan mushrifan ʿalā maṭbakhi al-sulṭāni wa-huwa kathīrun mā yaʾtī bi-al-duhni ilā baytihi wa-taʾkulu al-qiṭaṭu wa-al-fīrānu
sentences.l: And-was his-neighbour a-man, a-steward, overseeing over the-kitchen-of the-sultan; and-he (is) much what he-brings with-the-fat to his-house, and-eat the-cats and-the-mice.
sentences.i: Now this neighbour was a steward, an overseer of the sultan's kitchen; he often brought fat home to his house, and the cats and the rats would eat it.
sentences.n: شَاهِد here is an official title, an overseer or steward (not "witness"); the print then adds مُشْرِفًا عَلَى, "overlooking", to say what he oversees: the sultan's kitchen. كَثِيرٌ مَا يَأْتِي is printed so, "much (is) what he brings", for "he often brings" (Classical would be كَثِيرًا مَا). يَأْتِي بِـ is "bring": the verb chooses the بِـ. الدُّهْن is cooking fat. الْفِيرَان is the colloquial plural of فَأْرَة, "mice, rats". The edition prints يأتي with its hamza, so it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ طَابَ طَرَفُ لَيْلَةٍ تَنْزِلُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِلَابُ مِنَ السُّطُوحِ وَيَجُرُّونَهُ وَقَدْ آذَوْهُ كَثِيرًا فِي جَمِيعِ مَا يَأْتِي بِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-in ṭāba ṭarafu laylatin tanzilu ʿalayhi al-kilābu min al-suṭūḥi wa-yajurrūnahu wa-qad ādhawhu kathīran fī jamīʿi mā yaʾtī bihi
sentences.l: And-if became-good a-portion-of a-night, come-down upon-it the-dogs from the-roofs, and-they-drag-it; and-indeed they-harmed-him much in all-of what he-brings with-it.
sentences.i: and given half a chance on any night, the dogs come down on it from the rooftops and drag it away; they have cost him a great deal of what he brings.
sentences.n: وَإِنْ طَابَ طَرَفُ لَيْلَةٍ is obscure. Literally it is "if a portion (or end) of a night turns pleasant", and I take it as "if some stretch of the night is quiet", that is, whenever the dogs get their chance; the reading is uncertain, and طَرَف may even be a slip. آذَوْهُ, "they harmed him", is printed with the long آ already written, and I keep it. فِي جَمِيعِ مَا يَأْتِي بِهِ means "in respect of all that he brings", that is, the neighbour is already put out by the dogs.

sentences.t: فَطَلَعَ الْيَهُودِيُّ وَ زَوْجَتُهُ وَهُمْ حَامِلِينَ الْأَحْدَبَ وَأَنْزَلُوهُ بِيَدَيْهِ وَرِجْلَيْهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭalaʿa al-yahūdiyyu wa- zawjatuhu wa-hum ḥāmilīna al-aḥdaba wa-anzalūhu bi-yadayhi wa-rijlayhi ilā al-arḍi
sentences.l: And-went-up the-Jew and- his-wife, and-they carrying the-hunchback, and-they-lowered-him by-his-two-hands and-his-two-feet to the-ground.
sentences.i: The Jew and his wife went up, carrying the hunchback, and lowered him by his hands and feet to the ground.
sentences.n: The edition breaks the line after وَ and starts زَوْجَتُهُ on the next, so the و ("and") stands apart from its word; I keep it as printed. وَهُمْ حَامِلِينَ is Middle Arabic: a plural "they" followed by a participle in the accusative-genitive ending -īna, where Classical would say وَهُمَا حَامِلَانِ (a dual, for the two of them). بِيَدَيْهِ وَرِجْلَيْهِ is "by his hands and his feet": they held him by the limbs to let him down, and بِـ marks what they held him by.

sentences.t: وَخَلَّوْهُ مُلَاصِقَ الْحَائِطِ وَأَنْزَلُوهُ وَانْصَرَفُوا وَمَالَحِقُوا يُنْزِلُونَ الْأَحْدَبَ إِلَّا وَالشَّاهِدُ جَاءَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَفَتَحَهُ وَطَلَعَ وَمَعَهُ شَمْعَةٌ مَوْقُودَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-khallawhu mulāṣiqa al-ḥāʾiṭi wa-anzalūhu wa-inṣarafū wa-mā laḥiqū yunzilūna al-aḥdaba illā wa-al-shāhidu jāʾa ilā al-bayti wa-fataḥahu wa-ṭalaʿa wa-maʿahu shamʿatun mawqūdatun
sentences.l: And-they-left-him adjoining the-wall, and-lowered-him, and-turned-away; and-not they-had-time (to) lower the-hunchback, but the-steward came to the-house, and-opened-it, and-went-up, and-with-him a-candle, lit.
sentences.i: They left him standing close against the wall, and went away; they had barely finished lowering the hunchback when the steward came to the house, opened it and came up, with a lit candle in his hand.
sentences.n: وَمَالَحِقُوا is printed with مَا glued to the verb; مَا لَحِقُوا يُنْزِلُونَ ... إِلَّا وَـ is "they had hardly managed to lower ... when" (the idiom ما ... إلا و). The repeated وَأَنْزَلُوهُ, "and they lowered him", appears twice in the print, here and just before; it may be a compositor's repeat, and I give it as printed. مُلَاصِقَ الْحَائِطِ is "adjoining the wall", in the accusative as a state. جَاءَ is printed with its hamza on the line.

sentences.t: فَطَلَعَ فِى الْبَيْتِ فَوَجَدَ ابْنَ آدَمَ وَاقِفًا فِي زَاوِيَةٍ تَحْتَ الْبَابِ الْبَادِ هَنْجِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭalaʿa fī al-bayti fa-wajada ibna Ādama wāqifan fī zāwiyatin taḥta al-bābi al-bādi hanji
sentences.l: And-he-went-up in the-house, and-found a-son-of Adam standing in a-corner under the-door, the-wind-catcher.
sentences.i: He went up into the house and found a human being standing in a corner beneath the door, under the ventilator.
sentences.n: ابْن آدَم, "a son of Adam", is simply "a human being" (a man, not an animal), and it matters later in the steward's speech. الْبَادِ هَنْجِ is printed as two words; it is the Persian بادهنج, a wind-catcher or air-shaft that sits over a house, here the corner under it. The Persian word is cut in two by the print, and I leave the space where it is. The edition prints آدم with the long آ, so it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الشَّاهِدُ وَاهْ وَاللَّهِ طَيِّبٌ إِنَّ الَّذِي يَسْرِقُ حَرَامِيٌّ مَا هُوَإِلَّا ابْنُ آدَمَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-shāhidu wāh wa-Allāhi ṭayyibun inna al-ladhī yasriqu ḥarāmiyyun mā huwa illā ibnu Ādama
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-steward: Ah! by-God, good! Indeed the-one-who steals (is) a-thief; not he (is) except a-son-of Adam.
sentences.i: The steward said to him: Aha! By God, so that is it! The one who has been stealing is a thief, and he is nothing but a human being!
sentences.n: وَاهْ is a colloquial interjection of surprise or discovery. طَيِّبٌ is "good, fine", used as an exclamation ("very well!"). حَرَامِيّ is the colloquial "thief" (from حَرَام, "forbidden, illicit"), and I give it the nominative the sentence needs. مَا هُوَإِلَّا is printed as one word, هُوَ glued to إِلَّا, and I keep it so. The point the steward is making is that the thief is a human being and not a cat or a dog: he has always put the losses down to animals.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لِهَذَا اللَّحْمِ وَالدُّهْنِ تَأْخُذُهُ أَنْتَ وَأَنَا أَحْسِبُهُ مِنَ الْقِطَطِ وَالْكِلَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-ltafata ilayhi wa-qāla li-hādhā al-laḥmi wa-al-duhni taʾkhudhuhu anta wa-anā aḥsibuhu min al-qiṭaṭi wa-al-kilābi
sentences.l: And-he-turned to-him and-said: For-this the-meat and-the-fat, you-take-it, you, and-I I-reckon-it from the-cats and-the-dogs?
sentences.i: He turned to him and said: So it is you who takes this meat and fat, while I put it down to the cats and dogs?
sentences.n: The opening لِهَذَا is not easy: I read it as "as for this meat and fat" (لِـ introducing the topic), then "you take it, and I reckon it (a loss) to the cats and dogs", so as a bitter question; it could also be read as "is it for this that ...?". مِنَ in أَحْسِبُهُ مِنَ الْقِطَطِ means "I count it as coming from" the cats, that is, as their doing.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا قَتَلْتُ قِطَطَ الْحَارَةِ وَكِلَابَهَا وَدَخَلْتُ فِي خَطِيئَتِهِمْ وَأَنْتَ تَنْزِلُ مِنَ السُّطُوحِ
sentences.tr: wa-anā qataltu qiṭaṭa al-ḥārati wa-kilābahā wa-dakhaltu fī khaṭīʾatihim wa-anta tanzilu min al-suṭūḥi
sentences.l: And-I killed the-cats-of the-quarter and-its-dogs, and-entered into their-sin, and-you you-come-down from the-roofs.
sentences.i: I have killed the cats of the quarter and its dogs and taken their sin upon myself, and all the while you were coming down from the rooftops!
sentences.n: دَخَلْتُ فِي خَطِيئَتِهِمْ is "I entered into their sin", that is, I took on the guilt of killing the animals. The edition prints خطيئتهم with its hamza (ئ), so it is kept as printed. الْحَارَة is the colloquial "quarter, lane" (Classical حَارَة is the same word); كِلَابَهَا is "its dogs", the dogs of the quarter.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذَ مِطْرَقَةً عَظِيمَةً وَهَمَزَ بِهَا وَصَارَ عِنْدَهُ وَضَرَبَهُ عَلَى صَدْرِهِ فَوَجَدَهُ مَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma akhadha miṭraqatan ʿaẓīmatan wa-hamaza bihā wa-ṣāra ʿindahu wa-ḍarabahu ʿalā ṣadrihi fa-wajadahu māta
sentences.l: Then he-took a-mallet, huge, and-thrust with-it, and-became beside-him, and-struck-him on his-chest, and-found-him he-had-died.
sentences.i: Then he took a huge mallet, lunged with it, stepped up to him and struck him on the chest, and found that he was dead.
sentences.n: هَمَزَ بِهَا is obscure. The verb is "to prod, to jab", and with the mallet I take it as a lunge or a swing that gets him moving; I give that reading with some doubt. صَارَ عِنْدَهُ is "he came to be beside him", that is, he went up to him. مَاتَ follows وَجَدَهُ with no قَدْ, "found him (that) he had died".

sentences.t: فَحَزِنَ وَقَالَ لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ وَخَافَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ وَقَٰلَ لَعَنَ اللَّهُ الدُّهْنَ وَاللِّيَةَ وَكَيْفَ فَرَغَتْ مَنِيَّةُ هَذَا الرَّجُلِ عَلَى يَدَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥazina wa-qāla lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi al-ʿaliyyi al-ʿaẓīmi wa-khāfa ʿalā nafsihi wa-qāla laʿana Allāhu al-duhna wa-al-liyyata wa-kayfa faraghat maniyyatu hādhā al-rajuli ʿalā yadayya
sentences.l: And-he-grieved, and-said: No power and-no strength except with-God the-High, the-Mighty; and-he-feared for himself, and-he-said: May-God-curse the-fat and-the-tail-fat! and-how was-finished the-doom-of this the-man upon my-two-hands?
sentences.i: He grew sorrowful and said: There is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. And he feared for himself, and said: God curse the fat and the tail-fat! And how did this man's doom come to be fulfilled at my hands?
sentences.n: The edition prints قل for قال in وَقَٰلَ, which is read qāla, "he said", and is pointed with the dagger alif; it is a slip of the print. اللِّيَة is the print's spelling of اللَّيَّة or اِلْيَة, the fat tail of a sheep, run together with the article. The pointing here is only my best reading. مَنِيَّة is "fate, doom" (the day of one's death); فَرَغَتْ is "was finished, ran out". عَلَى يَدَيَّ is "at my two hands", that is, by my doing.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ فَإِذَا هُوَ أَحْدَبُ
sentences.tr: thumma naẓara ilayhi fa-idhā huwa aḥdabu
sentences.l: Then he-looked at-him, and-behold he (was) a-hunchback.
sentences.i: Then he looked at him, and saw that he was a hunchback.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ مَايَكْفِى أَنَّكَ أَحْدَبُ حَتَّى تَصِيرَ حَرَامِيًّا وَتَسْرِقَ اللَّحْمَ وَالدُّهْنَ يَاسَتَّارُ اسْتُرْنِي بِسِتْرِكَ الْجَمِيلِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla mā yakfī annaka aḥdabu ḥattā taṣīra ḥarāmiyyan wa-tasriqa al-laḥma wa-al-duhna yā-sattāru usturnī bi-sitrika al-jamīli
sentences.l: And-he-said: Not it-suffices that-you (are) a-hunchback, until you-become a-thief, and-steal the-meat and-the-fat! O-Concealer, cover-me with-your-covering, the-beautiful.
sentences.i: He said: Is it not enough that you are a hunchback, that you must turn thief and steal meat and fat? O Concealer, cover me with your fair covering!
sentences.n: مَايَكْفِى is printed as one word, with the ى the edition uses for the final ī; I keep it as printed, and it reads "does it not suffice?". حَتَّى with the subjunctive means "until, so far as to". يَاسَتَّارُ is printed as one word: يَا ("O") glued to سَتَّار, "the Concealer", a name of God who covers sins and faults; the plea is that God cover him with a fair cover (سِتْر) so that the killing is not found out. اسْتُرْنِي بِسِتْرِكَ uses بِـ for the means: "cover me with your covering".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَمَلَهُ عَلَى أَكْتَافِهِ وَنَزَلَ بِهِ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ آخِرَ اللَّيْلِ وَمَا زَالَ بِهِ أَىْ أَوَّلَ السُّوقِ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥamalahu ʿalā aktāfihi wa-nazala bihi min baytihi ākhira al-layli wa-mā zāla bihi ay awwala al-sūqi
sentences.l: Then he-carried-him upon his-shoulders, and-went-down with-him from his-house (at) the-end-of the-night, and-not he-ceased with-him, that-is, (to) the-beginning-of the-market.
sentences.i: Then he lifted him onto his shoulders and went down with him from his house at the end of the night, and he kept going with him as far as the head of the market,
sentences.n: أَىْ is printed اى. I read it as أَيْ, "that is", which explains how far he went ("that is, to the head of the market"); it may instead stand for إِلَى with a letter dropped, "as far as", and the sense comes out the same. مَا زَالَ بِهِ is "he went on with him", with بِـ for the one he was carrying. The edition prints آخر with the long آ, so it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَأَوْقَفَهُ بِجَانِبِ دُكَّانٍ فِي رَأْسِ عَطْفَةٍ وَتَرَكَهُ وَرَاحَ
sentences.tr: fa-awqafahu bi-jānibi dukkānin fī raʾsi ʿaṭfatin wa-tarakahu wa-rāḥa
sentences.l: And-he-stood-him by-the-side-of a-shop, at the-head-of a-lane, and-left-him, and-went-off.
sentences.i: and stood him up beside a shop at the head of a lane, and left him and went off.
sentences.n: دُكَّان is a shop or a shop's stone bench; عَطْفَة is a side-lane or turning. بِجَانِبِ means "at the side of", where بِـ gives the place ("by the side of"). The edition prints رأس with its hamza, so it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِنَصْرَانِيٍّ سِمْسَارِ السُّلْطَانِ وَكَانَ سَكْرَانَ فَخَرَجَ يُرِيدُ الْحَمَّامَ فَقَالَلَهُ سُكْرُهُ إِنَّ التَّسْبِيحَ قَرِيبٌ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-naṣrāniyyin simsāri al-sulṭāni wa-kāna sakrāna fa-kharaja yurīdu al-ḥammāma fa-qālalahu sukruhu inna al-tasbīḥa qarībun
sentences.l: And-behold, with-a-Christian, broker-of the-sultan, and-he-was drunk; so-he-went-out wanting the-bath, and-said-to-him his-drunkenness that the-glorification (is) near.
sentences.i: And behold, there was a Christian, the sultan's broker, who was drunk. He went out, wanting the bathhouse, and his drunkenness told him that the dawn chanting was near.
sentences.n: فقالله is one printed word, فقال له, "and said to him"; I keep it as one token. The subject is سكره, "his drunkenness": he is so far gone that his own intoxication is what tells him the hour. التسبيح is the "glorification" (of God), the chant from the minarets that comes before dawn; I take it so, but the print gives no more than the word. The بِـ after وَإِذَا only marks what appears.

sentences.t: فَمَا زَالَ يَمْشِي وَيَتَمَايَلُ حَتَّى قَرُبَ مِنَ الْأَحْدَبِ وَجَلَسَ يَبُولُ قُبَالَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-mā zāla yamshī wa-yatamāyalu ḥattā qaruba mina al-aḥdabi wa-jalasa yabūlu qubālahu
sentences.l: So-he-did-not cease walking and-swaying until he-drew-near from the-hunchback, and-sat urinating opposite-him.
sentences.i: He kept on walking and swaying until he drew near the hunchback, and he sat down to urinate right in front of him.
sentences.n: مَا زَالَ + imperfect is "he kept on doing". The hunchback is the dead body of the story, propped up where the tailor's wife and the Jew had left him; the drunk does not know it. قُبَالَهُ is "opposite him".

sentences.t: فَلَاحَتْ مِنْهُ الْتِفَاتَةٌ وَإِذَا بِوَاحِدٍ وَاقِفٍ وَكَانَ النَّصْرَانِيُّ خَطَفُوا عِمَامَتَهُ فِي أَوَّلِ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lāḥat minhu iltifātatun wa-idhā bi-wāḥidin wāqifin wa-kāna al-naṣrāniyyu khaṭafū ʿimāmatahu fī awwali tilka al-laylati
sentences.l: So-appeared from-him a-glance, and-behold, with-one standing; and-was the-Christian, they-had-snatched his-turban, in the-beginning-of that the-night.
sentences.i: He happened to glance aside, and behold, someone was standing there. Now the Christian's turban had been snatched from him at the start of that very night.
sentences.n: فلاحت منه التفاتة is "a glance showed itself from him": he chanced to look round. وَكَانَ النَّصْرَانِيُّ خَطَفُوا عِمَامَتَهُ sets the subject first and then gives a plural verb with no subject of its own, the Middle Arabic way of saying "people had snatched his turban"; Classical grammar would not allow it, so I point it as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْأَحْدَبَ قَائِمًا اعْتَقَدَأَنَّهُ يُرِيدُ يَخْطِفُ عِمَامَتَهُ فَطَبَّقَ كَفَّهُ وَلَكَمَ الْأَحْدَبَ عَلَى رَقَبَتِهِ فَوَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā al-aḥdaba qāʾiman iʿtaqada annahu yurīdu yakhṭifu ʿimāmatahu fa-ṭabbaqa kaffahu wa-lakama al-aḥdaba ʿalā raqabatihi fa-waqaʿa ʿalā al-arḍi
sentences.l: So-when he-saw the-hunchback standing, he-believed-that-he wants (he-)snatches his-turban; so-he-closed his-palm and-punched the-hunchback on his-neck, and-he-fell upon the-ground.
sentences.i: When he saw the hunchback standing there, he took it that the man meant to snatch his turban. So he clenched his fist and punched the hunchback on the neck, and the hunchback fell to the ground.
sentences.n: اعتقدانه is one printed word, اعتقد انه, "he believed that he"; I keep it as one token. يُرِيدُ يَخْطِفُ, "he wants (he) snatches", has no أَنْ between the two verbs: ordinary Middle Arabic. طَبَّقَ كَفَّهُ is "he closed his hand", that is, made a fist.

sentences.t: وَصَرَخَ النَّصْرَانِيُّ عَلَى خَفِيرِ السُّوقِ وَنَزَلَ عَلَى الْأَحْدَبِ مِنْ شِدَّةِ سُكْرِهِ وَبَقِيَ يَلْكُمُهُ وَيَخْنُقُهُ خَنْقًا
sentences.tr: wa-ṣarakha al-naṣrāniyyu ʿalā khafīri al-sūqi wa-nazala ʿalā al-aḥdabi min shiddati sukrihi wa-baqiya yalkumuhu wa-yakhnuquhu khanqan
sentences.l: And-cried-out the-Christian at the-watchman-of the-market, and-came-down upon the-hunchback from the-intensity-of his-drunkenness, and-remained punching-him and-throttling-him a-throttling.
sentences.i: The Christian shouted for the market watchman, and in the violence of his drunkenness he fell on the hunchback and kept on punching him and throttling him hard.
sentences.n: خَنْقًا is the cognate accusative: "throttling him a throttling", for emphasis. نَزَلَ عَلَى is "came down on", here "set upon".

sentences.t: فَجَاءَ الْخَفِيرُ فَوَجَدَ النَّصْرَانِيَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِ وَهُوَ يَلْكُمُهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَفِيرُ مَالِهَذَا
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾa al-khafīru fa-wajada al-naṣrāniyya bārik ʿalā al-muslimi wa-huwa yalkumuhu fa-qāla lahu al-khafīru mā li-hādhā
sentences.l: So-came the-watchman and-found the-Christian kneeling upon the-Muslim, and-he punching-him; and-said to-him the-watchman: What for-this-one?
sentences.i: The watchman came and found the Christian crouched on top of the Muslim, punching him. "What is the matter with this man?" the watchman asked him.
sentences.n: مالهذا is one printed word, ما لهذا, literally "what (is) for this one?", that is, "what is wrong with him?"; I keep it as one token. بَارِكْ, printed without the alif of the accusative circumstantial (Classical بَارِكًا), is the participle of بَرَكَ, "to kneel, to crouch", used of a camel and here of a man squatting on his victim.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّصْرَانِيُّ هَذَا أَرَادَأَنْ يَخْطِفَ عِمَا مَتِي فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَفِيرُ قُمْ عَنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-naṣrāniyyu hādhā arāda an yakhṭifa ʿimā matī fa-qāla lahu al-khafīru qum ʿanhu
sentences.l: So-said to-him the-Christian: This-one wanted-that he-snatch my-tur ban. So-said to-him the-watchman: Get-up off-him.
sentences.i: "This man meant to snatch my turban," the Christian told him. "Get off him," said the watchman.
sentences.n: ارادان is one printed word, اراد ان, "he wanted that"; I keep it as one token. عما متي is the print's split of عمامتي, "my turban": عما and متي are the two halves of one word, and I point each half as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ فَتَقَدَّمَ إِلَيْهِ فَوَجَدَهُ مَيِّتًا فَقَالَ الْخَفِيرُ وَاللَّهِ طَيِّبٌ نَصْرَانِيٌّ يَقْتُلُ مُسْلِمًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma fa-taqaddama ilayhi fa-wajadahu mayyitan fa-qāla al-khafīru wa-allāhi ṭayyibun naṣrāniyyun yaqtulu muslimān
sentences.l: So-he-rose, and-the-other-advanced to-him and-found-him dead; and-said the-watchman: By-God, fine! a-Christian kills a-Muslim!
sentences.i: The Christian got up, and the watchman stepped up to the body and found it dead. "By God, that is fine!" said the watchman. "A Christian killing a Muslim!"
sentences.n: The print does not name who rose and who stepped forward: the Christian gets up off the body, and the watchman goes to look. طَيِّبٌ, "good, fine", is the watchman's bitter irony. The verbs قام and تقدم have no stated subjects; I have supplied them in the idiomatic layer.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَسَكَ الْخَفِيرُ النَّصْرَانِيَّ وَكَتَّفَهُ وَجَاءَ بِهِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْوَالِي
sentences.tr: thumma masaka al-khafīru al-naṣrāniyya wa-kattafahu wa-jāʾa bihi ilā bayti al-wālī
sentences.l: Then seized the-watchman the-Christian and-bound-his-arms-of-him and-came with-him to the-house-of the-governor.
sentences.i: Then the watchman seized the Christian, tied his arms, and brought him to the governor's house.
sentences.n: مَسَكَ is the colloquial "to seize, to hold", for Classical أَمْسَكَ. كَتَّفَهُ is "he tied his arms behind him", from كَتِف, "shoulder". جَاءَ بِـ is the ordinary "to bring", literally "to come with".

sentences.t: وَالنَّصْرَانِيُّ يَقُولُ فِي نَفْسِهِ يَا مَسِيحُ يَا عَذْرَاءُ كَيْفَ قَتَلْتُ هَذَا وَمَا أَسْرَعَ مَا مَاتَ مِنْ لَكْمَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-al-naṣrāniyyu yaqūlu fī nafsihi yā masīḥu yā ʿadhrāʾu kayfa qataltu hādhā wa-mā asraʿa mā māta min lakmatin wāḥidatin
sentences.l: And-the-Christian says in his-self: O Messiah, O Virgin! How did-I-kill this-one, and-what quickly (is) what he-died from a-punch one!
sentences.i: And the Christian was saying to himself, "O Messiah! O Virgin! How did I kill this man? How quickly he died, from a single punch!"
sentences.n: وَمَا أَسْرَعَ مَا مَاتَ is the exclamatory pattern مَا أَفْعَلَهُ: "how swiftly he died!", with the second مَا as the relative or the noun-making particle. يَقُولُ فِي نَفْسِهِ, "says in his self", is "says to himself".

sentences.t: فَرَاحَتِ السَّكْرَةُ وَجَاءَتِ الْفِكْرَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-rāḥati al-sakratu wa-jāʾati al-fikratu
sentences.l: So-went the-drunkenness, and-came the-thought.
sentences.i: The drunkenness left him, and sober thought came.
sentences.n: A small piece of rhymed prose: السَّكْرَةُ and الْفِكْرَةُ rhyme, and the proverb-like balance of "went" and "came" is part of the effect. رَاحَ is "to go away".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ السِّمْسَارَ وَالْأَحْدَبَ وَالنَّصْرَانِيَّ بَاتُوا فِي بَيْتِ الْوَالِي إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-simsāra wa-al-aḥdaba wa-al-naṣrāniyya bātū fī bayti al-wālī ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: Then indeed the-broker and-the-hunchback and-the-Christian spent-the-night in the-house-of the-governor until the-morning.
sentences.i: Then the broker, the hunchback and the Christian spent the night in the governor's house until morning.
sentences.n: As printed, three persons are listed, but السمسار, "the broker", and النصراني are the same man: the Christian is the sultan's broker. The plural بَاتُوا is the print's; I point it as it stands and do not try to repair the count. The hunchback, of course, is the body.

sentences.t: وَأَصْبَحَ الْوَالِي طَلَعَ فَأَمَرَ بِشَنْقِ الْقَاتِلِ وَأَمَرَ الْمَشَاعِلِيَّ أَنْ يُنَادِيَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-aṣbaḥa al-wālī ṭalaʿa fa-amara bi-shanqi al-qātili wa-amara al-mashāʿiliyya an yunādiya ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And-became-morning the-governor, (he-)went-up, and-commanded with-the-hanging-of the-killer, and-commanded the-torchbearer that he-proclaim against-him.
sentences.i: In the morning the governor went up and commanded that the killer be hanged. He told the executioner to proclaim it against him.
sentences.n: أَصْبَحَ الْوَالِي طَلَعَ puts two verbs side by side with no connecting word: "the governor rose, went up". المشاعلي is the mashʿalī, literally the torch-bearer, the officer who carries out sentences. أَمَرَ بِـ is "to command (something)", the verb choosing the preposition; بِشَنْقِ is "the hanging of". نَادَى عَلَيْهِ is "to cry out about him", a public proclamation of the sentence.

sentences.t: وَ نَصَبَ لِلنَّصْرَانِيِّ خَشَبَةً وَأَوْقَفَهُ تَحْتَهَا وَجَاءَ الْمَشَاعِلِيُّ رَمَى فِي رَقَبَةِ النَّصْرَانِيِّ الْحَبْلَ وَأَرَادَأَنْ يُعَلِّقَهُ
sentences.tr: wa nasaba li-al-naṣrāniyyi khashabatan wa-awqafahu taḥtahā wa-jāʾa al-mashāʿiliyyu ramā fī raqabati al-naṣrāniyyi al-ḥabla wa-arāda an yuʿalliqahu
sentences.l: And he-set-up for-the-Christian a-timber, and-made-him-stand under-it; and-came the-torchbearer, (he-)threw on the-neck-of the-Christian the-rope, and-wanted-that he-hang-him.
sentences.i: He had a gallows erected for the Christian and stood him beneath it. The executioner came, threw the rope around the Christian's neck, and made ready to hang him.
sentences.n: The print leaves a line break after the و, so وَ and نَصَبَ are two tokens; I point them as printed. The لِـ in لِلنَّصْرَانِيِّ marks the one for whom the gallows is set up: "for the Christian". خَشَبَةً, "a timber", is the gallows. جَاءَ الْمَشَاعِلِيُّ رَمَى has two verbs side by side, "came, threw". ارادان is one printed word, اراد ان; I keep it as one token.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالشَّاهِدِ قَدْ شَقَّ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ فَرَأَى النَّصْرَانِيَّ وَ هُوَ رَائِحٌ يُشْنَقُ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-shāhidi qad shaqqa bayna al-nāsi fa-raʾā al-naṣrāniyya wa huwa rāʾiḥun yushnaqu
sentences.l: And-behold, with-the-steward, he-had-cleaved between the-people, and-saw the-Christian, and he going-off to-be-hanged.
sentences.i: And behold, the steward had pushed his way through the crowd, and he saw the Christian, who was about to be hanged.
sentences.n: الشَّاهِد is the same man introduced earlier as شَاهِد, the overseer of the sultan's kitchen, whose house the hunchback was lowered into; the print gives him the same title each time, so the translation calls him "the steward" throughout. The و and هو are two tokens in print, split by a line break. رَائِحٌ is "going"; with a following verb it means "about to". The بِـ after وَإِذَا only marks what appears.

sentences.t: فَفَسَحَ النَّاسَ وَقَالَ لِلْمَشَاعِلِيِّ لَا تَفْعَلْ أَنَا الَّذِي قَتَلْتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-fasaḥa al-nāsa wa-qāla li-al-mashāʿiliyyi lā tafʿal anā al-ladhī qataltuhu
sentences.l: So-he-made-room (among) the-people, and-said to-the-torchbearer: Do-not do; I (am) the-one-who I-killed-him.
sentences.i: He cleared the people aside and said to the executioner, "Do not do it! I am the one who killed him."
sentences.n: فَسَحَ النَّاسَ, "he made room among the people", takes the crowd as a direct object; the sense is that he made them give way. قَالَ لِـ is "said to", with لِـ marking the person addressed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَالِي لِأَيِّ شَيٍّ قَتَلْتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wālī li-ayyi shayyin qataltahu
sentences.l: So-said to-him the-governor: For what thing did-you-kill-him?
sentences.i: The governor said to him, "Why did you kill him?"
sentences.n: لِأَيِّ شَيٍّ is "for what thing?", that is, "why?". The print writes شي without the hamza (شَيْء), the everyday spelling; I point what is printed, with tanwīn.

sentences.t: قَالَ إِنِّي طَلَعْتُ اللَّيْلَةَ بَيْتِي فَرَأَيْتُهُ نَزَلَ مِنَ الْبَادْ هَنْجِ وَسَرَقَ رَحْلِي فَضَرَبْتُهُ بِمِطْرَقَةٍ عَلَى صَدْرِهِ فَمَاتَ فَحَمَلْنَهُ
sentences.tr: qāla innī ṭalaʿtu al-layla bayti fa-raʾaytuhu nazala mina al-bād hanji wa-saraqa raḥlī fa-ḍarabtuhu bi-miṭraqatin ʿalā ṣadrihi fa-māta fa-ḥamalnahu
sentences.l: He-said: Indeed-I went-up tonight (to) my-house, and-saw-him, he-came-down from the-bādhanj, and-stole my-baggage; so-I-struck-him with-a-hammer on his-chest, and-he-died, and-carried-him.
sentences.i: He said, "Tonight I went up to my house, and I saw him come down from the roof ventilator and steal my belongings. So I struck him on the chest with a hammer, and he died. Then I carried him.
sentences.n: طَلَعْتُ بَيْتِي, "I went up (to) my house", has no preposition before the noun: ordinary colloquial usage. الباد هنج is printed as two words: the bādhanj (Persian bād, "wind"), the wind-catcher or ventilation shaft that opens in a roof. نَزَلَ, "he came down", follows رَأَيْتُهُ with no connecting word. رَحْلِي is "my baggage, my gear". The last word, فحملنه, is printed with a nūn where the sense wants a tā': it should be فحملته, "and I carried him" (the following verb is first person singular). It may be a compositor's slip. I point it as printed, so the form reads as a feminine plural, "they (f.) carried him", which cannot be meant; the translation follows the sense.

sentences.t: وَجِئْتُ إِلَى السُّوقِ وَأَوْقَفْتُهُ فِي مَوْضِعِ كَذَا فِي عَطْفَةِ كَذَا
sentences.tr: wa-jiʾtu ilā al-sūqi wa-awqaftuhu fī mawḍiʿi kadhā fī ʿaṭfati kadhā
sentences.l: And-I-came to the-market, and-stood-him in (the)-place-of such, in (the)-turning-of such.
sentences.i: Then I went to the market and stood him up in such-and-such a place, in such-and-such an alley."
sentences.n: كَذَا is "such-and-such", the speaker's own way of not naming the exact spot. عَطْفَة is a turning, a side-lane, an alley.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ الشَّاهِدُ مَاكَفَانِي أَنِّي قَتَلْتُ مُسْلِمًا حَتَّى أَقْتُلَ نَصْرَانِيًّا فَلَا تَشْنُقْ غَيْرِي
sentences.tr: thumma qāla al-shāhidu mā kafānī annī qataltu muslimān ḥattā aqtula naṣrāniyyan fa-lā tashnuq ghayrī
sentences.l: Then said the-steward: Did-it-not-suffice-me that I-killed a-Muslim, until I-kill a-Christian? So-do-not hang other-than-me.
sentences.i: Then the steward said, "Was it not enough for me that I killed a Muslim, that I should also kill a Christian? Hang no one but me."
sentences.n: ماكفاني is one printed word, ما كفاني; I keep it as one token. The sentence is a rhetorical question without a question word: "it did not suffice me ... " meaning "was it not enough?". The speaker, who thinks he has killed a Muslim already, now refuses to be the cause of a second death. حَتَّى أَقْتُلَ takes the subjunctive.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَالِي كَلَامَ الشَّاهِدِ أَطْلَقَ النَّصْرَانِيَّ السِّمْسَارَ وَقَالَ لِلْمَشَاعِلِيِّ اُشْنُقْ هَذَا بِاعْتِرَافِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wālī kalāma al-shāhidi aṭlaqa al-naṣrāniyya al-simsāra wa-qāla li-al-mashāʿiliyyi ushnuq hādhā bi-iʿtirāfihi
sentences.l: So-when heard the-governor the-speech-of the-steward, he-released the-Christian the-broker, and-said to-the-torchbearer: Hang this-one by-his-confession.
sentences.i: When the governor heard the steward's words, he released the Christian broker and said to the executioner, "Hang this man on his own confession."
sentences.n: النصراني السمسار, "the Christian broker", puts the two nouns side by side as one description. بِاعْتِرَافِهِ is "by his confession": the بِـ gives the ground, the means by which he is condemned.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ الْحَبْلَ مِنْ رَقَبَةِ النَّصْرَانِيِّ وَوَضَعَهُ فِي رَقَبَةِ الشَّاهِدِ وَأَوْقَفَهُ تَحْتَ الْخَشَبَةِ وَأَرَادَأَنْ يُعَلِّقَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha al-ḥabla min raqabati al-naṣrāniyyi wa-waḍaʿahu fī raqabati al-shāhidi wa-awqafahu taḥta al-khashabati wa-arāda an yuʿalliqahu
sentences.l: So-he-took the-rope from the-neck-of the-Christian, and-put-it on the-neck-of the-steward, and-stood-him under the-timber, and-wanted-that he-hang-him.
sentences.i: So the executioner took the rope off the Christian's neck, put it around the steward's neck, stood him under the gallows, and made ready to hang him.
sentences.n: ارادان is one printed word, اراد ان; I keep it as one token.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالْيَهُودِيِّ الطَّبِيبِ قَدْ شَقَّا نَاسَ وَصَرَخَ عَلِي النَّاسِ وَعَلَى الْمَشَاعِلِيِّ وَقَالَ لَهُ لَا تَفْعَلْ مَا قَتَلَهُ إِلَّا أَنَا
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-yahūdiyyi al-ṭabībi qad shaqqā nāsa wa-ṣarakha ʿalā al-nāsi wa-ʿalā al-mashāʿiliyyi wa-qāla lahu lā tafʿal mā qatalahu illā anā
sentences.l: And-behold, with-the-Jew the-physician, he-had-cleaved people, and-cried-out at the-people and-at the-torchbearer, and-said to-him: Do-not do; none killed-him but I.
sentences.i: And behold, the Jewish physician had forced his way through the people, and he shouted at the crowd and at the executioner and said to him, "Do not do it! No one killed him but I.
sentences.n: شقا ناس is printed for شق الناس, "he cleaved the people": the alif has strayed to the verb and the article is missing. I point the two words as printed. عَلِي, "upon", is the print's spelling of عَلَى with ي; I keep the ي and point it with a sukūn (read ʿalā). صَرَخَ عَلَى is "to shout at".

sentences.t: فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ كُنْتُ فِي بَيْتِي وَإِذَا بِرَجُلٍ وَامْرَأَةٍ دَقُّوا الْبَابَ وَمَعَهُمْ هَذَا الْأَحْدَبُ ضَعِيفٌ
sentences.tr: fī hādhihi al-laylati kuntu fī baytī wa-idhā bi-rajulin wa-imraʾatin daqqū al-bāba wa-maʿahum hādhā al-aḥdabu ḍaʿīfun
sentences.l: In this the-night I-was in my-house, and-behold, with-a-man and-a-woman, they-knocked the-door, and-with-them this the-hunchback, weak.
sentences.i: On this very night I was in my house, and behold, a man and a woman knocked at the door, and with them was this hunchback, looking sick.
sentences.n: رَجُلٍ وَامْرَأَةٍ دَقُّوا uses a plural verb for two people, where Classical would say دَقَّا; the print then goes back to duals (فَأَدْخَلَاهُ, وَوَضَعَاهُ). ضَعِيفٌ, "weak", means "ailing, sick": this is how the couple presents him, a sick man being brought for treatment. The بِـ after وَإِذَا only marks what appears.

sentences.t: قَدْ دَفَعُوا لِلْجَارِيَةِ رُبْعَ دِينَارٍ فَمَا عَلَّمَتْنِي وَأَعْطَتْنِي إِيَّاهُ
sentences.tr: qad dafaʿū li-al-jāriyati rubʿa dīnārin fa-mā ʿallamatnī wa-aʿṭatnī iyyāhu
sentences.l: They-had-paid to-the-girl a-quarter-of a-dinar; so-she-did-not inform-me, and-gave-me him.
sentences.i: They had paid the maid a quarter of a dinar, and she took it, said nothing to me, and handed him over to me.
sentences.n: دَفَعُوا لِلْجَارِيَةِ is "they paid the girl": the لِـ marks the one to whom the money is handed. The sentence is obscure: I read فَمَا عَلَّمَتْنِي as "she did not tell me" (perhaps for Classical أَعْلَمَتْنِي), that is, the maid took the coin and let the couple's man pass without a word. Another reading is possible, so take my version as the likeliest only. إِيَّاهُ is the emphatic object "him".

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الرَّجُلُ وَالْمَرْأَةُ فَأَدْخَلَاهُ فِي الْبَيْتِ وَوَضَعَاهُ عَلَيْ السُّلَّمِ وَذَهَبَا
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-rajulu wa-al-marʾatu fa-adkhalāhu fī al-bayti wa-waḍaʿāhu ʿalā al-sullami wa-dhahabā
sentences.l: And-as-for the-man and-the-woman, so-they-two-brought-him-in into the-house, and-placed-him on the-stairs, and-they-two-went.
sentences.i: As for the man and the woman, the two of them brought him into the house, set him on the stairs, and left.
sentences.n: عَلَيْ is the print's عَلَي with ي, for عَلَى; I keep the ي. السُّلَّم is the stairs, here the stairway inside the house.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلْتُ لِأَ نْظُرَهُ وَأَنَا فِي الظَّلَامِ فَعَثَرْتُ فِيهِ فَوَقَعَ مِنْ فَوْقِ السُّلَّمِ لِأَ سْفَلَ فَمَاتَ مِنْ وَقْتِهِ فَحَمَلْنَاهُ أَنَا وَزَوْجَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-nazaltu li-a nẓurahu wa-anā fī al-ẓalāmi fa-ʿathartu fīhi fa-waqaʿa min fawqi al-sullami li-a sfala fa-māta min waqtihi fa-ḥamalnāhu anā wa-zawjatī
sentences.l: So-I-went-down, to-that-I-look-at-him, and-I in the-darkness, and-stumbled on-him; so-he-fell from above-of the-stairs to-below, and-died from his-time; and-we-carried-him, I and-my-wife.
sentences.i: So I went down to look at him, in the dark, and I stumbled over him, and he fell from the top of the stairs to the bottom and died on the spot. Then my wife and I carried him.
sentences.n: لا نظره and لا سفل are printed as two words each, for لأنظره ("in order that I look at him") and لأسفل ("to below"); the hamza belongs to the first half, and I point each half as printed. فَعَثَرْتُ فِيهِ is "I stumbled on him". مِنْ وَقْتِهِ, "from his time", is "at that very moment". أَنَا وَزَوْجَتِي after فَحَمَلْنَاهُ is the plain way to say "I and my wife".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ طَلَعْنَا بِهِ إِلَى السَّطْحِ وَدَارُ الشَّاهِدِ هَذَا بِجِوَارِ دَارِي
sentences.tr: thumma ṭalaʿnā bihi ilā al-saṭḥi wa-dāru al-shāhidi hādhā bi-jiwāri dārī
sentences.l: Then we-went-up with-him to the-roof, and-the-house-of the-steward this (is) beside my-house.
sentences.i: Then we took him up to the roof. The house of this steward is next to mine.
sentences.n: بِجِوَارِ is "beside, next to". طَلَعَ بِـ is "to go up with", that is, "to take up". The wa- before دَارُ is the circumstantial wa-, "seeing that the house ... was".

sentences.t: فَأَرْخَيْنَا هَذَا الْأَحْدَبَ فِي الْبَادْ هَنْجِ بِتَاعِ الشَّاهِدِ وَهُوَ مَيِّتٌ
sentences.tr: fa-arkhaynā hādhā al-aḥdaba fī al-bād hanji bitāʿi al-shāhidi wa-huwa mayyitun
sentences.l: So-we-let-down this the-hunchback into the-bādhanj of-the-steward, and-he (was) dead.
sentences.i: So we lowered this hunchback down the ventilator of the steward, dead as he was.
sentences.n: بِتَاع, "of, belonging to", is the Egyptian colloquial word for possession, here "the steward's ventilator". The print spells it بتاع; I point it bitāʿ. الباد هنج: see the note above, the roof wind-catcher or shaft, printed as two words. أَرْخَى is "to let down, to lower on a rope".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا طَلَعَ هَذَا الشَّاهِدُ وَجَدَهُ فِي بَيْتِهِ فَاعْتَقَدَ أَنَّهُ حَرَامِي فَضَرَبَهُ بِمِطْرَقَةٍ فَوَقَعَ عَلَيْ الْأَرْضِ فَاعْتَقَدَ أَنَّهُ قَتَلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṭalaʿa hādhā al-shāhidu wajadahu fī baytihi fa-iʿtaqada annahu ḥarāmī fa-ḍarabahu bi-miṭraqatin fa-waqaʿa ʿalā al-arḍi fa-iʿtaqada annahu qatalahu
sentences.l: So-when went-up this the-steward, he-found-him in his-house, and-believed that-he (was) a-thief; so-he-struck-him with-a-hammer, and-he-fell upon the-ground, and-believed that-he killed-him.
sentences.i: When this steward went up, he found him in his own house and took him for a thief. He struck him with a hammer, and he fell to the ground, and the steward believed he had killed him.
sentences.n: حَرَامِي is the colloquial "thief" (Classical حَرَامِيّ or لِصّ), with the single ي and no nisba shadda. عَلَيْ is the print's عَلَي with ي; I keep the ي. The Jew has no way of knowing this unless the witness told him, but the story lets him narrate it.

sentences.t: فَمَا كَفَانِي قَتَلْتُ مُسْلِمًا بِغَيْرِ عِلْمِي وَآخُذُ فِي ذِمَّتِي مُسْلِمًا آخَرَ بِعِلْمِي
sentences.tr: fa-mā kafānī qataltu muslimān bi-ghayri ʿilmī wa-ākhudhu fī dhimmatī muslimān ākhara bi-ʿilmī
sentences.l: So-did-not suffice-me: I-killed a-Muslim with-other-than my-knowledge, and-I-take on my-account another Muslim with my-knowledge?
sentences.i: Was it not enough that I killed a Muslim without knowing it, that I should take another Muslim on my conscience knowingly?
sentences.n: فَمَا كَفَانِي قَتَلْتُ puts the verb directly after the question, with no أَنْ or أَنِّي: "did it not suffice me, I killed ...". The sense is a rhetorical question. ذِمَّتِي, "my account, my charge", is the sphere of a person's responsibility: to "take it into one's dhimma" is to saddle oneself with the guilt. بِغَيْرِ عِلْمِي is "without my knowing"; بِعِلْمِي is "with my knowledge".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَالِي كَلَامَ الْيَهُودِيِّ قَالَ لِلْمَشَاعِلِيِّ أَطْلِقِ الشَّاهِدَ وَاشْنُقِ الْيَهُودِيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wālī kalāma al-yahūdiyyi qāla li-al-mashāʿiliyyi aṭliqi al-shāhida wa-ushnuqi al-yahūdiyya
sentences.l: So-when heard the-governor the-speech-of the-Jew, he-said to-the-torchbearer: Release the-steward and-hang the-Jew.
sentences.i: When the governor heard the Jew's words, he said to the executioner, "Release the steward and hang the Jew."

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَهُ الْمَشَاعِلِيُّ وَحَطَّ الْحَبْلَ فِي رَقَبَتِهِ وَإِذَا بِالْخَيَّاطِ شَقَّ النَّاسَ وَقَالَ لِلْمَشَاعِلِيِّ لَاتَفْعَلْ مَا قَتَلَهُ إِلَّا أَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhahu al-mashāʿiliyyu wa-ḥaṭṭa al-ḥabla fī raqabatihi wa-idhā bi-al-khayyāṭi shaqqa al-nāsa wa-qāla li-al-mashāʿiliyyi lā-tafʿal mā qatalahu illā anā
sentences.l: So-took-him the-torchbearer, and-put the-rope on his-neck; and-behold, with-the-tailor, he-cleaved the-people, and-said to-the-torchbearer: Do-not-do; none killed-him but I.
sentences.i: The executioner took him and put the rope around his neck. And behold, the tailor pushed through the people and said to the executioner, "Do not do it! No one killed him but I.
sentences.n: حَطَّ is the colloquial "to put, to set". لاتفعل is one printed word, لا تفعل, "do not do"; I keep it as one token. The بِـ after وَإِذَا only marks what appears.

sentences.t: وَذَلِكَ أَنِّي كُنْتُ بِالنَّهَارِ أَتَفَرَّجُ وَجِئْتُ الْعِشَاءَ فَلَقِيتُ هَذَا الْأَحْدَبَ سَكْرَانًا
sentences.tr: wa-dhālika annī kuntu bi-al-nahāri atafarraju wa-jiʾtu al-ʿishāʾa fa-laqītu hādhā al-aḥdaba sakrānan
sentences.l: And-that (is) that-I was by-the-day I-amuse-myself, and-I-came (at) the-evening, and-met this the-hunchback, drunk.
sentences.i: Here is how it was: I had spent the day out amusing myself, and I came home in the evening and met this hunchback, drunk.
sentences.n: بِالنَّهَارِ is "by day": the بِـ gives the time in which the action took place. أَتَفَرَّجُ, "I amuse myself, I take in the sights", is colloquial; the verb follows كُنْتُ with no connecting word. سَكْرَانًا is printed with the alif of the accusative tanwīn, as if the word took full case endings; Classical سَكْرَانَ is diptote. I point it as printed.

sentences.t: وَمَعَهُ دَفٌّ وَهُوَيُغَنِّي بِعَزْمِهِ عَلَيْهِ فَعَزَمْتُ عَلَيْهِ وَجِبْتُهُ إِلَى بَيْتِي
sentences.tr: wa-maʿahu daffun wa-huwayughannī bi-ʿazmihi ʿalayhi fa-ʿazamtu ʿalayhi wa-jibtuhu ilā baytī
sentences.l: And-with-him a-tambourine, and-he-sings with-his-inviting upon-him; so-I-invited upon-him, and-brought-him to my-house.
sentences.i: He had a tambourine with him and was singing, hinting for an invitation, so I invited him and brought him to my house.
sentences.n: هويغني is one printed word, هو يغني, "he sings"; I keep it as one token. بعزمه عليه is obscure: عَزَمَ عَلَى is "to invite" (to a meal), and the next clause has the tailor doing exactly that, so I read the phrase as the drunk fishing for an invitation as he sings. The printed form might be a garble, so treat my wording as a likely guess. وَجِبْتُهُ is the colloquial جِبْتُهُ, "I brought him", for جِئْتُ بِهِ.

sentences.t: وَاشْتَرَيْتُ سَمَكًا وَقَعَدْنَا نَأْكُلُ
sentences.tr: wa-ishtaraytu samakan wa-qaʿadnā naʾkulu
sentences.l: And-I-bought fish, and-we-sat we-eat.
sentences.i: I bought fish, and we sat down to eat.
sentences.n: نَأْكُلُ follows قَعَدْنَا with no connecting word, "we sat, we eat", the usual colloquial way. The print writes ناكل with a bare alif: I add the hamza.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْ زَوْجَتِي قِطْعَةَ سَمَكٍ وَلُقْمَةً وَدَسَّتْهَا فِي حَنَكِهِ فَازْوَرَّ بَعْضُهُ فِي حَنَكِهِ فَمَاتَ لِوَقْتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhat zawjatī qiṭʿata samakin wa-luqmatan wa-dassathā fī ḥanakihi fa-azwarra baʿḍuhu fī ḥanakihi fa-māta li-waqtihi
sentences.l: So-took my-wife a-piece-of fish and-a-morsel, and-shoved-it into his-palate; so-turned-aside part-of-it in his-palate, and-he-died at-his-time.
sentences.i: My wife took a piece of fish and a morsel, and she crammed it into his mouth, and part of it lodged crosswise in his throat, and he died at once.
sentences.n: دَسَّ is "to shove, to thrust". The حَنَك is the palate or jaw, here the inside of the mouth and throat. فَازْوَرَّ بَعْضُهُ is obscure: ازْوَرَّ means "to turn aside", and I take بعضه to be a part of the fish, lodging crosswise; it could also mean that part of his body recoiled. The "morsel" is from لُقْمَة, a mouthful, a lump of food; the print does not say of what. لِوَقْتِهِ, "at his time", is "at once", like مِنْ وَقْتِهِ above.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْنَاهُ أَنَا وَزَوْجَتِي وَجِئْنَا بِهِ لِبَيْتِ الْيَهُودِيِّ فَنَزَلَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَفَتَحَتْ لَنَا الْبَابَ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhnāhu anā wa-zawjatī wa-jiʾnā bihi li-bayti al-yahūdiyyi fa-nazalati al-jāriyatu wa-fataḥat lanā al-bāba
sentences.l: So-we-took-him, I and-my-wife, and-came with-him to-the-house-of the-Jew; so-came-down the-girl and-opened to-us the-door.
sentences.i: So my wife and I took him and brought him to the Jew's house, and the maid came down and opened the door for us.
sentences.n: لِبَيْتِ is "to the house of": the لِـ here takes the place of إِلَى, marking where they were going. فَتَحَ لَنَا الْبَابَ is "opened the door for us".

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا قُولِي لِسَيِّدِكِ إِنَّ بِالْبَابِ امْرَأَةٌ وَرَجُلٌ وَمَعَهُمَا ضَعِيفٌ تَعَالَ اُنْظُرْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā qūlī li-sayyidiki inna bi-al-bābi imraʾatun wa-rajulun wa-maʿahumā ḍaʿīfun taʿāla unẓurhu
sentences.l: So-I-said to-her: Say to-your-master that at-the-door (are) a-woman and-a-man, and-with-them-two a-sick-one: Come, look-at-him.
sentences.i: I said to her, "Tell your master that a woman and a man are at the door, with a sick person: come and look at him."
sentences.n: لِسَيِّدِكِ, "to your master", is addressed to the girl, so the pronoun is feminine. إِنَّ بِالْبَابِ امْرَأَةٌ وَرَجُلٌ: the "at the door" is put first and the woman and the man follow; Classical grammar would put them in the accusative after إِنَّ, but the print has no ending-letters there and I point them plainly. ضَعِيفٌ, "weak", is "sick". تَعَالَ اُنْظُرْهُ is "come, look at him", two imperatives side by side; نَظَرَ takes a direct object here, "look at him", without إِلَى.

sentences.t: وَأَعْطَيْتُ لَهَا رُبْعَ دِينَارٍ فَطَلَعَتْ لِسَيِّدِهَا وَحَمَلْتُ أَنَا الْأَحْدَبَ لِرَأْسِ السُّلَّمِ وَأَسْنَدْتُهُ وَمَضَيْتُ أَنَا وَزَوْجَتِي
sentences.tr: wa-aʿṭaytu lahā rubʿa dīnārin fa-ṭalaʿat li-sayyidihā wa-ḥamaltu anā al-aḥdaba li-raʾsi al-sullami wa-asnadtuhu wa-maḍaytu anā wa-zawjatī
sentences.l: And-I-gave to-her a-quarter-of a-dinar; so-she-went-up to-her-master, and-I-carried, I, the-hunchback to-the-head-of the-stairs, and-propped-him, and-went, I and-my-wife.
sentences.i: I gave her a quarter of a dinar, and she went up to her master. Then I carried the hunchback to the head of the stairs, propped him there, and my wife and I went away.
sentences.n: لِرَأْسِ السُّلَّمِ is "to the head of the stairs", the top step: the لِـ marks the direction, as لِبَيْتِ does above. أَسْنَدَ is "to prop, to lean (against)".

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَ الْيَهُودِيُّ فَعَثَرَ فِيهِ فَظَنَّ أَنَّهُ قَتَلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-nazala al-yahūdiyyu fa-ʿathara fīhi fa-ẓanna annahu qatalahu
sentences.l: So-came-down the-Jew, and-stumbled on-him, and-thought that-he killed-him.
sentences.i: Then the Jew came down, stumbled over him, and thought he had killed him.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ الْخَيَّاطُ لِلْيَهُودِيِّ صَحِيحٌ قُلْ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla al-khayyāṭu li-al-yahūdiyyi ṣaḥīḥun qul naʿam
sentences.l: Then said the-tailor to-the-Jew: True? Say: yes.
sentences.i: Then the tailor said to the Jew, "Is that true? Say yes."
sentences.n: قُلْ is the imperative "say", not the slip for قَالَ.

sentences.t: وَالْتَفَتَ الْخَيَّاطُ لِلْوَالِي وَقَالَ لَهُ أَطْلِقِ الْيَهُودِيَّ وَاشْنُقْنِي
sentences.tr: wa-iltafata al-khayyāṭu li-al-wālī wa-qāla lahu aṭliqi al-yahūdiyya wa-ushnuqnī
sentences.l: And-turned the-tailor to-the-governor, and-said to-him: Release the-Jew and-hang-me.
sentences.i: The tailor turned to the governor and said, "Release the Jew and hang me."

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَالِي كَلَامَهُ تَعَجَّبَ مِنْ أَمْرِ هَذَا الْأَحْدَبِ وَقَالَ إِنَّ هَذَا أَمْرٌ يُؤَرَّخُ فِى الْكُتُبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wālī kalāmahu taʿajjaba min amri hādhā al-aḥdabi wa-qāla inna hādhā amrun yuʾarrakhu fī al-kutubi
sentences.l: So-when heard the-governor his-speech, he-marvelled at the-affair-of this the-hunchback, and-said: Indeed this (is) an-affair (that) is-dated in the-books.
sentences.i: When the governor heard his words, he marvelled at the matter of this hunchback and said, "This is an affair to be written down in the books."
sentences.n: فى is the print's spelling of في, with ى; I keep it. يُؤَرَّخُ is the passive of أَرَّخَ, "to date, to record": a matter fit for the chronicles. تَعَجَّبَ مِنْ is "to marvel at", the verb choosing the preposition.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لِلْمَشَاعِلِيِّ أَطْلِقِ الْيَهُودِيَّ وَاشْنُقِ الْخَيَّاطَ بِاعْتِرَافِهِ فَقَدَّمَهُ الْمَشَاعِلِيُّ وَقَالَ تَعِبْنَا نُقَدِّمُ هَذَا وَنُؤَخِّرُ هَذَا وَلَايُشْنَقُ وَاحِدٌ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla li-al-mashāʿiliyyi aṭliqi al-yahūdiyya wa-ushnuqi al-khayyāṭa bi-iʿtirāfihi fa-qaddamahu al-mashāʿiliyyu wa-qāla taʿibnā nuqaddimu hādhā wa-nuʾakhkhiru hādhā wa-lā-yushnaqu wāḥidun
sentences.l: Then he-said to-the-torchbearer: Release the-Jew and-hang the-tailor by-his-confession. So-brought-forward-him the-torchbearer and-said: We-are-tired, we-bring-forward this-one and-we-put-back this-one, and-not-is-hanged one.
sentences.i: Then he said to the executioner, "Release the Jew and hang the tailor on his own confession." The executioner brought him forward and said, "We are worn out, bringing this one forward and putting that one back, and not one of them is hanged."
sentences.n: ولايشنق is one printed word, ولا يشنق, "and one is not hanged"; I keep it as one token. نُقَدِّمُ هَذَا وَنُؤَخِّرُ هَذَا, "we put this one forward and that one back", is the executioner's weary summary of the shuffle. بِاعْتِرَافِهِ is "on his confession", as above.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ وَضَعَ الْحَبْلَ فِي رَقَبَةِ الْخَيَّاطِ
sentences.tr: thumma waḍaʿa al-ḥabla fī raqabati al-khayyāṭi
sentences.l: Then he-put the-rope on the-neck-of the-tailor.
sentences.i: Then he put the rope around the tailor's neck.

sentences.t: فَهَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ هَؤُلَاءِ وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْأَ حْدَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā mā kāna min amri hāʾulāʾi wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-a ḥdabi
sentences.l: So-this (is) what was of the-affair-of these; and-as-for what was of the-affair-of the-hunch back:
sentences.i: So much for what happened to these men. As for what happened to the hunchback:
sentences.n: This is the storyteller's formula for changing scenes: "this is what befell these; and as for what befell so-and-so". الا حدب is the print's split of الأحدب: الْأَ and حْدَبِ are the two halves of one word, and I point each as printed.

sentences.t: فَقِيلَ إِنَّهُ كَانَ مَسْخَرَةً لِلسُّلْطَانِ وَكَانَ لَا يَقْدِرُ يُفَارِقَةْ
sentences.tr: fa-qīla innahu kāna maskharatan li-al-sulṭāni wa-kāna lā yaqdiru yufāriqahu
sentences.l: So-it-was-said that-he was a-buffoon for-the-sultan, and-he-was not able (to) part-with-him.
sentences.i: It is told that he was the sultan's jester, and the sultan could not bear to be parted from him.
sentences.n: مَسْخَرَة is a buffoon, a jester; the لِـ in لِلسُّلْطَانِ says whose jester he was. The last word is printed with ة where the pronoun ه is meant (يفارقه, "part with him"): a compositor's slip. I keep the ة, pointed with a sukūn, and read it yufāriqahu. لَا يَقْدِرُ يُفَارِقُ has no أَنْ before the second verb, as is usual in Middle Arabic. The subject of the verb is the Sultan, who cannot do without his jester.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَكِرَ الْأَ حْدَبُ وَغَابَ عَنْهُ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ وَثَانِي يَوْمٍ إِلَى نِصْفِ النَّهَارِ سَأَلَ عَنْهُ بَعْضَ الْحَاضِرِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā sakira al-a ḥdabu wa-ghāba ʿanhu tilka al-layla wa-thānī yawmin ilā niṣfi al-nahāri saʾala ʿanhu baʿḍa al-ḥāḍirīna
sentences.l: So-when became-drunk the-hunch back, and-was-absent from-him that the-night and-(the)-second day until (the)-half-of the-daytime, he-asked about-him some-of the-present-ones.
sentences.i: Now when the hunchback got drunk and was away from him that night, and the next day until noon, the sultan asked some of those present about him.
sentences.n: الا حدب is split in print here too: الْأَ and حْدَبُ. The sentence has no stated subject for سَأَلَ; it is the Sultan. بَعْضَ is the object, "some of those present". ثَانِي يَوْمٍ is "the second day", that is, "the next day". نِصْفُ النَّهَارِ, "half of the daytime", is noon.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَهُ يَا مَوْلَانَا طَلَعَ بِهِ الْوَالِي وَهُوَ مَيِّتٌ وَأَمَرَ بِشَنْقِ قَاتِلِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lahu yā mawlānā ṭalaʿa bihi al-wālī wa-huwa mayyitun wa-amara bi-shanqi qātilihi
sentences.l: So-they-said to-him: O our-master, went-up with-him the-governor, and-he (was) dead, and-commanded with-the-hanging-of his-killer.
sentences.i: They said to him, "My lord, the governor took him up, dead, and ordered his killer hanged."
sentences.n: يَا مَوْلَانَا, "O our master", is the courtier's address to the Sultan. طَلَعَ بِهِ is "went up with him", that is, took him up; the print does not say to where. أَمَرَ بِشَنْقِ, "he ordered the hanging of", has the preposition chosen by the verb.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَ الْوَالِي يَشْنُقُ الْقَاتِلَ فَحَضَرَ ثَانِي وَثَالِثٌ وَكُلُّ وَاحِدٍ يَقُولُ مَا قَتَلَهُ إِلَّا أَنَا وَكُلُّ وَاحِدٍ يَذْكُرُ الْمَوَالِي سَبَبَ قَتْلِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-nazala al-wālī yashnuqu al-qātila fa-ḥaḍara thānī wa-thālithun wa-kullu wāḥidin yaqūlu mā qatalahu illā anā wa-kullu wāḥidin yadhkuru al-mawālī sababa qatlihi
sentences.l: So-came-down the-governor (he-)hangs the-killer; so-attended a-second and-a-third, and-every one says: None killed-him but I, and-every one mentions the-clients the-cause-of his-killing.
sentences.i: The governor came down to hang the killer, and a second and a third came forward, and each one said, "No one killed him but I," and each one told the governor the reason he had killed him.
sentences.n: ثَانِي is printed for ثَانٍ, "a second", without the tanwīn the Classical form would take. الموالي is printed for الوالي (or لِلْوَالِي), "to the governor": الْمَوَالِي is the plural of مَوْلًى, "masters, clients", and does not fit; I point it as printed and read the governor. يَذْكُرُ الْمَوَالِي سَبَبَ has no لِـ before the person addressed. كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ is "each one".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ صَرَخَ عَلَى الْحَاجِبِ وَقَالَ انْزِلْ إِلَى الْوَالِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku hādhā al-kalāma ṣarakha ʿalā al-ḥājibi wa-qāla inzil ilā al-wālī
sentences.l: So-when heard the-king this the-speech, he-cried-out upon the-chamberlain and-said: Go-down to the-governor,
sentences.i: When the king heard this tale, he shouted to the chamberlain and said: Go down to the governor
sentences.n: صرخ عَلَى, "cried out upon", is the usual way to say "shouted at/to" someone. The الحاجب (al-ḥājib) is the chamberlain, the officer who admits people to the king. الوالي is the governor of the city, who also commands the police.

sentences.t: وَاِئْتِنِي بِهِمْ جَمِيعًا فَنَزَلَ الْحَاجِبُ فَوَجَدَ الْمَشَاعِلِيَّ رَائِحٌ يَشْنُقُ الْخَيَّاطَ
sentences.tr: wa-i'tinī bihim jamīʿan fa-nazala al-ḥājibu fa-wajada al-mashāʿiliyya rāʾiḥun yashnuqu al-khayyāṭa
sentences.l: and-bring-me with-them all. So-went-down the-chamberlain and-found the-torchbearer going-off (to) hang the-tailor.
sentences.i: and bring them all to me. So the chamberlain went down and found the executioner on the point of hanging the tailor.
sentences.n: The print spells the imperative وائتني, with an alif followed by a hamza on a yā-seat (ئ); I point it wa-iʾtinī, "and bring me" (أتى بِـ, "to bring"). المشاعلي is the executioner, literally the torch-bearer (mashʿalī), a police word of the period. رائح is a bare participle where Classical would put the circumstantial accusative رَائِحًا; I point what is printed, and read it as "going off (to hang)", that is, "about to hang". This undeclined participle of circumstance recurs in the night.

sentences.t: فَصَرَخَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَاجِبُ وَقَالَ لَاتَفْعَلْ وَأَعْلِمِ الْوَالِيَ بِقِصَّةِ الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣarakha ʿalayhi al-ḥājibu wa-qāla lā-tafʿal wa-aʿlimi al-wāliya bi-qiṣṣati al-maliki
sentences.l: So-cried-out upon-him the-chamberlain and-said: Do-not-do (it)! and-inform the-governor with-the-story-of the-king.
sentences.i: The chamberlain shouted at him and said: Do not do it! And tell the governor the king's story.
sentences.n: لاتفعل is printed as one word, "do not do (it)"; I keep it as one token. واعلم is read as the command wa-aʾlimi, "and inform" (Form IV أعلم), with بِـ introducing the matter told: "inform him of the king's story".

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَهُ وَأَخَذَ الْأَ حْدَبَ مَعَهُ مَحْمُولًا وَالْخَيَّاطَ وَالْيَهُودِيَّ وَالنَّصْرَانِيَّ وَالشَّاهِدَ وَطَلَعُوا بِالْجَمِيعِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhahu wa-akhadha al-a ḥdaba maʿahu maḥmūlan wa-al-khayyāṭa wa-al-yahūdiyya wa-al-naṣrāniyya wa-al-shāhida wa-ṭalaʿū bi-al-jamīʿi
