sentences.l: So-he-took him, and-took the-hunchback with-him carried, and-the-tailor and-the-Jew and-the-Christian and-the-steward, and-they-went-up with-the-all.
sentences.i: So he took him, and took the hunchback along with him, carried, together with the tailor, the Jew, the Christian and the steward, and they went up with the whole company.
sentences.n: The print splits the hunchback's name as الا حدب, "al-" plus "aḥdab", with a space; the same word is printed whole (الاحدب) elsewhere in this night. I keep the printed space and point the two halves as one word. محمولا is the circumstantial accusative: the hunchback is carried along. The subject of the first two verbs is the chamberlain. طلعوا بِـ, "went up with", means "took up" (the party went up to the king, bringing everyone). الشاهد is "the witness".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَمَثَّلَ الْوَالِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ قَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ وَحَكَى لَهُ عَلَى مَا جَرَى مِنَ الْجَمِيعِ وَلَيْسَ فِى الْإِعَادَةِ إِفَادَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā tamaththala al-wālī bayna yadayhi qabbala al-arḍa wa-ḥakā lahu ʿalā mā jarā min al-jamīʿi wa-laysa fī al-iʿādati ifādatun
sentences.l: So-when presented-himself the-governor between his-hands, he-kissed the-earth, and-related to-him upon what happened from the-all, and-there-is-not in the-repetition benefit.
sentences.i: When the governor stood before him, he kissed the ground and told him everything that had passed with them all; and there is no profit in repeating it.
sentences.n: بين يديه, "between his hands", is "in his presence". حكى لَهُ عَلَى ما جرى is colloquial in its use of عَلَى after حكى: Classical would say حكى له ما جرى. The clause وليس في الاعادة افادة, "there is no benefit in the repetition", is the narrator's aside: the reader already knows the story. فى is printed with dotless ى.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ الْحِكَايَةَ تَعَجَّبَ وَأَخَذَهُ الطَّرَبُ وَأَمَرَأَنْ يُؤَرَّخَ ذَلِكَ بِمَاءِ الذَّهَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku al-ḥikāyata taʿajjaba wa-akhadhahu al-ṭarabu wa-amarān yuʾarrakha dhālika bi-māʾi al-dhahabi
sentences.l: So-when heard the-king the-story, he-marvelled, and-took-him the-delight, and-he-ordered-that be-dated that with-water-of the-gold.
sentences.i: When the king heard the story he marvelled, delight took hold of him, and he commanded that it be written down in gold ink.
sentences.n: وامران is printed as one word, wa-amara + an, "and he ordered that"; I keep it as one token. يؤرخ is read as a passive, yuʾarrakha, "be recorded" (literally "be dated", from تاريخ). بماء الذهب, "with gold-water", means with gold ink, a sign of high honour.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِلْحَاضِرِينَ هَلْ سَمِعْتُمْ بِأَعْجَبَ مِنْ قِصَّةِ هَذَا الْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-al-ḥāḍirīna hal samiʿtum bi-aʿjaba min qiṣṣati hādhā al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: And-he-said to-the-present-ones: Have-you-heard of-more-wonderful than the-story-of this the-hunchback?
sentences.i: and said to those present: Have you ever heard of anything more wonderful than the story of this hunchback?
sentences.n: سمع بِـ means "hear of" (not "hear"), and بِأَعْجَبَ is the elative "more wonderful", with an unspoken "thing".

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ تَقَدَّمَ النَّصْرَانِيُّ وَقَالَ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ إِنْ أَذِنْتَ لِي حَدَّثْتُكَ بِشَيْءٍ جَرَى لِي وَهُوَا عَجَبٌ وَأَغْرَبُ وَأَطْرَبُ مِنْ قِصَّةِ الْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika taqaddama al-naṣrāniyyu wa-qāla yā malika al-zamāni in adhinta lī ḥaddathtuka bi-shayʾin jarā lī wa-huwā ʿajabun wa-aghrabu wa-aṭrabu min qiṣṣati al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: So-at that came-forward the-Christian and-said: O king-of the-age, if you-permitted to-me, I-would-tell-you with-a-thing (that) happened to-me, and-it a-wonder, and-stranger, and-more-delightful than the-story-of the-hunchback.
sentences.i: At that the Christian stepped forward and said: O king of the age, if you permit me, I will tell you of something that happened to me, which is a marvel, and stranger and more delightful than the story of the hunchback.
sentences.n: هوا is printed with a final alif (huwā for huwa), a Middle Arabic spelling; the pointing follows it. عجب is read as the noun ʿajab, "a wonder", and is followed by two elatives, اغرب and اطرب, which together take مِنْ "than"; the sentence is loose but clear. ان اذنت is a conditional whose answer, حدثتك, is a perfect with the force of a future ("I will tell you").

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ حَدِّثْنَا بِمَا عِنْدَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku ḥaddithnā bi-mā ʿindaka
sentences.l: So-said the-king: Tell-us with-what (is) with-you.
sentences.i: The king said: Tell us what you have.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ إِنِّي لَمَّا دَخَلْتُ تِلْكَ الدِّيَارَ أَتَيْتُ بِمَتْجَرٍ وَأَوْقَعَنِي الْمَقْدُورُ عِنْدَكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā malika al-zamāni innī lammā dakhaltu tilka al-diyāra ataytu bi-matjarin wa-awqaʿanī al-maqdūru ʿindakum
sentences.l: So-he-said: O king-of the-age, indeed-I, when I-entered those the-lands, I-came with-a-merchandise, and-made-me-fall the-decreed (fate) with-you.
sentences.i: He said: O king of the age, when I entered these lands I came with merchandise, and fate cast me down among you.
sentences.n: أتى بِـ is "come with", that is "bring"; مَتْجَر is trade-goods, a stock to sell. المقدور is "the decreed", that is, destiny. عندكم, "with you", means "in your country".

sentences.t: وَأَصْلُ مَوْلِدِي بِمِصْرَ وَأَنَا مِنْ قِبْطِهَا وَتَرَبَّيْتُ بِهَا وَكَانَ وَالِدِي سِمْسَارًا
sentences.tr: wa-aṣlu mawlidī bi-miṣra wa-anā min qibṭihā wa-tarabbaytu bihā wa-kāna wālidī simsāran
sentences.l: And-origin-of my-birth in-Egypt, and-I (am) of its-Copts, and-I-was-raised in-it, and-was my-father a-broker.
sentences.i: My birth was originally in Egypt; I am one of its Copts, and I was raised there, and my father was a broker.
sentences.n: وأصل مولدي, "the origin of my birth", is a nominal clause with no verb: "my birthplace is Egypt". القبط (al-qibṭ) are the Copts, Egypt's native Christians. السمسار is a broker, one who arranges sales for a commission.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا بَلَغْتُ مَبْلَغَ الرِّجَالِ تُوُفِّيَ وَالِدِي فَعَمِلْتُ سِمْسَارًا مَكَانَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā balaghtu mablagha al-rijāli tuwuffiya wālidī fa-ʿamiltu simsāran makānahu
sentences.l: So-when I-reached the-reaching-of the-men, was-taken-in-death my-father, and-I-worked (as) a-broker in-his-place.
sentences.i: When I came of age, my father died, and I worked as a broker in his place.
sentences.n: توفي is passive in form, tuwuffiya, "was taken (by God)", the ordinary Arabic for "died". بلغ مبلغ الرجال, "reached the reaching of men", means "reached manhood".

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا أَنَا فِي يَوْمٍ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ قَاعِدٌ وَإِذَا بِشَابٍّ أَحْسَنَ مَا يَكُونُ وَعَلَيْهِ أَفْخَرُ مَلْبُوسٍ وَهُوَ رَاكِبٌ حِمَارًا
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā anā fī yawmin mina al-ayyāmi qāʿidun wa-idhā bi-shābbin aḥsana mā yakūnu wa-ʿalayhi afkharu malbūsin wa-huwa rākibun ḥimāran
sentences.l: So-while I, on a-day of the-days, sitting, and-behold, with-a-youth, most-handsome (that) which he-could-be, and-upon-him finest-of clothing, and-he riding a-donkey.
sentences.i: One day, as I was sitting, behold, there was a youth, as handsome as a man can be, wearing the finest clothes, and riding a donkey.
sentences.n: في يوم من الايام, "on a day of the days", is the storyteller's "one day". وإذا بِـ, "and behold, with", is the surprise-idiom: the بِـ only marks what appears (here a youth). قاعد and راكب are bare participles of circumstance, as before. أحسن ما يكون, "most handsome of what there could be", means "as handsome as could be".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآنِي سَلَّمَ عَلَيَّ فَقُمْتُ تَعْظِيمًا لَهُ فَأَخْرَجَ مِنْدِيلًا وَفِيهِ قَدْرُ سِمْسِمٍ وَقَالَ كَمْ يُسَاوِي الْأَرْدَبُّ مِنْ هَذَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾānī sallama ʿalayya fa-qumtu taʿẓīman lahu fa-akhraja mindīlan wa-fīhi qadru simsimin wa-qāla kam yusāwī al-ardabbu min hādhā
sentences.l: So-when he-saw-me, he-greeted upon-me, and-I-stood (in) honouring for-him, and-he-took-out a-kerchief, and-in-it a-measure-of sesame, and-said: How-much equals the-ardabb of this?
sentences.i: When he saw me he greeted me, and I stood up in his honour. He took out a kerchief with a little sesame in it and said: What is an ardabb of this worth?
sentences.n: سلّم عَلَيَّ is "greeted me" (literally "gave peace upon me"). الاردب (ardabb) is the great Egyptian dry measure for grain, about two hundred litres. سمسم is sesame, a major trade crop in Egypt. The sesame in the kerchief is the sample.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ مِائَةُ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu miʾatu dirhamin
sentences.l: So-I-said to-him: A-hundred dirham(s).
sentences.i: I said to him: A hundred dirhams.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي خُذِ التَّرَّاسِينَ وَالْكَيَّالِينَ وَاعْمِدَا لِي بَابَ النَّصْرِ إِلَى خَانِ الْجَوَالِي تَجِدْنِي فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī khudhi al-tarrāsīna wa-al-kayyālīna wa-iʿmidā lī bāba al-naṣri ilā khāni al-jawālī tajidnī fīhi
sentences.l: So-he-said to-me: Take the-porters and-the-measurers, and-make-for (you-two), for-me, the-Gate-of the-Victory, to the-inn-of al-Jawālī; you-will-find-me in-it.
sentences.i: He said to me: Take the porters and the measurers, and head for the Gate of Victory, to the Khān al-Jawālī; you will find me there.
sentences.n: التراسين is the colloquial "porters" (tarrās) and الكيالين "the measurers" (those who measure grain by the ardabb). واعمدا is a dual imperative ("make for, you two"); it may be addressed to the porters and measurers as the two groups, or may be a scribal slip for the singular; I point what is printed. باب النصر is the Bāb al-Naṣr of Cairo; خان الجوالي is the inn (khān) where merchants stored and traded goods. تجدني is a command-and-result pair: "[do this], you will find me".

sentences.t: وَتَرَكَنِي وَمَضَى وَأَعْطَانِي السِّمْسِمَ بِمِنْدِيلِهِ الَّذِي فِيهِ الْعَيِّنَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-tarakanī wa-maḍā wa-aʿṭānī al-simsima bi-mindīlihi alladhī fīhi al-ʿayyinata
sentences.l: And-he-left-me and-went-off, and-gave-me the-sesame with-his-kerchief which in-it (is) the-sample.
sentences.i: Then he left me and went off, having given me the sesame together with the kerchief that held the sample.
sentences.n: بمنديله, "with his kerchief", has the بِـ of accompaniment: the kerchief went along with the sesame. العينة (al-ʿayyina) is a sample of goods.

sentences.t: فَدُرْتُ عَلَى الْمُشْتَرِينَ فَجَابَ كُلُّ أَرْدَبٍّ مِايَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ دِرْهَمًا
sentences.tr: fa-durtu ʿalā al-mushtarīna fa-jāba kullu ardabbin māyatun wa-ʿishrūna dirhaman
sentences.l: So-I-went-around upon the-buyers, and-brought every ardabb a-hundred and-twenty dirhams.
sentences.i: So I went around to the buyers, and every ardabb fetched a hundred and twenty dirhams.
sentences.n: جاب is colloquial for Classical جاء بِـ, "brought (in)", here "fetched". ماية is the Middle Arabic spelling of مائة, without hamza; and it and وعشرون are left in the nominative, where Classical would use the accusative as the object. I point them as printed. دِرْهَمًا is a regular accusative after twenty.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْتُ مَعِي أَرْبَعَ تَرَّاسِينَ وَمَضَيْتُ إِلَيْهِ فَوَجَدْتُهُ فِي انْتِظَارِي
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhtu maʿī arbaʿa tarrāsīna wa-maḍaytu ilayhi fa-wajadtuhu fī intiẓārī
sentences.l: So-I-took with-me four porters and-went to-him, and-found-him in waiting-for-me.
sentences.i: So I took four porters with me and went to him, and found him waiting for me.
sentences.n: اربع is printed without the tāʾ marbūṭa that the masculine counted noun requires (Classical أربعة), and a sound plural تراسين follows it; both are loose Middle Arabic habits, and I point what is printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآنِي قَامَ إِلَى الْمَخْزَنِ وَفَتَحَهُ حَتَّى فَرَغَ الْمَخْزَنُ فَكِيلْنَاهُ فَجَاءَ خَمْسِينَ أَرْدَ بًّا بِخَمْسَةِ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾānī qāma ilā al-makhzani wa-fataḥahu ḥattā faragha al-makhzanu fa-kīlnāhu fa-jāʾa khamsīna arda bban bi-khamsati ālāfi dirhamin
sentences.l: So-when he-saw-me, he-got-up to the-storeroom and-opened-it, until was-emptied the-storeroom; so-we-measured-it, and-it-came-to fifty ardabb for-five thousand dirham(s).
sentences.i: When he saw me, he went to the storeroom and opened it until the storeroom was emptied; we measured the sesame out, and it came to fifty ardabbs, worth five thousand dirhams.
sentences.n: ارد با is printed as two pieces, ardab + bā, for the accusative ardabban; I keep the space and put the tanwīn on the bā. فكيلناه is printed with a yāʾ, kaylnāhu; I read it as the ordinary kilnāhu, "we measured it", with yāʾ for the long ī (the Classical spelling is كلناه). خمسين is accusative as printed, where "it came to fifty" would take the nominative; and بخمسة آلاف, "for five thousand", is the بِـ of price.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّابُّ لَكَ فِي سَمْسَرَتِكَ فِي كُلِّ أَرْدَبٍّ عَشَرَةٌ وَاقْبِضِ الثَّمَنَ وَخَلِّ لِي عِنْدَكَ أَرْبَعَةَ آلَافٍ وَخَمْسَمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shābbu laka fī samsaratika fī kulli ardabbin ʿasharatun wa-iqbiḍi al-thamana wa-khalli lī ʿindaka arbaʿata ālāfin wa-khamsamiʾati dirhamin
sentences.l: So-said the-youth: For-you, in your-brokerage, in every ardabb, ten; and-take-in-hand the-price, and-leave for-me with-you four thousands and-five-hundred of-dirham(s).
sentences.i: The youth said: Your brokerage is ten dirhams on every ardabb. Collect the price, and keep with you, for me, four thousand five hundred dirhams.
sentences.n: لك في سمسرتك is "yours, as your brokerage": the ten is ten dirhams, as the broker's cut. اقبض الثمن is "take the price (in hand)". The sum left is the five thousand less five hundred in brokerage.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا أَفْرُغُ أَنَا مِنْ بَيْعِ حَوَاصِلِي أَجِيءُ لَكَ آخُذُ الْمَبْلَغَ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā afrughu anā min bayʿi ḥawāṣilī ajīʾu laka ākhudhu al-mablagha min ʿindika fa-qultu lahu naʿam
sentences.l: So-when I-am-free I, from selling-of my-goods, I-come to-you, I-take the-sum from with-you. So-I-said to-him: Yes.
sentences.i: When I have finished selling my goods, I will come to you and take the sum from you. I said to him: Yes.
sentences.n: The print has افرغ, which I read as afrughu, "I finish" (a present tense after إذا); and the pronoun انا is added for emphasis. اجيء لك آخذ is two verbs side by side with no "and": "I come to you, I take", a Middle Arabic way to say "I will come and take". حواصل (ḥawāṣil) are goods in store, stock.

sentences.t: فَقَبَّلْتُ يَدَيْهِ وَمَضَيْتُ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ فَحَصَلَ لِي فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ أَلْفُ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qabbaltu yadayhi wa-maḍaytu min ʿindihi fa-ḥaṣala lī fī dhālika al-yawmi alfu dirhamin
sentences.l: So-I-kissed his-hands and-went from with-him, and-accrued to-me on that the-day a-thousand dirham(s).
sentences.i: I kissed his hands and left him, and that day I made a thousand dirhams.
sentences.n: حصل لي, "accrued to me", is "I gained". The thousand is as printed, though the ten-dirham brokerage on fifty ardabbs would be only five hundred.

sentences.t: فَغَابَ عَنِّي شَهْرًا وَجَاءَ وَقَالَ لِي أَيْنَ الدَّرَاهِمُ
sentences.tr: fa-ghāba ʿannī shahran wa-jāʾa wa-qāla lī ayna al-darāhimu
sentences.l: So-he-was-absent from-me a-month, and-came and-said to-me: Where (are) the-dirhams?
sentences.i: Then he was gone for a month, and came and said to me: Where are the dirhams?

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِ وَقُلْتُ لَهُ هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ تَأْكُلَ عِنْدَنَا شَيْأً فَأَبَى
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-sallamtu ʿalayhi wa-qultu lahu hal laka an taʾkula ʿindanā shayʾan fa-abā
sentences.l: So-I-stood and-greeted upon-him and-said to-him: Is-there for-you (a wish) that you-eat with-us a-thing? And-he-refused.
sentences.i: I stood up, greeted him, and said to him: Would you care to eat something with us? But he refused
sentences.n: هل لك ان تأكل, "is there for you (a wish) to eat", is the polite offer "would you like to eat?". شيأ is printed with a final hamza-alif and no seat for the tanwīn; I point it shayʾan. فابى is fa-abā, "and he refused", written with a dotless final ى.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ احْضِرْلِي الدَّرَاهِمَ حَتَّى أَمْضِيَ وَأَجِيءَ آخُذَهُمْ مِنْكَ ثُمَّ وَلَّى
sentences.tr: wa-qāla aḥḍirlī al-darāhima ḥattā amḍiya wa-ajīʾa ākhudhahum minka thumma wallā
sentences.l: and-said: Bring-me the-dirhams, until I-go and-come, I-take-them from-you. Then he-turned-away.
sentences.i: and said: Bring me the dirhams, so that I may go off and come back and take them from you. Then he turned away.
sentences.n: احضرلي is printed as one word, aḥḍir lī, "bring me"; I keep it as one token. ولى, "he turned (away)", is the usual way to say that someone left.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَأَحْضَرْتُ لَهُ الدَّرَاهِمَ وَقَعَدْتُ أَنْتَظِرُهُ فَغَابَ عَنِّي شَهْرًا وَجَاءَ وَقَالَ لِي أَيْنَ الدَّرَاهِمُ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-aḥḍartu lahu al-darāhima wa-qaʿadtu antaẓiruhu fa-ghāba ʿannī shahran wa-jāʾa wa-qāla lī ayna al-darāhimu
sentences.l: So-I-stood and-brought for-him the-dirhams, and-sat I-wait-for-him; and-he-was-absent from-me a-month, and-came and-said to-me: Where (are) the-dirhams?
sentences.i: So I got up and brought him the dirhams, and sat down waiting for him; but he was gone for another month, and came and said to me: Where are the dirhams?
sentences.n: The whole exchange is now repeated almost word for word, as the print has it. قعدت انتظره, "I sat (and) wait for him", puts two verbs side by side with no "and".

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِ وَقُلْتُ لَهُ هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ تَأْكُلَ عِنْدَنَا شَيْأً فَأَبَى وَقَالَ لِي احْضِرْلِي الدَّرَاهِمَ حَتَّى أَمْضِيَ وَأَجِيءَ آخُذَهُمْ مِنْكَ ثُمَّ وَلَّى
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-sallamtu ʿalayhi wa-qultu lahu hal laka an taʾkula ʿindanā shayʾan fa-abā wa-qāla lī aḥḍirlī al-darāhima ḥattā amḍiya wa-ajīʾa ākhudhahum minka thumma wallā
sentences.l: So-I-stood and-greeted upon-him and-said to-him: Is-there for-you (a wish) that you-eat with-us a-thing? And-he-refused and-said to-me: Bring-me the-dirhams, until I-go and-come, I-take-them from-you. Then he-turned-away.
sentences.i: So I got up, greeted him, and said: Would you care to eat something with us? He refused and said to me: Bring me the dirhams, so that I may go off and come back and take them from you. Then he turned away.
sentences.n: The same lines, repeated verbatim in the print (here تاكل is printed without the hamza that appeared above in تأكل; I supply it).

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَأَحْضَرْتُ لَهُ الدَّرَاهِمَ وَقَعَدْتُ أَنْتَظِرُهُ فَغَابَ عَنِّي شَهْرًا فَقُلْتُ هَذَا الشَّابُّ كَامِلُ السَّمَاحَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-aḥḍartu lahu al-darāhima wa-qaʿadtu antaẓiruhu fa-ghāba ʿannī shahran fa-qultu hādhā al-shābbu kāmilu al-samāḥati
sentences.l: So-I-stood and-brought for-him the-dirhams, and-sat I-wait-for-him; and-he-was-absent from-me a-month. So-I-said: This the-youth (is) complete-of the-generosity.
sentences.i: So I got up and brought him the dirhams, and sat waiting for him; and he was gone for a month. And I said: This youth is perfect in generosity.
sentences.n: كامل السماحة, "complete of generosity", is an iḍāfa of the adjective type: "perfectly generous": the broker concludes that the youth is too open-handed to hurry back for his money.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ الشَّهْرِ جَاءَ رَاكِبًا عَلَى بَغْلَةٍ وَعَلَيْهِ ثِيَابٌ فَاخِرَةٌ وَهُوَ كَالْقَمَرِ لَيْلَةَ الْبَدْرِ فِي تَمَامِهِ وَكَأَنَّهُ قَدْ خَرَجَ مِنَ الْحَمَّامِ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda al-shahri jāʾa rākiban ʿalā baghlatin wa-ʿalayhi thiyābun fākhiratun wa-huwa ka-al-qamari laylata al-badri fī tamāmihi wa-ka-annahu qad kharaja mina al-ḥammāmi
sentences.l: Then after the-month he-came riding upon a-mule, and-upon-him garments splendid, and-he like-the-moon (on) the-night-of the-full-moon in its-completeness, and-as-if-he indeed had-come-out from the-bath.
sentences.i: Then, after the month, he came riding a mule, wearing splendid clothes, and he was like the moon on the night of the full moon at its fullness, as if he had just come out of the bath.
sentences.n: كالقمر ليلة البدر في تمامه: the كَـ here means "like"; ليلة البدر is the fourteenth night of the lunar month, when the moon is full. The comparison with the freshly washed look of one "just come from the bath" is a standard sign of beauty.

sentences.t: وَوَجْهُهُ كَالْقَمَرِ وَهُوَ بِخَدٍّ أَحْمَرَ وَجَبِينٍ أَزْهَرَ وَشَامَةٍ كَأَنَّهَا قُرْصُ عَنْبَرٍ كَمَا قِيلَ فِيهِ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-wajhuhu ka-al-qamari wa-huwa bi-khaddin aḥmara wa-jabīnin azhara wa-shāmatin ka-annahā qurṣu ʿanbarin ka-mā qīla fīhi shiʿrun
sentences.l: And-his-face like-the-moon, and-he with-a-cheek red, and-a-brow radiant, and-a-mole as-if-it (were) a-disc-of ambergris, as was-said of-him in-verse:
sentences.i: His face was like the moon, with a rosy cheek, a shining brow, and a beauty mark like a disc of ambergris, just as was said of him in verse:
sentences.n: بخد احمر, "with a red cheek", is the stock praise of a flushed, healthy cheek; the بِـ marks the feature he has ("with"). الشامة is a beauty mark or mole, thought of as dark like ambergris. شعر is pointed shiʿran, "in verse" (an accusative of manner). The dash that follows it in the print is furniture and is dropped from the text.

sentences.t:
اَلْبَدْرُ وَالشَّمْسُ فِي بُرْجٍ قَدِ اجْتَمَعَا * فِي غَايَةِ الْحُسْنِ وَالْإِقْبَالِ قَدْ طَلَعَا
وَقَدْ اَظْهَرَا حُسْنَهُمْ غَيْرَ النُّفُوسِ بِهِمْ * فَيَا لَهُمْ عِنْدَمَا دَاعِي السِّرِّ وَرِدْعَا
بِالْحُسْنِ وَالظَّرْفِ قَدْ تَمَّتْ مَحَاسِنُهُ * وَزَانَهَا الْعَقْلُ وَالْحَيَاءُ قَدْ بُرِعَا
تَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ مَخْلُوقًا لَهُ عَجَبٌ * مَا شَاءَ رَبُّ الْعُلَا فِي خَلْقِهِ صَنَعَا
sentences.tr:
al-badru wa-al-shamsu fī burjin qadi ijtamaʿā * fī ghāyati al-ḥusni wa-al-iqbāli qad ṭalaʿā
wa-qad aẓharā ḥusnahum ghayra al-nufūsi bihim * fa-yā lahum ʿindamā dāʿī al-sirri wa-ridʿā
bi-al-ḥusni wa-al-ẓarfi qad tammat maḥāsinuhu * wa-zānahā al-ʿaqlu wa-al-ḥayāʾu qad burʿā
tabāraka Allāhu makhlūqan lahu ʿajabun * mā shāʾa rabbu al-ʿulā fī khalqihi ṣanaʿā
sentences.l:
The-full-moon and-the-sun in a-sign indeed have-come-together, * in the-utmost-of the-beauty and-the-good-fortune have-risen;
and-indeed they-two-showed their-beauty, other-than the-souls with-them; * so-O for-them when (the) summoner-of the-secret and-a-stain.
With-the-beauty and-the-grace indeed were-complete his-fine-points, * and-adorned-them the-intellect and-the-modesty, indeed were-excelled.
Blessed-be God (as) a-creature (for whom) is a-wonder; * what willed the-lord-of the-heights in his-creation he-made.
sentences.i:
The full moon and the sun have come together in one sign, risen in the utmost of beauty and good fortune.
They have shown their beauty, beyond what hearts could bear; ah, how it is for them, when the summoner of the secret calls, and a stain.
His fine points are complete in beauty and grace, and intellect and modesty have adorned them, made perfect.
Blessed be God, for a creature of such wonder: whatever the Lord of the heights willed in his creation, he made.
sentences.n: The verse is printed pointed and is copied as printed; the print leaves bare alif with a fatḥa in اَظْهَرَا where Classical writes a hamza. The second line is obscure and may be corrupt: حُسْنَهُمْ is plural though the moon and sun are a pair, غَيْرَ النُّفُوسِ بِهِمْ is hard to place, and the last word وَرِدْعَا (ridʿ, a stain of saffron or blood) looks forced by the rhyme; my English is a tentative reading. In the third line بُرِعَا is a passive form of baraʿa, "to excel", that I have not seen elsewhere; the pointing is kept as printed. إِقْبَال is "good fortune, the turning-toward of favour".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَيْتُهُ قَبَّلْتُ يَدَيْهِ وَقُمْتُ لَهُ وَدَعَوْتُ لَهُ وَقُلْتُ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾaytuhu qabbaltu yadayhi wa-qumtu lahu wa-daʿawtu lahu wa-qultu lahu
sentences.l: And-when I-saw-him, I-kissed his-two-hands, and-I-rose for-him, and-I-prayed for-him, and-I-said to-him:
sentences.i: When I saw him, I kissed his hands, stood up for him, prayed for his well-being, and said to him,
sentences.n: دعوت لَهُ, "I prayed for him", means calling down blessings on him, a courtesy to a guest.

sentences.t: يَا سَيِّدِي مَا تَقْبِضُ دَرَاهِمَكَ
sentences.tr: yā sayyidī mā taqbiḍu darāhimaka
sentences.l: O my-lord, what (that) you-take your-dirhams?
sentences.i: My lord, why do you not collect your dirhams?
sentences.n: Here ما with a plain imperfect asks "why (do you not)?", a colloquial turn; Classical would say لِمَ لَا or مَا لَكَ لَا.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَأَيْشِ الْعَجَلَةُ حَتَّى أَفْرُغَ مِنْ مَصَالِحِي وَآخُذَهَا مِنْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-ayshi al-ʿajalatu ḥattā afrugha min maṣāliḥī wa-ākhudhahā minka
sentences.l: And-he-said: And-what (is) the-haste? Until I-finish from my-affairs and-take-them from-you.
sentences.i: He said, "What is the hurry? Let me finish my errands, and then I will take it from you."
sentences.n: وَأَيْشِ (ايش) is the colloquial "what?", from أَيُّ شَيْءٍ "which thing"; I point it as it is pronounced in the spoken language. The ـهَا of وَآخُذَهَا is feminine singular, standing for the plural دراهمك ("your dirhams"), as Arabic treats plurals of things.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ وَلَّى
sentences.tr: thumma wallā
sentences.l: Then he-turned-away.
sentences.i: Then he went off.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ وَاللَّهِ إِذَا جَاءَ هَذِهِ الْمَرَّةَ لَابُدَّ أَنْ أَعْزِمَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu wa-allāhi idhā jāʾa hādhihi al-marrata lābudda an aʿzima ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And-I-said: By-God, if he-comes this the-time, no-escape that I-urge upon-him.
sentences.i: And I said, "By God, if he comes this time, I must press him to accept my invitation."
sentences.n: لابد is printed as one word, لَا + بُدَّ, "there is no escape (from)", that is, "I must". عزم عليه means to urge someone to accept an invitation, here to dine.

sentences.t: لِكَوْنِى اتَّجَرْتُ فِي دَرَاهِمِهِ وَحَصَّلْتُ مِنْهَا مَالًا كَثِيرًا
sentences.tr: li-kawnī ittajartu fī darāhimihi wa-ḥaṣṣaltu minhā mālan kathīran
sentences.l: For-my-being, I-traded in his-dirhams and-I-gained from-them money, much.
sentences.i: For I had traded with his dirhams and made a good deal of money from them.
sentences.n: لكونى is printed with final ى (not ي), a common spelling of the edition. After لِكَوْنِى, "because I was", Classical would put أَنِّي or a participle; the bare perfect اتجرت that follows is looser, closer to speech: "because — I traded". اتجر is the eighth form, "to trade with".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ آخِرَ السَّنَةِ جَاءَ وَعَلَيْهِ بَدْلَةٌ أَفْخَرُ مِنَ الْأُولَى
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna ākhira al-sanati jāʾa wa-ʿalayhi badlatun afkharu mina al-ūlā
sentences.l: And-when was end-of the-year, he-came, and-upon-him a-suit more-splendid than the-first.
sentences.i: When the year's end came, he returned, and he wore a finer suit of clothes than the first.
sentences.n: آخِرَ السَّنَةِ is pointed as an accusative of time, "at the end of the year", after an impersonal كان. وَعَلَيْهِ is a circumstantial clause: "with upon him ...", that is, "wearing".

sentences.t: فَحَلَفْتُ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَنْزِلَ عِنْدِي وَيَأْكُلَ ضِيَافَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-ḥalaftu ʿalayhi an yanzila ʿindī wa-yaʾkula ḍiyāfatī
sentences.l: And-I-swore upon-him that he-alight with-me and-eat my-hospitality.
sentences.i: So I swore an oath that he must stay with me and eat my hospitality.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي بِشَرْطِ أَنْ مَا تُنْفِقُهُ عَلَيَّ يَكُونُ مِنْ مَالِى الَّذِي عِنْدَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī bi-sharṭi an mā tunfiquhu ʿalayya yakūnu min mālī al-ladhī ʿindaka
sentences.l: And-he-said to-me: On-condition that what you-spend on-me be from my-money that (is) with-you.
sentences.i: He said to me, "On the condition that whatever you spend on me comes out of my own money that you are holding."
sentences.n: أَنْ مَا is printed as two words, "that what"; the clause is introduced without a governing verb, and يكون stays indicative rather than subjunctive after أَنْ; I point it as printed. مالى has final ى for ي, as often.

sentences.t: قُلْتُ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: qultu naʿam
sentences.l: I-said: Yes.
sentences.i: I said, "Yes."
sentences.n: The edition prints قلت without the usual فَـ or وَ; the narrator simply runs on. Not a slip of قال.

sentences.t: وَأَجْلَسْنَهُ وَنَزَلْتُ هَيَّأْتُ مَا يَنْبَغِي مِنَ الْأَطْعِمَةِ وَالْأَشْرِبَةِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-ajlasnahu wa-nazaltu hayyaʾtu mā yanbaghī mina al-aṭʿimati wa-al-ashribati wa-ghayri dhālika
sentences.l: And-I-seated-him, and-I-went-down; I-prepared what (is) fitting of the-foods and-the-drinks and-other-than that.
sentences.i: I seated him, went downstairs, and prepared whatever was fitting of food and drink and the like.
sentences.n: واجلسنه is printed with ن where sense wants ت: it is evidently a compositor's slip for وَأَجْلَسْتُهُ, "and I seated him". I point the letters as printed (the ـنَ would otherwise read as a feminine plural, which cannot be meant) and translate the sense. نَزَلْتُ is followed directly by هَيَّأْتُ with no "and": two verbs side by side, "I went down (and) prepared".

sentences.t: وَجِبْتُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَقُلْتُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: wa-jibtu bayna yadayhi wa-qultu bi-smi allāhi
sentences.l: And-I-brought (it) between his-two-hands, and-I-said: In-the-name-of God.
sentences.i: I set it before him and said, "In the name of God."
sentences.n: جِبْتُ is the colloquial "I brought", from جئت بـ; Classical would be وَجِئْتُ بِهِ. The object is left to be understood, the food. بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ, "between his two hands", is the idiom for "before him".

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ لِلْمَائِدَةِ وَمَدَّيَدَهُ الشِّمَالَ وَأَكَلَ مَعِى
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama li-al-māʾidati wa-maddayadahu al-shimāla wa-akala maʿī
sentences.l: And-he-advanced to-the-table, and-he-stretched-his-hand the-left, and-ate with-me.
sentences.i: He came forward to the table, stretched out his left hand, and ate with me.
sentences.n: ومديده is printed as a single word, وَ + مَدَّ + يَدَهُ, "and he stretched his hand"; I keep the glued spelling and point it as one word. الشِّمَالَ, "the left", is in apposition to the hand, a loose usage. The lām in لِلْمَائِدَةِ is "to/towards", colloquial for إِلَى. معى is spelled with ى.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبْتُ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjabtu minhu
sentences.l: And-I-marvelled at-him.
sentences.i: I was amazed at him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغْنَا غَسَلْتُ يَدَهُ وَنَاوَلْتُهُ مَا يَمْسَحُ بِهِ يَدَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghnā ghasaltu yadahu wa-nāwaltuhu mā yamsaḥu bihi yadahu
sentences.l: And-when we-finished, I-washed his-hand and-I-handed-him what he-wipes with-it his-hand.
sentences.i: When we had finished, I washed his hand and handed him something to dry it with.
sentences.n: As printed, the host says "I washed his hand"; one would expect "he washed his hand" (غَسَلَ) or "my hand". I point the letters as they stand and translate them as printed. The ـبِهِ of يَمْسَحُ بِهِ is the instrument: "wipe (it) with it".

sentences.t: وَجَلَسْنَا لِلْحَدِيثِ بَعْدَ مَا قَدَّمْتُ لَهُ شَيْأً مِنَ الْحَلْوَى فَقُلْتُ
sentences.tr: wa-jalasnā li-al-ḥadīthi baʿda mā qaddamtu lahu shayʾan mina al-ḥalwā fa-qultu
sentences.l: And-we-sat for-the-conversation after that I-presented to-him a-thing of the-sweet, and-I-said:
sentences.i: We sat down to talk, after I had set a few sweets before him, and I said,

sentences.t: يَا سَيِّدِي فَرِّجْ عَنِّي كُرْبَةً
sentences.tr: yā sayyidī farrij ʿannī kurbatan
sentences.l: O my-lord, relieve from-me a-distress:
sentences.i: My lord, relieve me of a distress:
sentences.n: فَرِّجْ عَنِّي كُرْبَةً is a polite request, "lift a worry from me": the host's curiosity is the worry.

sentences.t: لِمَ أَكَلْتَ بِيَدِكَ الشِّمَالِ لَعَلَّ فِي يَدِكَ شَيْأً يُؤْلِمُكَ
sentences.tr: lima akalta bi-yadika al-shimāli laʿalla fī yadika shayʾan yuʾlimuka
sentences.l: Why did-you-eat with-your-hand the-left? Perhaps in your-hand (is) a-thing that-pains-you.
sentences.i: Why did you eat with your left hand? Perhaps there is something in your hand that pains you?

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ كَلَامِي أَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ شِـــــعْـــــرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa kalāmī anshada yaqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: And-when he-heard my-speech, he-recited, saying: Poetry.
sentences.i: When he heard my words, he recited, saying these lines:
sentences.n: شعر, "verse", is the printed heading that stands before a poem; the edition spaces its letters out with long strokes, which I keep.

sentences.t:
خَلِيلَيَّ لَا تَسَالْ عَلَى مَا بِمُهْجَتِي * مِنَ اللَّوْعَةِ الْحَرَّا فَتُظْهِرَ اَسْقَامِي
وَمَا عَنْ رِضًى صَاحَبْتُ سَلْمَى بِدِيَانَةٍ * بِلَيْلَى وَلَكِنْ لِلضَّرُورَةِ اَحْكَامِ
sentences.tr:
khalīlayya lā tasāl ʿalā mā bi-muhjatī * min al-lawʿati al-ḥarrā fa-tuẓhira asqāmī
wa-mā ʿan riḍan ṣāḥabtu salmā bi-diyānatin * bi-laylā wa-lakin li-al-ḍarūrati aḥkāmi
sentences.l:
My-two-friends, not you-ask about what (is) in-my-heart's-blood, * of the-burning-passion, the-fiery, so-that you-bring-out my-sicknesses;
and-not from contentment I-kept-company Salmā, in-piety, in-place-of Laylā, * but for-the-necessity (are) rulings.
sentences.i:
My friends, do not ask what my heart's blood holds, that fiery passion, lest you lay my sicknesses bare.
It was not from contentment that I kept Salmā's company, out of piety, in place of Laylā; but necessity has its rulings.
sentences.n: The verse is printed pointed and is copied as printed. The print has bare alif where Classical writes hamza (تَسَالْ for تَسْأَلْ, اَسْقَامِي, اَحْكَامِ) and ends the last line with a kasra, اَحْكَامِ, where a plain nominative would be expected; I leave both. الْحَرَّا is the printed spelling of الْحَرَّى, "the burning". The second line is obscure to me. I read Salmā and Laylā as two women's names standing for the left and the right hand, so that the speaker is saying he did not choose the left in place of the right, but was forced; this is a guess, and the line may simply be a stock verse about a forced love.

sentences.t: وَأَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ مِنْ كُمِّهِ وَإِذَا هِيَ مَقْطُوعَةُ زَنْدٍ بــلا كَفٍّ
sentences.tr: wa-akhraja yadahu min kummihi wa-idhā hiya maqṭūʿatu zandin bi-lā kaffin
sentences.l: And-he-drew-out his-hand from his-sleeve, and-behold it (was) cut-off-of wrist without palm.
sentences.i: He drew his hand out of his sleeve, and behold, it was cut off at the wrist, with no palm.
sentences.n: مَقْطُوعَةُ زَنْدٍ is pointed as an idafa, "wrist-cut", "cut off at the wrist"; an accusative of specification (مَقْطُوعَةٌ زَنْدًا) is also possible. The زند is the wrist or the forearm near the wrist. وَإِذَا هِيَ "and behold, it" is إذا of surprise; the hand is feminine.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبْتُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjabtu min dhālika
sentences.l: And-I-marvelled at that.
sentences.i: I was amazed at the sight.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي لَا تَعْجَبْ وَلَا تَقُلْ فِي بَالِكَ أَنِّي أَكَلْتُ مَعَكَ بِيَدِيَ الشِّمَالِ عَجَبًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī lā taʿjab wa-lā taqul fī bālika annī akaltu maʿaka bi-yadiya al-shimāli ʿajaban
sentences.l: And-he-said to-me: Do-not marvel, and-do-not say in your-mind that-I ate with-you with-my-hand the-left (as) a-marvel.
sentences.i: He said to me, "Do not be amazed, and do not tell yourself that it is strange that I ate with you with my left hand,
sentences.n: قال في بالك, "say in your mind", is the idiom for "think". عجبا is an accusative of the thing wondered at: "(do not think that it is) a marvel".

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ لِقَطْعِ الْيَمِينِ سَبَبٌ مِنَ الْعَجَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-lakin li-qatʿi al-yamīni sababun mina al-ʿajabi
sentences.l: And-but for-the-cutting-of the-right a-cause (that is) of the-wonder.
sentences.i: for the cutting off of my right hand has a cause, and a wondrous one."
sentences.n: لِقَطْعِ here is the lām of reason or ownership: "for the cutting off ... (there is) a cause". اليمين, "the right", stands for the right hand. من العجب means "of the wonders", that is, "of the marvellous kind".

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ وَمَاسَبَبُ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu wa-māsababu dhālika
sentences.l: And-I-said to-him: And-what-the-cause-of that?
sentences.i: I said to him, "And what is the cause of that?"
sentences.n: The edition prints وماسبب with وَ + مَا + سَبَب glued into one word; I keep it as one word, and point it accordingly.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ اِعْلَمْ أَنِّي مِنْ أَوْلَادِ بَغْدَادَ وَوَالِدِي مِنْ أَكَابِرِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla iʿlam annī min awlādi baghdāda wa-wālidī min akābirihā
sentences.l: And-he-said: Know that-I (am) from the-sons-of Baghdad, and-my-father (was) from its-great-ones.
sentences.i: He said, "Know that I am a native of Baghdad, and my father was one of its notables.
sentences.n: أولاد بغداد, "sons of Baghdad", means "natives of Baghdad". أكابر is the plural of أكبر, "greater", used as a noun for "the great".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا بَلَغْتُ مَبْلَغَ الرِّجَالِ سَمِعْتُ السَّيَّاحِينَ وَالْمُسَافِرِينَ وَالتُّجَّارَ يَتَحَدَّثُونَ عَنِ الدِّيَارِ الْمِصْرِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā balaghtu mablagha al-rijāli samiʿtu al-sayyāḥīna wa-al-musāfirīna wa-al-tujjāra yataḥaddathūna ʿani al-diyāri al-miṣriyyati
sentences.l: And-when I-reached the-reach-of the-men, I-heard the-travellers and-the-voyagers and-the-merchants speaking about the-lands the-Egyptian.
sentences.i: When I reached manhood, I heard travellers, voyagers and merchants talking about the land of Egypt.
sentences.n: مَبْلَغَ الرِّجَالِ, "the reach of men", is manhood. السياحين, with the sound plural, is the printed form of the "travellers" (سَيَّاحُونَ); I point it as an accusative object. الديار المصرية is literally "the Egyptian abodes", the usual way to say the land of Egypt.

sentences.t: فَبَقِيَ ذَلِكَ فِي خَاطِرِي حَتَّى مَاتَ وَالِدِي
sentences.tr: fa-baqiya dhālika fī khāṭirī ḥattā māta wālidī
sentences.l: And-remained that in my-mind until died my-father.
sentences.i: And that stayed in my mind until my father died.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْتُ أَمْوَالًا كَثِيرَةً
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhtu amwālan kathīratan
sentences.l: And-I-took wealth(s), many.
sentences.i: Then I took a great fortune,
sentences.n: أخذت, "I took", is "I took my inheritance": the money is his father's estate.

sentences.t: وَعَبَّيْتُ مَتْجَرًا مِنْ قُمَاشٍ بَغْدَادِىٍّ وَمَوْصِلِيٍّ وَسَرَّيْتُ الْكُلَّ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿabbaytu matjaran min qumāshin baghdādiyyin wa-mawṣiliyyin wa-sarraytu al-kulla
sentences.l: And-I-packed a-merchandise of cloth Baghdadi and-Mosuli, and-I-dispatched the-whole.
sentences.i: and packed a stock of Baghdadi and Mosuli cloth, and I sent the whole lot off.
sentences.n: عَبَّيْتُ is the colloquial "I packed (goods) up" (Classical عَبَّأْتُ). سَرَّيْتُ الْكُلَّ is the doubtful word: it could be "I sent it all on its way" or something like "I got it all ready", and I am not sure of the root; I translate by the sense of the sentence. بغدادى has ى for ي. موصلي, "of Mosul", was a famed cloth town.

sentences.t: وَسَفَرْتُ مِنْ بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: wa-safartu min baghdāda
sentences.l: And-I-set-out from Baghdad.
sentences.i: I set out from Baghdad,
sentences.n: سَفَرْتُ is printed without the alif of the third form (سَافَرْتُ), and is pointed as the simple verb سَفَرَ, "to go forth", which is Classical for departing on a journey.

sentences.t: وَكَتَبَ اللَّهُ لِي السَّلَامَةَ حَتَّى دَخَلْتُ مَدِينَتَكُمْ هَذِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kataba allāhu lī al-salāmata ḥattā dakhaltu madīnatakum hādhihi
sentences.l: And-wrote God for-me the-safety until I-entered your-city this.
sentences.i: and God wrote safety for me, until I entered this city of yours.
sentences.n: كتب الله لي, "God wrote for me", means He decreed it for me: what is written is what is fated.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَكَى وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُ — وْلُ
sentences.tr: thumma bakā wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: Then he-wept and-recited, saying:
sentences.i: Then he wept, and recited:
sentences.n: The word يقول is split across a line-end by the printer's dash (يق — ول); I keep the break as printed and point each part so that together they read yaqūlu.

sentences.t:
قَدْ يَسْلَمُ الْمُطْمِسُ مِنْ حُفْرَةٍ * وَيَقَعُ فِيهَا الْبَاصِرُ النَّاظِرُ
وَيَسْلَمُ الْجَاهِلُ مِنْ لَفْطَةٍ * وَيَهْلَكُ فِيهَا الْعَالِمُ الْمَاهِرُ
وَيُعْسِرُ الْمُؤْمِنُ فِي رِزْقِهِ * وَيُرْزَقُ الْكَافِرُ وَالْفَاجِرُ
مَا حِيلَةُ الْمَرْءِ وَمَا فِعْلُهُ * هَذَا الَّذِي قَدَّرَهُ الْقَادِرُ
sentences.tr:
qad yaslamu al-muṭmisu min ḥufratin * wa-yaqaʿu fīhā al-bāṣiru al-nāẓiru
wa-yaslamu al-jāhilu min lafṭatin * wa-yahlaku fīhā al-ʿālimu al-māhiru
wa-yuʿsiru al-muʾminu fī rizqihi * wa-yurzaqu al-kāfiru wa-al-fājiru
mā ḥīlatu al-marʾi wa-mā fiʿluhu * hādhā al-ladhī qaddarahu al-qādiru
sentences.n: The verse is printed pointed and is copied as printed. المُطْمِس is the man whose eyes are blotted out, that is, the blind. لَفْطَة is printed with ط; it is probably لَفْظَة, "an utterance", so that the line says the ignorant escapes a slip of the tongue, while the learned is undone by one; I keep the ط as printed. يُعْسِرُ is pointed as an active, "is in difficulty"; the Classical form would be the passive يُعْسَرُ or يَعْسُرُ, and I leave the printed vowel. القادر, "the Able", is a name of God.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ قَٰلَ فَدَخَلْتُ مِصْرَو نَزَّلْتُ الْقُمَاشَ فِي خَانِ مَسْرُورٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi qāla fa-dakhaltu miṣra wa-nazzaltu al-qumāsha fī khāni masrūrin
sentences.l: And-when he-finished from his-poetry, he-said: And-I-entered Miṣr, and-I-unloaded the-cloth in the-khan-of Masrūr,
sentences.i: When he had finished his verses, he said: I entered Cairo and unloaded my cloth at the Khan of Masrūr.
sentences.n: قل is printed for قال; read qāla and pointed with the dagger alif. The printer has put the و of ونزلت ("and I unloaded") on the end of the word before it, giving مصرو; read Miṣra wa-nazzaltu. Miṣr is Cairo here, as often in the Nights.

sentences.t: وَفَكَيْتُ أَحْمَالِي وَدَخَلْتُهَا وَأَعْطَيْتُ الْخَادِمَ دَرَاهِمَ يَشْتَرِي لَنَا شَيْأً نَأكُلُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-fakaytu aḥmālī wa-dakhaltuhā wa-aʿṭaytu al-khādima darāhima yashtarī lanā shayʾan nākuluhu
sentences.l: And-I-undid my-loads, and-I-entered-it, and-I-gave the-servant dirhams (that) he-buy for-us something we-eat-it.
sentences.i: I undid my bales and went into the room, and gave the servant some dirhams to buy us something to eat.
sentences.n: فكيت is a colloquial form of فككت, "I undid"; the verb of a weak root has been made out of a doubled one. ودخلتها, "and I entered it", refers to the room I took in the khan. يشتري has no أن before it: the two verbs simply follow each other, which is normal in Middle Arabic. شيأ is printed with a hamza (أ) after the yā; read shayʾan.

sentences.t: وَنِمْتُ قَلِيلًا فَلَمَّا قُمْتُ ذَهَبْتُ بَيْنَ الْقَصْرَيْنِ وَرَجَعْتُ بِتُّ لَيْلَتِي
sentences.tr: wa-nimtu qalīlan fa-lammā qumtu dhahabtu bayna al-qaṣrayni wa-rajaʿtu bittu laylatī
sentences.l: And-I-slept a-little; and-when I-rose, I-went between the-two-palaces, and-I-returned, I-spent-the-night my-night.
sentences.i: I slept a little, and when I got up I walked out to Bayn al-Qaṣrayn, then came back and spent the night.
sentences.n: بين القصرين, "between the two palaces", is the famous street in the old centre of Cairo. بت ليلتي ("I passed my night") is a fixed phrase; the second verb simply follows the first without a conjunction.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحْتُ فَتَحْتُ فَرْدَةً مِنَ الْقُمَاشِ وَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي أَقُومُ أَشُقُّ بَعْضَ الْأَسْوَاقِ وَأَنْظُرُ الْحَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥtu fataḥtu fardatan mina al-qumāshi wa-qultu fī nafsī aqūmu ashuqqu baʿḍa al-aswāqi wa-anẓuru al-ḥāla
sentences.l: And-when I-became-morning, I-opened a-bale from the-cloth, and-I-said in my-self: I-will-rise, I-will-cleave some-of the-markets, and-I-will-look-at the-state.
sentences.i: When morning came I opened one bale of cloth and said to myself: I will get up, stroll through some of the markets, and see how things stand.
sentences.n: اشق بعض الاسواق, literally "I split some of the markets", means to make one's way through them. الحال, "the state (of things)", is here the general situation of the city and its trade.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذْتُ بَعْضَ الْقُمَاشِ وَحَمَلْتُهُ لِبَعْضِ غِلْمَانِي وَسِرْتُ حَتَّى وَصَلْتُ قَيْصَرِيَّةَ جِرْجِسَ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadtu baʿḍa al-qumāshi wa-ḥamaltuhu li-baʿḍi ghilmānī wa-sirtu ḥattā waṣaltu qayṣariyyata jirjisa
sentences.l: And-I-took some-of the-cloth, and-I-loaded-it on-some-of my-boys, and-I-walked until I-arrived-at the-qaysariyya-of Jirjis.
sentences.i: I took some of the cloth, had one of my boys carry it, and walked until I reached the Qayṣariyya of Jirjis.
sentences.n: وحملته لبعض غلماني is literally "I loaded it on some of my boys": the cloth was given to a servant to carry. A قيصرية is a covered market hall for cloth; this one is named for Jirjis (George).

sentences.t: فَاسْتَقْبَلَنِي السِّمَا سِرَةُ وَكَانُوا عَلِمُوا بِمَجِئِي فَأَخَذُوا مِنِّي الْقُمَاشَ وَنَادَوْا عَلَيْهِ فَلَمْ يَجِبْ رَأْسُ مَا لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-istaqbalanī al-simā sirati wa-kānū ʿalimū bi-majīʾī fa-akhadhū minnī al-qumāsha wa-nādaw ʿalayhi fa-lam yajib raʾsu mā lahu
sentences.l: So-met-me the-brokers, and-they-were they-had-known of-my-coming, so-they-took from-me the-cloth and-called-out over-it, and-it-did-not come-due (to) the-head-of what to-it.
sentences.i: The brokers came to meet me, for they had already learned of my arrival. They took the cloth from me and cried it for sale, but the bids did not even reach its cost.
sentences.n: السما سرة is the word السماسرة, "brokers", split by a space in the print; read al-samāsira. In Middle Arabic وكانوا علموا ("they had known") strings the auxiliary and the verb with no particle. فلم يجب رأس ما له is obscure; the print splits ماله into two words, which I read as māl-ihi, "its capital", spelled as ma lahu: I read yajib, "to be due, to reach", so that the price did not reach even the capital (cost) of the cloth, which is how the next sentence takes it; but the form could also be a colloquial "bring" (جاب), and the sense would stay about the same.

sentences.t: فَاغْتَمَيْتُ لِذَلِكَ فَقَالَ لِى شَيْخُ الدَّلَّالِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-ightamaytu li-dhālika fa-qāla lī shaykhu al-dallālīna
sentences.l: So-I-was-grieved for-that; so-he-said to-me, the-elder-of the-auctioneers:
sentences.i: I was distressed by this, and the head of the auctioneers said to me:
sentences.n: اغتميت is a Middle Arabic form of اغتممت, "I was distressed": a doubled verb has been conjugated like a weak one. لى is printed with ى for ي, as the edition often does; read lī. The دلالون are the auctioneers who cry goods for sale in the market.

sentences.t: يَاسَيِّدِي أَعْرِفُ لَكَ شَيْأً تَسْتَفِيدُ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: yāsayyidī aʿrifu laka shayʾan tastafīdu minhu
sentences.l: O-my-master, I-know for-you something you-profit from-it.
sentences.i: My lord, I know of something that will profit you.
sentences.n: ياسيدي is printed as one word; read yā sayyidī. There is no relative pronoun before تستفيد: "something you profit from" is a plain asyndetic relative clause.

sentences.t: تَعْمَلُ مَا يَعْمَلُ التُّجَّا وَتَبِيعُ مَتْجَرَكَ إِلَى أَشْهُرٍ مَعْلُومَةٍ بِكَاتِبٍ وَشَاهِدٍ وَصَيْرَفِيٍّ
sentences.tr: taʿmalu mā yaʿmalu al-tujjā wa-tabīʿu matjaraka ilā ashhurin maʿlūmatin bi-kātibin wa-shāhidin wa-ṣayrafiyyin
sentences.l: You-do what they-do the-merchants, and-you-sell your-merchandise to months known, with-a-clerk and-a-witness and-a-money-changer,
sentences.i: Do what the merchants do: sell your goods on credit for a fixed number of months, with a clerk, a witness and a money-changer attending,
sentences.n: التجا is التجار "the merchants" with the final ر dropped by the printer; read al-tujjār. The creditors' note is drawn up before a clerk, a witness and a money-changer (صيرفي), who guarantees it. بكاتب etc.: بِـ here means "in the presence of / by means of".

sentences.t: وَتَأْخُذُ مَالَكَ كُلَّ يَوْمِ خَمِيسٍ وَ اثْنَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-taʾkhudhu mālaka kulla yawmi khamīsin wa ithnayni
sentences.l: and-you-take your-wealth every day-of Thursday and Monday;
sentences.i: and collect your money every Thursday and Monday.
sentences.n: Thursday (al-khamīs, "the fifth") and Monday (al-ithnayn, "the second") are the two days of the week on which the merchants settled their accounts. The edition prints the و as a word of its own at the end of the line, before اثنين.

sentences.t: فَتَكْسِبُ الدَّرَاهِمَ كُلَّ دِرْهَمٍ اثْنَيْنِ وَزِيَادَةً عَلَى ذَلِكَ تَتَفَرَّجُ عَلَى مِصْرَو نِيلِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-taksibu al-darāhima kulla dirhamin ithnayni wa-ziyādatan ʿalā dhālika tatafarraju ʿalā miṣra wa-nīlihā
sentences.l: So-you-earn the-dirhams, every dirham two, and-an-increase over that you-take-a-stroll over Miṣr and-its-Nile.
sentences.i: You will earn dirhams, two for every one, and on top of that you can enjoy yourself looking over Cairo and its Nile.
sentences.n: كل درهم اثنين, "every dirham two", means that each dirham brings you another: your money doubles. The و of ونيلها is printed on the end of the word before it (مصرو نيلها); read Miṣra wa-nīlihā. تتفرج على, "you take in the sights of", is a colloquial turn.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ هَذَا رَأْيٌ سَدِيدٌ فَأَخَذْتُ مَعِي الدَّلَّالِينَ وَذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْخَانِ فَأَخَذُوا الْقُمَاشَ إِلَى الْقَيْصَرِيَّةِ وَبِعْتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu hādhā raʾyun sadīdun fa-akhadhtu maʿī al-dallālīna wa-dhahabtu ilā al-khāni fa-akhadhū al-qumāsha ilā al-qayṣariyyati wa-biʿtuhu
sentences.l: So-I-said: This is an-opinion sound. So-I-took with-me the-auctioneers, and-I-went to the-khan, and-they-took the-cloth to the-qaysariyya, and-I-sold-it.
sentences.i: I said: That is sound advice. So I took the auctioneers with me, went to the khan, and they carried the cloth to the Qayṣariyya, where I sold it.

sentences.t: وَكَتَبْتُ عَلَيْهِمُ الثَّمَنَ وَرَفَعْتُ الْوَرَقَةَ لِلصَّيْرَفِيِّ وَأَخَذْتُ وَرَقَةً وَرَجَعْتُ الْخَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-katabtu ʿalayhimu al-thamana wa-rafaʿtu al-waraqata li-al-ṣayrafiyyi wa-akhadhtu waraqatan wa-rajaʿtu al-khāna
sentences.l: And-I-wrote against-them the-price, and-I-raised the-paper to-the-money-changer, and-I-took a-paper, and-I-returned-to the-khan.
sentences.i: I wrote the price down against the buyers, handed the note to the money-changer, took a receipt, and returned to the khan.
sentences.n: كتبت عليهم الثمن, "I wrote the price against them", records the sum as a debt owed by the buyers. رجعت الخان, "I returned the khan", takes the place directly as its object, with no إلى.

sentences.t: وَأَقَمْتُ أَيَّا مًا كُلَّ يَوْمٍ أُفْطِرُ عَلَى قَدَحِ شَرَابٍ وَأُحْضِرُ اللَّحْمَ الضَّانِيَ وَالْحَلْوِيَاتِ شَهْرًا
sentences.tr: wa-aqamtu ayyāman kulla yawmin ufṭiru ʿalā qadaḥi sharābin wa-uḥḍiru al-laḥma al-ḍāniya wa-al-ḥalwiyyāti shahran
sentences.l: And-I-stayed days — every day I-break-fast on a-cup-of drink and-I-bring the-meat the-sheep and-the-sweets — a-month.
sentences.i: I stayed there for days, every day breaking my fast over a cup of wine and sending for mutton and sweetmeats, for a whole month.
sentences.n: ايا ما is a split spelling of أياما, "days"; read ayyāman. شراب, "drink", is the usual word for wine in the Nights; the edition leaves it as plain "drink", and so does the literal line. اللحم الضاني is "sheep's meat", mutton. The sentence is a run of verbs without particles; the time expression شهرا, "for a month", closes it.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَ الشَّهْرُ الَّذِي اسْتَحْقَيْتُ فِيهِ الْجِبَايَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhala al-shahru alladhī istaḥqaytu fīhi al-jibāyata
sentences.l: And-entered the-month which I-was-entitled in-it (to) the-collection.
sentences.i: And the month came round in which I was due to collect.
sentences.n: استحقيت is the colloquial form of استحققت, "I was entitled to"; the doubled verb is treated as a weak one. الجباية is the collecting of what is owed (here, the money due on the sales). "The month entered" is the idiom for a new month beginning.

sentences.t: فَبَقِيتُ كُلَّ يَوْمِ خَمِيسٍ وَاثْنَيْنِ أَدْخُلُ الْقَيْصَرِيَّةَ وَأَقْعُدُ عَلَى دَكَاكِينِ التُّجَّارِوَ يَمْضِي الصَّيْرَفِيُّ وَالْكَاتِبُ يَجِيبُونَ الدَّرَاهِمَ مِنَ التُّجَّارِ إِلَى بَعْدِ الْعَصْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-baqītu kulla yawmi khamīsin wa-ithnayni adkhulu al-qayṣariyyata wa-aqʿudu ʿalā dakākīni al-tujjāri wa yamḍī al-ṣayrafiyyu wa-al-kātibu yajībūna al-darāhima mina al-tujjāri ilā baʿdi al-ʿaṣri
sentences.l: So-I-remained every day-of Thursday and-Monday I-enter the-qaysariyya and-I-sit on the-shops-of the-merchants, and the-money-changer signs, and-the-clerk, they-bring the-dirhams from the-merchants, until after the-afternoon.
sentences.i: So every Thursday and Monday I went into the Qayṣariyya and sat at the merchants' shops while the money-changer and the clerk signed and fetched the dirhams from the merchants, until after the afternoon prayer.
sentences.n: The و that starts "the money-changer signs" is printed on the end of التجار (التجارو); read al-tujjāri wa-yamḍī. يمضي is "signs, endorses", from أمضى. يجيبون is colloquial "they bring" (Classical يجيئون or يجلبون), with the clerk added after the money-changer as a second subject. The "ʿaṣr" is the mid-afternoon prayer time.

sentences.t: فَأَحْسُبُهَا وَأَخْتِمُهَا وَآخُذُهَا وَأَنْصَرِفُ إِلَى الْخَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-aḥsubuhā wa-akhtimuhā wa-ākhudhuhā wa-anṣarifu ilā al-khāni
sentences.l: So-I-count-them, and-I-seal-them, and-I-take-them, and-I-depart to the-khan.
sentences.i: I would count the dirhams, seal them, take them, and go back to the khan.
sentences.n: The feminine pronoun in احسبها refers to الدراهم, "the dirhams" (a plural of things takes the feminine singular).

sentences.t: فَفِي يَوْمٍ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ وَكَانَ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-fī yawmin mina al-ayyāmi wa-kāna yawma al-ithnayni
sentences.l: And-on a-day from the-days — and-it-was the-day-of the-Monday —
sentences.i: Then one day, and it was a Monday,
sentences.n: في يوم من الأيام, "on one of the days", is the usual way of beginning "one day" in a story.

sentences.t: دَخَلْتُ الْحَمَّامَ وَخَرَجْتُ إِلَى الْخَانِ وَدَخَلْتُ مَوْضِعِي وَفَطَرْتُ عَلَى قَدَحِ الشَّرَابِ وَنِمْتُ وَانْتَبَهْتُ
sentences.tr: dakhaltu al-ḥammāma wa-kharajtu ilā al-khāni wa-dakhaltu mawḍiʿī wa-faṭartu ʿalā qadaḥi al-sharābi wa-nimtu wa-intabahtu
sentences.l: I-entered the-bath, and-I-went-out to the-khan, and-I-entered my-place, and-I-broke-fast on the-cup-of the-drink, and-I-slept, and-I-woke.
sentences.i: I went to the bath, came out and returned to the khan, went into my room, broke my fast over a cup of wine, slept, and woke.
sentences.n: فطرت is Form I (faṭara) where Classical Arabic would use Form IV, أفطرت, "I broke my fast"; I read it as printed. The meal is breakfast, since the narrator has just risen.

sentences.t: فَأَكَلْتُ دَجَاجَةً وَتَعَطَّرْتُ وَذَهَبْتُ لِلدُّكَّانِ تَاجِرٍ يَقُولُ لَهُ بَدْرُالدِّينِ الْبُسْتَانِيُّ
sentences.tr: fa-akaltu dajājatan wa-taʿaṭṭartu wa-dhahabtu li-al-dukkāni tājirin yaqūlu lahu badru al-dīni al-bustāniyyu
sentences.l: So-I-ate a-chicken, and-I-perfumed-myself, and-I-went to-the-shop-of a-merchant, one-says to-him Badr-al-Dīn the-gardener.
sentences.i: Then I ate a chicken, put on perfume, and went to the shop of a merchant called Badr al-Dīn the Gardener.
sentences.n: للدكان تاجر is printed with the article on دكان even though it is the first term of a genitive ("the shop of a merchant"); read li-al-dukkāni tājirin, with the article taken as a slip for لدكان تاجر. يقول له, literally "says to him", is the impersonal "one calls him", Classical يقال له. In بدرالدين the printer joins the two parts of the name; read Badr al-Dīn.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآنِي رَحَّبَ بِي وَتَحَدَّثْتُ مَعِي سَاعَةً حَتَّى قَامَ السُّوقُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾānī raḥḥaba bī wa-taḥaddathtu maʿī sāʿatan ḥattā qāma al-sūqu
sentences.l: And-when he-saw-me he-welcomed me, and-I-talked with-me an-hour, until the-market stood-up.
sentences.i: When he saw me he welcomed me, and we talked for an hour, until the market was in full swing.
sentences.n: وتحدثت معي is printed with first-person endings and with معي, "with me", where the sense requires "and he talked with me" or "and I talked with him" (تحدث معي / تحدثت معه). It looks like a slip; I point it as printed and the idiomatic line gives the sense. قام السوق, "the market stood up", means that trade was at its height.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِأمْرَأَةٍ مَيَّاسَةِ الْقَوَامِ وَهِيَ تَتَبَخْتَرُ فِي مَشْيِهَا جَاءَتْ بِعُصْبَةٍ هَائِلَةٍ وَرَوَائِحَ فَائِحَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-imraʾatin mayyāsati al-qawāmi wa-hiya tatabakhtaru fī mashyihā jāʾat bi-ʿuṣbatin hāʾilatin wa-rawāʾiḥa fāʾiḥatin
sentences.l: And-behold, with-a-woman swaying-of the-stature, and-she strutting in her-walking; she-came with-a-turban awesome and-scents wafting.
sentences.i: And behold, a woman of swaying figure, strutting as she walked. She came in a magnificent headdress, with fragrances wafting from her.
sentences.n: The بِـ after وإذا only marks what appears: "and behold, a woman". جاءت بعصبة هائلة is "she came with a wondrous headband": عصبة is a band or turban-cloth, here a rich head-covering. I read it so; the word can also mean "a company", but the perfumes that follow make the headdress the more likely sense. The phrase after مياسة is a genitive of limitation: "swaying of figure".

sentences.t: وَرَفَعَتِ الشِّعْرِيَّةَ فَنَظَرْتُ إِلَى أَحْدَاقٍ سُودٍ
sentences.tr: wa-rafaʿati al-shiʿriyyata fa-naẓartu ilā aḥdāqin sūdin
sentences.l: And-she-raised the-hair-veil, and-I-looked at eyes black.
sentences.i: She lifted her veil, and I looked into black eyes.
sentences.n: الشعرية is the sheʿriyya, the fine black mesh veil worn over the face. The narrator is struck first by her eyes as the veil goes up.

sentences.t: فَسَلَّمَتْ عَلَى بَدْرِالدِّينِ فَرَدَّ عَلَيْهَا السَّلَامَ وَوَقَفَ وَتَحَدَّثَ مَعَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-sallamat ʿalā badri al-dīni fa-radda ʿalayhā al-salāma wa-waqafa wa-taḥaddatha maʿahā
sentences.l: So-she-greeted Badr-al-Dīn, and-he-returned to-her the-greeting, and-he-stood, and-he-conversed with-her.
sentences.i: She greeted Badr al-Dīn; he returned her greeting, stood up, and conversed with her.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ كَلَامَهَا تَمَكَّنَ حُبُّهَا مِنْ قَلْبِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu kalāmahā tamakkana ḥubbuhā min qalbī
sentences.l: And-when I-heard her-speech, her-love took-hold from my-heart.
sentences.i: When I heard her speak, love of her took hold of my heart.
sentences.n: تمكن حبها من قلبي is literally "her love gained a seat from my heart": it settled in and took possession. The preposition من is the one the verb chooses.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لِبَدْرِالدِّينِ هَلْ عِنْدَكَ تَفْصِيلَةٌ طَرْدُ وَحْشٍ مُقَصَّبٌ طَرْشٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu li-badri al-dīni hal ʿindaka tafṣīlatun ṭardu waḥshin muqaṣṣabun ṭarshun
sentences.l: So-I-said to-Badr-al-Dīn: Is there with-you a-dress-length, a-chase-of wild-beasts, gold-threaded, ṭarsh?
sentences.i: I said to Badr al-Dīn: Have you a dress-length woven with a hunt of wild beasts, in gold thread, and ṭarsh?
sentences.n: This is a list of the features of a cloth, and I give each word as printed. تفصيلة is a length cut to make a dress. طرد وحش, "chase of wild beasts", is a design of hunting scenes. مقصب is "gold-threaded" (from قصب, gold or silver thread). طرش is obscure to me; it may name a type of weave, but it could also be corrupt, and I leave it untranslated.

sentences.t: فَأَخْرَجَ لَهَا تَفْصِيلَةً مِنَ التَّفَاصِيلِ الَّتِي اشْتَرَاهَا مِنِّي فَبَايَعْتُهُ عَلَيْهَا بِأَلْفٍ وَمِائَتَيْنِ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: fa-akhraja lahā tafṣīlatan mina al-tafāṣīli allatī ishtarāhā minnī fa-bāyaʿtuhu ʿalayhā bi-alfin wa-miʾatayni dirhamin
sentences.l: So-he-brought-out for-her a-dress-length from the-dress-lengths which he-had-bought-them from-me; so-I-bargained-with-him over-it for-a-thousand and-two-hundred dirhams.
sentences.i: So he brought out for her a length from among those he had bought from me, and I struck a bargain with him for it at twelve hundred dirhams.
sentences.n: The last clause is hard to read: the narrator is bargaining with the merchant for the piece, even though the cloth was his own, so I take فبايعته عليها as "I agreed a price with him over it" for the lady's sake. بِـ in بألف gives the price, "at a thousand". ومائتين is "and two hundred"; the print spells the hundreds with ئ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِلتَّاجِرِ آخُذُ التَّفْصِيلَةَ وَأَذْهَبُ أُرْسِلُ لَكَ ثَمَنَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat li-al-tājiri ākhudhu al-tafṣīlata wa-adhhabu ursilu laka thamanahā
sentences.l: So-she-said to-the-merchant: I-take the-dress-length, and-I-go, I-send to-you its-price.
sentences.i: She said to the merchant: I will take the length and go, and send you its price.
sentences.n: The two verbs after واذهب ("I go, I send") stand side by side with no linking particle, as often in Middle Arabic and in speech.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا التَّاجِرُ لَايُمْكِنُ يَاسِتِّي لِأَنَّ هَذَا صَاحِبُ الْقُمَاشِ وَلَهُ عَلَيَّ قِسْطٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā al-tājiru lāyumkinu yāsittī li-anna hādhā ṣāḥibu al-qumāshi wa-lahu ʿalayya qisṭun
sentences.l: So-said to-her the-merchant: It-is-not-possible, O-my-lady, because this-one is the-owner-of the-cloth, and-to-him upon-me is-an-instalment.
sentences.i: The merchant said to her: It cannot be, my lady, for this gentleman is the owner of the cloth, and I owe him an instalment.
sentences.n: لايمكن is printed as one word, and ياستي (yā sittī, "O my lady") likewise; read lā yumkinu and yā sittī. ستي is the colloquial "my lady" (from سيدتي). قسط is a part-payment or instalment that falls due.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ وَيْلَكَ إِنِّي مُعَوَّدَةٌ آخُذُ مِنْكَ كُلَّ قِطْعَةِ قُمَاشٍ بِجُمْلَةٍ مِنَ الدَّرَاهِمِ وَأُفِيدُكَ فِيهَا فَوْقَ مَاتُرِيدُ وَأُرْسِلُ لَكَ ثَمَنَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat waylaka innī muʿawwadatun ākhudhu minka kulla qiṭʿati qumāshin bi-jumlatin mina al-darāhimi wa-ufīduka fīhā fawqa māturīdu wa-ursilu laka thamanahā
sentences.l: So-she-said: Woe-to-you! I (am) accustomed (that) I-take from-you every piece-of cloth for-a-sum from the-dirhams, and-I-benefit-you in-it above what-you-want, and-I-send to-you its-price.
sentences.i: She said: Shame on you! I am used to taking from you every piece of cloth for a round sum of dirhams, and I make it worth your while, above what you ask, and I send you the price.
sentences.n: ويلك, "woe to you", is a mild scolding here, the way one might say "for shame". Note that مُعَوَّدَة, "accustomed", takes a bare verb after it (آخذ) with no أن. ماتريد is printed as one word; read mā turīdu, "what you want".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نَعَمْ وَلَكِنِّي مُضْطَرٌّ إِلَى الثَّمَنِ فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla naʿam wa-lākinnī muḍṭarrun ilā al-thamani fī hādhā al-yawmi
sentences.l: So-he-said: Yes, but-I (am) compelled to the-price on this the-day.
sentences.i: He said: Yes, but I need the money today.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتِ التَّفْصِيلَةَ وَرَمَتْ بِهَا فِي صَدْرِهِ وَقَٰلَتْ طَائِفَتُكُمْ لَا تَعْرِفُ لِأَحَدٍقِيمَةً
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhati al-tafṣīlata wa-ramat bihā fī ṣadrihi wa-qālat ṭāʾifatukum lā taʿrifu li-aḥadinqīmatan
sentences.l: So-she-took the-dress-length, and-she-threw with-it in his-chest, and-she-said: Your-sort not knows for-anyone a-value.
sentences.i: She took the length and flung it at his chest, and said: Your kind has no notion of anyone's worth.
sentences.n: وقلت is printed for وقالت, "and she said", with the same slip as قل for قال; I point it with the dagger alif and read it qālat. لاحدقيمة is printed as one word, لأحد قيمة, "for anyone a value"; I keep it as a single word. طائفتكم, "your sort", is the lady's contemptuous word for merchants, who do not value a good customer.

sentences.t: وَقَامَتْ مُوَايَةً فَحَسَيْتُ بِرُوحِي رَاحَتْ مَعَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāmat muwāyatan fa-ḥasaytu bi-rūḥī rāḥat maʿahā
sentences.l: And-she-rose turning-away, so-I-felt with-my-soul it-had-gone with-her.
sentences.i: She rose and turned away, and I felt my soul go with her.
sentences.n: مواية looks like a misprint for مولية, muwalliya, "turning away", a word the next lines support (وقد ولت, "and she had turned away"); I keep the printed letters and point it muwāyatan. حسيت is colloquial for حسست, "I felt", with the weak-verb ending for a doubled verb. حس بـ is "to feel (something)".

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَأَوْقَفْتُهَا وَقُلْتُ لَهَا يَاسَيِّدَتِي تَصَدَّقِي عَلَيَّ وَارْجِعِي لِخُطُوَاتِكِ الْكَرِيمَةِ إِلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-awqaftuhā wa-qultu lahā yāsayyidatī taṣaddaqī ʿalayya wa-irjiʿī li-khuṭuwātiki al-karīmati ilayya
sentences.l: So-I-rose, and-I-made-her-stop, and-I-said to-her: O-my-lady, be-charitable upon-me, and-return for-your-steps the-noble to-me.
sentences.i: I got up and stopped her, and said: My lady, be gracious to me, and bring your noble steps back to me.
sentences.n: تصدقي علي, "give alms to me", is a polite entreaty meaning "be kind to me". The lām in لخطواتك has the sense "for the sake of / with": "return with your noble steps". ياسيدتي is printed as one word; read yā sayyidatī.

sentences.t: فَرَجَعَتْ وَتَبَسَّمَتْ وَقَالَتْ لِأَ جْلِكِ رَجَعْتُ وَقَعَدَتْ قُصَادِي عَلَى الدُّكَّانِ
sentences.tr: fa-rajaʿat wa-tabassamat wa-qālat li-a jlīki rajaʿtu wa-qaʿadat quṣādī ʿalā al-dukkāni
sentences.l: So-she-returned, and-she-smiled, and-she-said: For-the-sake of-you I-returned. And-she-sat opposite-me on the-shop-bench.
sentences.i: She came back, smiled, and said: For your sake I have returned. And she sat down facing me on the shop's bench.
sentences.n: لا جلك is printed as two words; read li-ajlīki, لأجلك, "for your sake", split in the middle. In the pointing the first half carries the lām and the hamza, and the second half the rest; the words are a single unit. قصادي is the colloquial "opposite me, facing me" (Classical قبالتي, تجاهي).

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لِبَدْرِالدِّينِ هَذِهِ التَّفْصِيلَةُ كَمْ شِرَاؤُهَا عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu li-badri al-dīni hādhihi al-tafṣīlatu kam shirāʾuhā ʿalayka
sentences.l: So-I-said to-Badr-al-Dīn: This the-dress-length, how-much its-buying upon-you?
sentences.i: I said to Badr al-Dīn: This length, what did it cost you to buy?
sentences.n: شراؤها عليك, "its purchase upon you", is the usual way to ask what something stands one in.

sentences.t: قَالَ أَلْفٌ وَمِائَةُ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: qāla alfun wa-miʾatu dirhamin
sentences.l: He-said: A-thousand and-a-hundred dirhams.
sentences.i: He said: Eleven hundred dirhams.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ وَلَكَ مِائَةُ دِرْهَمٍ فَائِدَةً فَهَاتِ وَرَقَةً أَكْتُبْ لَكَ فِيهَا ثَمَنَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu wa-laka miʾatu dirhamin fāʾidatan fa-hāti waraqatan aktub laka fīhā thamanahā
sentences.l: So-I-said to-him: And-to-you a-hundred dirhams (as) profit; so bring a-paper (that) I-write for-you on-it its-price.
sentences.i: I said to him: You have a hundred dirhams profit. Now bring a sheet and I will write out the price for you on it.
sentences.n: فائدة, "as profit", stands as a loose accusative of purpose. هات is the imperative "bring" (the Classical imperative of آتى, in speech هات); the next verb, اكتب, follows with no linking particle.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْتُ التَّفْصِيلَةَ مِنْهُ وَكَتَبْتُ لَهُ وَرَقَةً بِخَطِّي وَأَعْطَيْتُهَا التَّفْصِيلَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhtu al-tafṣīlata minhu wa-katabtu lahu waraqatan bi-khaṭṭī wa-aʿṭaytuhā al-tafṣīlata
sentences.l: So-I-took the-dress-length from-him, and-I-wrote for-him a-paper with-my-hand, and-I-gave-her the-dress-length.
sentences.i: I took the length from him, wrote him a note in my own hand, and gave her the length.
sentences.n: Here the pronoun of ا^َعْطَيْتُهَا ("I gave her") is the lady, and the second object is the cloth: aʿṭaytuhā al-tafṣīlata, "I gave her the dress-length". بخطي is "in my own hand".

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ لَهَا خُذِي أَنْتِ رُوحِي وَإِنْ شِئْتِ هَاتِي ثَمَنَهَا بِالسُّوقِ الْآتِي وَإِنْ شِئْتِ هِيَ ضِيَافَتُكِ مِنِّي
sentences.tr: wa-qultu lahā khudhī anti rūḥī wa-in shiʾti hātī thamanahā bi-al-sūqi al-ātī wa-in shiʾti hiya ḍiyāfatuki minnī
sentences.l: And-I-said to-her: Take, you my-soul, and-if you-wish bring its-price in-the-market the-coming, and-if you-wish it-is your-hospitality from-me.
sentences.i: And I said to her: Take it, my soul. If you wish, bring its price at the next market, or if you wish, it is my hospitality to you.
sentences.n: خذي انت روحي is "take it, you (are) my soul", an endearment. السوق الآتي, "the coming market", is the next market day, when she could pay. The second condition makes the cloth a gift, in the idiom of ضيافة, hospitality.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا وَرَزَقَكَ مَالِي وَجَعَلَكَ بَعْلِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat jazāka Allāhu khayran wa-razaqaka mālī wa-jaʿalaka baʿlī
sentences.l: So-she-said: Requite-you God (with) good, and-provided-you my-wealth, and-made-you my-husband.
sentences.i: She said: May God reward you well, and give you my wealth, and make you my husband.
sentences.n: A prayer in the perfect tense ("God requite you") stands for a wish. وجعلك بعلي, "and made you my husband", is a bold wish: the lady is saying outright that she would have him as her husband. The text takes this as the prayer God then accepts, in the next sentence.

sentences.t: فَتَقَبَّلَ اللَّهُ دُعَاءَهَا ثُمَّ قُلْتُ لَهَا يَا سَيِّدَتِي اجْعَلِي هَذِهِ التَّفْصِيلَةَ لَكِ وَلَكِ أَيْضًا مِثْلَهَا وَدَعِينِي أَنْظُرْ وَجْهَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-taqabbala Allāhu duʿāʾahā thumma qultu lahā yā sayyidatī ijʿalī hādhihi al-tafṣīlata laki wa-laki ayḍan mithlahā wa-daʿīnī anẓur wajhaki
sentences.l: So-accepted God her-prayer. Then I-said to-her: O my-lady, make this the-dress-length for-you, and-for-you also its-like, and-let-me (that) I-look-at your-face.
sentences.i: And God accepted her prayer. Then I said to her: My lady, take this length as yours, and another like it besides, and let me look upon your face.
sentences.n: The narrator tells us that God granted her prayer: the wish that he become her husband is going to come true. دعيني انظر is "let me look", with the second verb in the jussive, "that I may look".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَيْتُ وَجْهَهَا نَظْرَةً أَعْقَبَتْنِي أَلْفَ حَسْرَةٍ وَتَعَلَّقَ قَلْبِي بِمَحَبَّتِهَا فَصِرْتُ لَاأَمْلِكُ عَقْلِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾaytu wajhahā naẓratan aʿqabatnī alfa ḥasratin wa-taʿallaqa qalbī bi-maḥabbatihā fa-ṣirtu lāamliku ʿaqlī
sentences.l: And-when I-saw her-face — a-glance (that) followed-me (with) a-thousand sighs — and-my-heart clung with-love-of-her, so-I-became not-I-own my-mind.
sentences.i: When I saw her face, in one glance that left a thousand regrets behind it, my heart was bound to her in love, and I could no longer hold my wits.
sentences.n: I read نظرة اعقبتني الف حسرة as "a glance that left a thousand sighs after it": the glance is the cause, and the sighs (حسرة, longing or regret) follow it. لااملك is printed as one word, لا أملك, "I do not own"; read lā amliku. The imperfect after صرت, "I became (one who) does not own", is a common construction.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَرْخَتِ الشِّعْرِيَّةَ وَأَخَذَتِ التَّفْصِيلَةَ وَقَالَتْ يَاسَيِّدِي لَاتُوحِشْنِي
sentences.tr: thumma arkhati al-shiʿriyyata wa-akhadhati al-tafṣīlata wa-qālat yāsayyidī lātūḥishnī
sentences.l: Then she-let-down the-veil, and-she-took the-dress-length, and-she-said: O-my-master, not-make-me-desolate.
sentences.i: Then she let down her veil, took the length, and said: My lord, do not leave me lonely.
sentences.n: لاتوحشني is printed as one word, لا توحشني; read lā tūḥishnī. "Do not make me desolate" is a farewell asking him not to be a stranger, not to stay away. ياسيدي is also one word in print.

sentences.t: وَقَدْوَلَّتْ وَقَعَدْتُ أَنَا فِى الْقَيْصَرِيَّةِ إِلَى بَعْدِ الْعَصْرِ وَأَنَا غَائِبُ الْعَقْلِ
sentences.tr: wa-qadwallat wa-qaʿadtu anā fī al-qayṣariyyati ilā baʿdi al-ʿaṣri wa-anā ghāʾibu al-ʿaqli
sentences.l: And-she-had-turned-away, and-I-sat, I, in the-qaysariyya till after the-afternoon, and-I (was) absent-of the-mind.
sentences.i: She was gone. And I sat on in the Qayṣariyya until after the afternoon, absent in my wits.
sentences.n: وقدولت is printed as one word, وقد ولت, "and she had turned away". فى is printed with ى for ي: read fī. غائب العقل is "absent of mind", i.e. dazed.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ تَحَكَّمَ الْحُبُّ عِنْدِي فَمِنْ شِدَّةِ مَاحَصَلَ لِي مِنَ الْحُبِّ قُمْتُ وَسَأَلْتُ التَّاجِرَ عَنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qad taḥakkama al-ḥubbu ʿindī fa-min shiddati māḥaṣala lī mina al-ḥubbi qumtu wa-saʾaltu al-tājira ʿanhā
sentences.l: And-already love had-taken-command with-me; so from the-intensity-of what-befell to-me from the-love, I-rose, and-I-asked the-merchant about-her.
sentences.i: Love had taken command of me, and from the sheer force of what I felt I got up and asked the merchant about her.
sentences.n: ماحصل is printed as one word, ما حصل, "what befell". من شدة ما حصل لي من الحب has two من: the first "from (the force of)", the second "of (love)".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ هَذِهِ صَاحِبَةُ مَالٍ وَهِيَ بِنْتُ وَاحِدٍ أَمِيرٍ مَاتَ وَالِدُهَا وَخَلَّفَ مَالًاكَثِيرًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla hādhihi ṣāḥibatu mālin wa-hiya bintu wāḥidin amīrin māta wāliduhā wa-khallafa mālākathīran
sentences.l: So-he-said: This-one (is) an-owner-of wealth, and-she (is) the-daughter-of one emir; her-father died, and-he-left wealth much.
sentences.i: He said: She is a woman of means, the daughter of an emir. Her father is dead and left a great fortune.
sentences.n: واحد امير, "one emir", is the colloquial indefinite: "a certain emir". مالاكثيرا is printed as one word, مالا كثيرا, "much wealth".

sentences.t: فَوَدَّعْتُهُ وَانْصَرَفْتُ وَجِئْتُ لِلْخَانِ فَقَدَّمَ لِي الْعَشَاءَ
sentences.tr: fa-waddaʿtuhu wa-inṣaraftu wa-jiʾtu li-al-khāni fa-qaddama lī al-ʿashāʾa
sentences.l: So-I-bade-him-farewell, and-I-departed, and-I-came to-the-khan; so-he-served to-me the-supper.
sentences.i: I took my leave of him and went away, and came to the khan, where the servant set supper before me.
sentences.n: The one who served supper is the khan's servant. In جئت للخان the lām stands where Classical Arabic would use إلى, "to".

sentences.t: فَافْتَكَرْتُهَا فَلَمْ آكُلْ شَيْئًا وَنِمْتُ فَلَمْ يَجِئْنِي نَوْمٌ فَسَهِرْتُ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-iftakartuhā fa-lam ākul shayʾan wa-nimtu fa-lam yajiʾnī nawmun fa-sahirtu ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: So-I-thought-of-her, and-I-did-not eat anything; and-I-lay-down, and-sleep-did-not come-to-me; so-I-stayed-awake till the-morning.
sentences.i: I kept thinking of her, and could not eat a bite. I lay down, but sleep would not come to me, and I stayed awake until morning.
sentences.n: افتكر is the colloquial "to think of, recall" (Classical تذكر).

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ لَبِسْتُ بِدْلَةً غَيْرَالَّتِي كَانَتْ عَلَيَّ وَشَرِبْتُ قَدَحَ شَرَابٍ وَفَطَرْتُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ قَلِيلٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu labistu bidlatan ghayra-al-latī kānat ʿalayya wa-sharibtu qadaḥa sharābin wa-faṭartu ʿalā shayʾin qalīlin
sentences.l: So-I-rose, I-wore a-suit other-than-the-one-which was on-me, and-I-drank a-cup-of drink, and-I-broke-fast on a-thing little.
sentences.i: So I got up, put on a different suit from the one I had been wearing, drank a cup of wine, and broke my fast on a little food.
sentences.n: غيرالتي is printed as one word, غير التي, "other than the one which"; I keep it as one token. The first two verbs come with no "and" between them (قمت لبست, "I rose, I put on"), a plain run-on of actions. فطر على is "to break the fast with".

sentences.t: وَجِئْتُ دُكَّانَ التَّاجِرِ فَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِ وَجَلَسْتُ عِنْدَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-jiʾtu dukkāna al-tājiri fa-sallamtu ʿalayhi wa-jalastu ʿindahu
sentences.l: And-I-came the-shop-of the-merchant, and-I-greeted on-him, and-I-sat with-him.
sentences.i: Then I came to the merchant's shop, greeted him, and sat down beside him.
sentences.n: جئت دكان has no إلى: the place one comes to can stand bare in the accusative. The merchant is Badr al-Dīn, named a few lines on.

sentences.t: فَجَاءَتِ الصَّبِيَّةُ عَلَى عَادَتِهَا وَعَلَيْهَا بِدْلَةٌ أَفْخَرُ مِنَ الْأُولَى وَمَعَهَا جَارِيَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾati al-ṣabiyyatu ʿalā ʿādatihā wa-ʿalayhā bidlatun afkharu mina al-ūlā wa-maʿahā jāriyatun
sentences.l: So-came the-young-woman upon her-custom, and-on-her a-suit more-splendid than the-first, and-with-her a-slave-girl.
sentences.i: The young woman came as was her custom, wearing a suit finer than the first, and with her was a slave-girl.

sentences.t: وَسَلَّمَتْ عَلَيَّ دُونَ بَدْرَالدِّينِ
sentences.tr: wa-sallamat ʿalayya dūna Badra-al-Dīni
sentences.l: And-she-greeted on-me, without Badr-al-Dīn.
sentences.i: She greeted me, and not Badr al-Dīn.
sentences.n: دون is "to the exclusion of": she greeted me alone. بدرالدين is printed as one word, the merchant's name; I keep it as one token.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ بِلِسَانٍ فَصِيحٍ مَا سَمِعْتُ أَعْذَبَ وَلَاحْلَا مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat bi-lisānin faṣīḥin mā samiʿtu aʿdhaba wa-lāḥlā minhu
sentences.l: And-she-said, in-a-tongue fluent (not I-heard sweeter and-not-sweeter than-it):
sentences.i: And she said, in a fluent tongue (I never heard one sweeter or lovelier),
sentences.n: The narrator breaks in with an aside about her voice; the words she says follow in the next unit. ولاحلا is printed as one word, and it can only be ولا أحلى, "and not sweeter", with the alif of أحلى lost and the final ى printed as ا. I point it as printed. منه, "than it", refers back to the tongue (لسان).

sentences.t: أَرْسِلْ مَعِي مَنْ يَقْبِضُ الْأَلْفَ وَالْمِائَتَيْنِ دِرْهَمٍ ثَمَنَ التَّفْصِيلَةِ
sentences.tr: arsil maʿī man yaqbiḍu al-alfa wa-al-miʾatayni dirhamin thamana al-tafṣīlati
sentences.l: Send with-me one-who he-takes the-thousand and-the-two-hundred dirham, price-of the-cut-length.
sentences.i: "Send someone with me to collect the twelve hundred dirhams, the price of the cloth length."
sentences.n: الالف والمائتين درهم is "the 1,200 dirhams", with a singular noun after the number, as colloquial usage has it. التفصيلة is a length of cloth cut for a garment, which the heroine bought in the shop. ارسل is pointed as an imperative.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا وَأَيْشَ الْعَجَلَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā wa-aysh al-ʿajalatu
sentences.l: So-I-said to-her: And-what the-haste?
sentences.i: So I said to her, "And what is the hurry?"
sentences.n: ايش is the colloquial "what?", short for أي شيء. It is a Middle Arabic form; the Classical would be ما.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَاعَدِ مْنَاكَ وَنَاوَلَتْنِي الثَّمَنَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lāʿadi mnāka wa-nāwalatnī al-thamana
sentences.l: So-she-said: Not-we-lost you; and-she-handed-me the-price.
sentences.i: She said, "May we never lose you," and handed me the money.
sentences.n: لاعد مناك is printed as two words but is the stock phrase لا عدمناك, "may we not lose you", a courteous "thank you". I point it as printed, split where the print splits it: لَاعَدِ + مْنَاكَ.

sentences.t: وَقَعَدْتُ أَتَحَدَّثُ وَإِيَّاهَا فَأَوْمَيْتُ لَهَا بِالْإِشَارَةِ فَفَهِمَتْ أَنِّي أُرِيدُ وِصَالَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qaʿadtu ataḥaddathu wa-iyyāhā fa-awmaytu lahā bi-al-ishārati fa-fahimat annī urīdu wiṣālahā
sentences.l: And-I-sat I-converse and-her; and-I-signed to-her with-the-sign; and-she-understood that-I I-want union-with-her.
sentences.i: I sat talking with her, and then I made a sign to her, and she understood that I wanted to lie with her.
