sentences.n: وإياها, "and her", stands for "with her" (colloquial; Classical would be معها). أوميت is the print's form of أومأت, "I signalled", with the hamza dropped and the verb treated as a weak one; I point what is printed. وصال is union, here frankly sexual.

sentences.t: فَقَامَتْ عَلَى عَجَلٍ مِنْهَا وَاسْتَوْحَشَتْ مِنِّي وَقَلْبِي مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāmat ʿalā ʿajalin minhā wa-istawḥashat minnī wa-qalbī mutaʿalliqun bihā
sentences.l: So-she-rose in haste from-her, and-she-felt-estranged from-me, while-my-heart attached to-her.
sentences.i: She rose in haste and shrank away from me, while my heart clung to her.
sentences.n: استوحش من is "to feel ill at ease with, to recoil from". The last clause, وقلبي متعلق بها, is a circumstantial clause: "and my heart (all the while) attached to her".

sentences.t: وَخَرَجْتُ أَنَا خَارِجَ السُّوقِ فِي أَثَرِهَا وَإِذَا بِجَارِيَةٍ أَتَتْنِي وَقَالَتْ يَاسَيِّدِي كَلِّمْ سِتِّي
sentences.tr: wa-kharajtu anā khārija al-sūqi fī atharihā wa-idhā bi-jāriyatin atatnī wa-qālat yāsayyidī kallim sittī
sentences.l: And-I-went-out, I, outside the-market, in her-track; and-behold, with-a-slave-girl she-came-to-me and-said: O-my-master, speak-to my-lady.
sentences.i: I went out of the market after her, and behold, a slave-girl came up to me and said, "My master, speak to my lady."
sentences.n: وإذا بجارية is the "and behold" idiom, where بِـ only marks what appears. ياسيدي is printed as one word, يا سيدي. ستي is the colloquial form of سيدتي, "my lady".

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبْتُ وَقُلْتُ مَايَعْرِفُنِي هُنَا أَحَدٌ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjabtu wa-qultu māyaʿrifunī hunā aḥadun
sentences.l: So-I-was-astonished, and-I-said: Not-knows-me here anyone.
sentences.i: I was astonished and said, "No one here knows me."
sentences.n: مايعرفني is printed as one word, ما يعرفني.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ يَا سَيِّدِي مَا أَسْرَعَ مَانَسِيتَهَا سِتِّي الَّتِي كَانَتِ الْيَوْمَ عَلَى دُكَّانِ التَّاجِرِ فُلَانٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-jāriyatu yā sayyidī mā asraʿa mānasītahā sittī al-latī kānati al-yawma ʿalā dukkāni al-tājiri fulānin
sentences.l: So-said the-slave-girl: O my-master, how swift you-forgot-her, my-lady who was today at the-shop-of the-merchant so-and-so.
sentences.i: The slave-girl said, "My master, how quickly you have forgotten her: my lady, who was today at the shop of the merchant So-and-so."
sentences.n: ما أسرع ما نسيتها is the exclamation "how quickly you forgot her!", with the second ما printed glued to the verb (مانسيتها). فلان, "so-and-so", stands for the merchant's name.

sentences.t: فَمَشَيْتُ مَعَهَا إِلَى الصَّيْرَفِيِّ فَلَمَّا رَأَتْنِي أَزْوَتْنِي لِجَانِبِهَا وَقَالَتْ يَا حَبِيبِي
sentences.tr: fa-mashaytu maʿahā ilā al-ṣayrafiyyi fa-lammā raʾatnī azwatnī li-jānibihā wa-qālat yā ḥabībī
sentences.l: So-I-walked with-her to the-money-changer; and-when she-saw-me she-drew-me to-her-side, and-said: O my-beloved,
sentences.i: I walked with her to the money-changer's, and when she saw me she drew me to her side and said, "My darling,
sentences.n: الصيرفي is the money-changer, whose shop she had gone to. أزوتني is an uncommon form; I read it as the causative of زوى, "to draw in, gather", so "drew me to her side" (the sense is clear even if the form is not Classical). لجانبها: لِـ here is "to, toward", the way colloquial لِـ does the work of إلى.

sentences.t: وَقَعْتَ بِخَاطِرِي وَتَمَكَّنَ حُبُّكَ مِنْ قَلْبِي
sentences.tr: waqaʿta bi-khāṭirī wa-tamakkana ḥubbuka min qalbī
sentences.l: You-fell in-my-mind, and-your-love took-hold of my-heart.
sentences.i: You have taken hold of my mind, and love for you has settled in my heart.
sentences.n: وقع بخاطري is an idiom, "to come to my mind, to strike my fancy"; the closing quotation mark of the speech is not in the print, so the speech simply runs on across the units.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ سَاعَةِ أَنِّي رَأَيْتُكَ مَاهَنِي لِي نَوْمٌ وَلَا أَكْلٌ وَلَاشُرْبٌ
sentences.tr: wa-min sāʿati annī raʾaytuka māhanī lī nawmun wa-lā aklun wa-lāshurbun
sentences.l: And-from hour-of that-I I-saw-you, not-was-pleasant to-me sleep, and-not food, and-not-drink.
sentences.i: From the hour I saw you I have had no pleasure in sleep, or in food, or in drink."
sentences.n: من ساعة أني رأيتك is "from the moment I saw you" (Classical would be منذ). ماهني is printed with a final ي; it is the verb هنئ, "to be wholesome, pleasant" (for هَنِئَ), with the hamza dropped, as in the common phrase هنيئا. ولاشرب is printed glued, ولا شرب.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا عِنْدِي أَضْعَافُ ذَلِكَ وَالْحَالُ يُغْنِي عَنِ الشَّكْوَى
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā ʿindī aḍʿāfu dhālika wa-al-ḥālu yughnī ʿani al-shakwā
sentences.l: So-I-said to-her: With-me multiples-of that; and-the-state suffices from the-complaint.
sentences.i: I said to her, "What I feel is many times that, and the state I am in makes complaint needless."
sentences.n: عندي, "with me", is the way Arabic says "I have". والحال يغني عن الشكوى is a proverb-like saying: "the condition speaks for itself and spares you the complaint".

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَاحَبِيبِي عِنْدَكَ وَإِلَّا عِنْدِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yāḥabībī ʿindaka wa-illā ʿindī
sentences.l: So-she-said: O-my-beloved, with-you or-else with-me?
sentences.i: She said, "My darling, at your place, or at mine?"
sentences.n: ياحبيبي is printed as one word. والا is printed without hamza; it is وإلا, "or else", here a bare "or".

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَنَا رَجُلٌ غَرِيبٌ وَمَالِي مَكَانٌ يَأْوِينِي إِلَّا الْخَانُ فَإِنْ تَصَدَّقْتِ فَيَكُونُ عِنْدَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā anā rajulun gharībun wa-mālī makānun yaʾwīnī illā al-khānu fa-in taṣaddaqti fa-yakūnu ʿindaki
sentences.l: So-I-said to-her: I a-man a-stranger, and-not-to-me a-place it-shelters-me except the-inn; so-if you-gave-alms, then-it-will-be with-you.
sentences.i: I said to her, "I am a stranger here, and I have no place to shelter me but the inn; so if you would be so kind, let it be at your place."
sentences.n: تصدقت, "you have given alms", is the polite "if you would be so generous". The فَـ before يكون opens the answer to the condition, and the verb after it is in the plain indicative: "then it will be (so) with you", used as a request. مالي is printed glued, ما لي.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ نَعَمْ لَكِنِ اللَّيْلَةُ لَيْلَةُ الْجُمُعَةِ مَا فِيهَا شَيْءٌ
sentences.tr: qālat naʿam lākini al-laylatu laylatu al-jumuʿati mā fīhā shayʾun
sentences.l: She-said: Yes, but the-night night-of the-Friday, not in-it a-thing.
sentences.i: She said, "Yes, but tonight is Friday night, and there is nothing to be done in it.
sentences.n: ليلة الجمعة is the eve of Friday, that is Thursday night in our reckoning, since the Arabic day begins at sunset. ما فيها شيء is "there is nothing in it", that is, nothing can be arranged for it; the point comes in the next unit.

sentences.t: إِلَّا أَنْ كَانَ فِي غَدٍ بَعْدَ الصَّلٰوةِ صَلِّ وَ ارْكَبْ حِمَارَكَ وَاسْأَلْ عَنِ الْجَبَّانِيَةِ
sentences.tr: illā an kāna fī ghadin baʿda al-ṣalāti ṣalli wa irkab ḥimāraka wa-isʾal ʿani al-jabbāniyati
sentences.l: Except that-it-be on tomorrow after the-prayer: pray, and ride your-donkey, and-ask about the-Jabbāniyya.
sentences.i: Only tomorrow, after the prayer: pray, and ride your donkey, and ask for al-Jabbāniyya.
sentences.n: الصلوة is the old spelling of الصلاة, "the prayer" (here the Friday congregational prayer); the dagger alif marks the long ā. The print has صل و ارکب with a space after the و (the line breaks there), so I leave و as a separate token; I read صَلِّ as "pray", though a stray letter here may mean the text is slightly out of order. الجبانية is printed with a single ي; I read al-Jabbāniya, a district of Cairo by the cemeteries (jabbāna means "cemetery"). The pointing is mine.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ وَصَلْتَ فَاسْأَلْ عَنْ قَاعَةِ بَرَكَاتٍ النَّقِيبِ الْمَعْرُوفِ بِأَبِي شَامَةَ فَإِنِّي سَاكِنَةٌ هُنَاكَ
sentences.tr: fa-in waṣalta fa-isʾal ʿan qāʿati Barakātin al-naqībi al-maʿrūfi bi-Abī Shāmata fa-innī sākinatun hunāka
sentences.l: So-if you-arrive, then-ask about hall-of Barakāt the-marshal, the-known by-Abū Shāma; for-I dwelling there.
sentences.i: When you arrive, ask for the hall of Barakāt the marshal, who is known as Abū Shāma, for I live there.
sentences.n: النقيب is the naqīb, a marshal or officer of a guild or of the emirs. معروف بِـ is "known by (the name of)". I point the name بركات with tanwīn and ابي شامة as a genitive after بِـ; the print does not tell us either.

sentences.t: وَلَاتُبْطِىءْ فَإِنِّي فِي إِنْتِظَارِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-lātubṭiʾ fa-innī fī intiẓārika
sentences.l: And-not-be-slow, for-I in your-waiting.
sentences.i: Do not be slow, for I am waiting for you."
sentences.n: ولاتبطىء is printed glued, ولا تبطئ, and with the hamza on a ى seat. I point what is printed.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحْتُ فَرَحًا زَائِدًا ثُمَّ افْتَرَقْنَا وَجِئْتُ لِلْخَانِ الَّذِي أَنَا فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥtu faraḥan zāʾidan thumma iftaraqnā wa-jiʾtu li-al-khāni al-ladhī anā fīhi
sentences.l: So-I-rejoiced a-joy excessive; then we-parted; and-I-came to-the-inn which I in-it.
sentences.i: I was overjoyed, and then we parted, and I returned to the inn where I was staying.
sentences.n: فرحت فرحا زائدا is a cognate accusative, "I rejoiced an excess of joy". للخان: لِـ is "to", used as colloquial إلى.

sentences.t: وَمَضَيْتُ اللَّيْلَ سَهْرَانَ فَمَا صَدَّقْتُ أَنَّ الْفَجْرَ لَاحَ
sentences.tr: wa-maḍaytu al-layla sahrāna fa-mā ṣaddaqtu anna al-fajra lāḥa
sentences.l: And-I-passed the-night sleepless; and-not I-believed that the-dawn had-shone.
sentences.i: I spent the night without sleep, and I could hardly believe it when dawn broke.
sentences.n: اللَّيْلَ is an accusative of time, "I passed the night". ما صدقت أن is "I could hardly believe that".

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَغَيَّرْتُ مَلْبُوسِي وَتَعَطَّرْتُ وَتَطَيَّبْتُ وَأَخَذْتُ مَعِي خَمْسِينَ دِينَارًا فِي مِنْدِيلٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-ghayyartu malbūsī wa-taʿaṭṭartu wa-taṭayyabtu wa-akhadhtu maʿī khamsīna dīnāran fī mindīlin
sentences.l: So-I-rose, and-I-changed my-clothing, and-I-perfumed-myself and-I-scented-myself, and-I-took with-me fifty dinar in a-kerchief.
sentences.i: I got up, changed my clothes, put on perfume and scent, and took fifty dinars with me in a kerchief.
sentences.n: تعطرت وتطيبت is a pair of near-synonyms, "I perfumed myself and anointed myself with scent"; the pair also sets up a rhyme with the verbs before it. منديل is a cloth or kerchief, used here as a purse.

sentences.t: وَمَشَيْتُ مِنْ خَانِ مَسْرُورٍ إِلَى بَابِ زُوَيْلَةَ فَرَكِبْتُ حِمَارًا وَقُلْتُ لِصَاحِبِهِ امْشِ بِي إِلَى الْجَبَّانِيَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-mashaytu min khāni Masrūrin ilā bābi Zuwaylata fa-rakibtu ḥimāran wa-qultu li-ṣāḥibihi imshi bī ilā al-jabbāniyati
sentences.l: And-I-walked from inn-of Masrūr to gate-of Zuwayla; so-I-rode a-donkey, and-I-said to-its-owner: Walk with-me to the-Jabbāniyya.
sentences.i: I walked from the Khān of Masrūr to the Bāb Zuwayla, hired a donkey, and said to its owner, "Take me to al-Jabbāniyya."
sentences.n: باب زويلة is the Zuwayla Gate of Cairo. امش بي, "walk with me", is the colloquial "take me"; the donkey-owner walks beside his animal. صاحبه is "its owner", the donkey-man.

sentences.t: فَمَضَى فِي لَحْظَةٍ فَمَا أَسْرَعَ مَا وَقَفَ عَلَى دَرْبٍ يُقَالُ لَهُ دَرْبُ الْمِنْقَرِيِّ
sentences.tr: fa-maḍā fī laḥẓatin fa-mā asraʿa mā waqafa ʿalā darbin yuqālu lahu darbu al-Minqariyyi
sentences.l: So-he-went in a-moment; and-how swift that-he-stopped at an-alley it-is-said to-it Alley-of al-Minqarī.
sentences.i: He went off in a moment, and how quickly he stopped, at an alley called the Alley of al-Minqarī.
sentences.n: ما أسرع ما وقف is "how quickly he stopped!". The name المنقري is a nisba; I read al-Minqarī but I am not sure of the vowels, since the print gives none.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ ادْخُلِ الدَّرْبَ وَاسْأَلْ عَنْ قَاعَةِ النَّقِيبِ فَغَابَ قَلِيلًا وَقَالَ انْزِلْ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu udkhuli al-darba wa-isʾal ʿan qāʿati al-naqībi fa-ghāba qalīlan wa-qāla inzil
sentences.l: So-I-said to-him: Enter the-alley and-ask about hall-of the-marshal; so-he-was-gone a-little, and-said: Get-down.
sentences.i: I said to him, "Go into the alley and ask for the marshal's hall." He was gone for a little while, and then said, "Get down."

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ امْشِ قُدَّامِي إِلَى الْقَاعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu imshi quddāmī ilā al-qāʿati
sentences.l: So-I-said to-him: Walk in-front-of-me to the-hall.
sentences.i: I said to him, "Walk ahead of me to the hall."
sentences.n: قدامي, "in front of me", is the colloquial form; Classical has أمامي.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ لَهُ بَاكِرْ تَجِيئُنِي هُنَا وَتُوَدِّينِي
sentences.tr: wa-qultu lahu bākir tajīʾunī hunā wa-tuwaddīnī
sentences.l: And-I-said to-him: Come-early, you-come-to-me here and-you-take-me.
sentences.i: And I said to him, "Come early tomorrow, come to me here and take me back."
sentences.n: باكر is the colloquial "early, tomorrow morning", and the two verbs after it follow it with no "and" or "to" between them (تجيئني وتوديني, "you come to me and take me"), colloquial asyndesis. وَدَّى, "to take, to convey", is colloquial for Classical أَوْصَلَ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمُكَارِي بِسْمِ اللَّهِ فَنَاوَلْتُهُ رُبْعَ دِينَارٍ ذَهَبٍ فَأَخَذَهُ وَانْصَرَفَ فَطَرَقْتُ الْبَابَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-mukārī bismi Allāhi fa-nāwaltuhu rubʿa dīnārin dhahabin fa-akhadhahu wa-inṣarafa fa-ṭaraqtu al-bāba
sentences.l: So-said the-donkey-man: In-the-name-of God; so-I-handed-him quarter-of dinar, gold; so-he-took-it and-went-away; so-I-knocked the-door.
sentences.i: The donkey-man said, "In God's name," and I handed him a quarter-dinar of gold; he took it and went away, and I knocked at the door.
sentences.n: بسم الله, "in God's name", is used here as a polite "very well, at your service". ذهب, "gold", follows the coin as a plain specifier.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَتَا لِي صَبِيَّتَيْنِ صِغَارًا نُهَّدًا أَبْكَارًا كَأَنَّهُنَّ الْأَ قْمَارُ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajatā lī ṣabiyyatayni ṣighāran nuhhadan abkāran ka-annahunna al-a qmāru
sentences.l: So-the-two-came-out to-me, two-girls, small, high-breasted, virgins, as-though-they the-moons.
sentences.i: Two girls came out to me, young, full-breasted virgins, like moons.
sentences.n: The print has the dual verb فخرجتا, then صبيتين in the oblique case, and then plural adjectives and plural "they" (صغارا نهدا ابكارا، كأنهن); this is loose Middle Arabic agreement, and I point each word as printed. نهد describes breasts that are rising and firm. الا قمار is printed split, ال + اقمار, "the moons"; I keep the split.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لِي ادْخُلْ سَيِّدَتُنَا فِي إِنْتِظَارِكَ لَمْ تَنَمِ اللَّيْلَةَ لِفَرَحِهَا بِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lī udkhul sayyidatunā fī intiẓārika lam tanami al-layla lifaraḥihā bika
sentences.l: So-they-said to-me: Enter; our-mistress in your-waiting; she-did-not sleep the-night, for-her-joy in-you.
sentences.i: They said to me, "Come in; our mistress is waiting for you. She has not slept all night, for joy in you."
sentences.n: The print has the masculine plural فقالوا for the two girls, again loose agreement. لفرحها بك: لِـ gives the reason ("because of her joy"), and بِـ after فرح is "in" (joy in you).

sentences.t: فَدَخَلْتُ إِلَى قَاعَةٍ مُعَلَّقَةٍ بِسَبْعَةِ أَبْوَابٍ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhaltu ilā qāʿatin muʿallaqatin bi-sabʿati abwābin
sentences.l: So-I-entered to a-hall hung with-seven doors.
sentences.i: I went into a hall hung with seven doors,
sentences.n: معلقة is literally "hung"; it may mean a raised, upper hall, or one fitted with hung doors. I read it as the second, but the sense is not certain.

sentences.t: وَدَائِرُهَا شَبَابِيكُ مُطِلَّةٌ عَلَى بُسْتَانٍ
sentences.tr: wa-dāʾiruhā shabābīku muṭillatun ʿalā bustānin
sentences.l: And-its-circuit windows, overlooking on a-garden,
sentences.i: with windows all around it, looking out on a garden
sentences.n: دائرها is "its circuit, all around it": the print has no verb, so the windows are simply set beside the hall.

sentences.t: فِيهِ مِنَ الْفَوَاكِهِ أَلْوَانٌ وَبِهِ أَنْهَارٌ دَافِقَةٌ وَطُيُورُهَا نَاطِقَةٌ
sentences.tr: fīhi mina al-fawākihi alwānun wa-bihi anhārun dāfiqatun wa-ṭuyūruhā nāṭiqatun
sentences.l: in-it, of the-fruits, colours; and-in-it rivers gushing, and-its-birds speaking.
sentences.i: with fruits of every colour in it, and gushing streams, and birds that sing.
sentences.n: من الفواكه ألوان is "kinds of fruit" (literally "colours of fruits"). دافقة / ناطقة rhyme: this stretch of description is in rhymed prose. ناطقة is "speaking", and the birds are said to speak, that is, to sing. The suffix in طيورها looks back to the garden (بستان) taken as feminine.

sentences.t: وَهِيَ مُبَيَّضَةٌ بِبَيَاضٍ سُلْطَانِيٍّ يَرَى الْإِنْسَانُ وَجْهَهُ فِيهَا
sentences.tr: wa-hiya mubayyaḍatun bi-bayāḍin sulṭāniyyin yarā al-insānu wajhahu fīhā
sentences.l: And-it whitened with-whiteness sultanic, sees the-person his-face in-it.
sentences.i: The hall was whitewashed with a royal whiteness, so that a person could see his face in it,
sentences.n: ببياض سلطاني is "with a sultan's whiteness", the finest plaster. The relative clause يرى الانسان وجهه فيها has no connective: "(such that) a man sees his face in it".

sentences.t: وَسَقْفُهَا مُقَرْبَصٌ بِذَهَبٍ وَطِرَازَاتٌ مَكْتُوبَةٌ بِاللَّازَوَرْدِ قَدْ حَرَتْ أَوْصَافًا حَسَنَةً وَأَضَاءَتْ لِلنَّاظِرِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-saqfuhā muqarbaṣun bi-dhahabin wa-ṭirāzātun maktūbatun bi-al-lāzawardi qad ḥarat awṣāfan ḥasanatan wa-aḍāʾat li-al-nāẓirīna
sentences.l: And-its-ceiling vaulted with-gold, and-bands written with-the-lapis-lazuli, it-has ḥarat qualities beautiful, and-it-shone for-the-beholders.
sentences.i: its ceiling vaulted and worked with gold, and bands of ornament inscribed in lapis lazuli, which had gathered beautiful qualities and shone for all who looked.
sentences.n: مقربص is a rare word, and I read it as "vaulted" (from the verb قربص, to curve or arch); I am not sure of that. طرازات are bands of inscription or ornament. حرت is as printed; I suspect a misprint for حوت, "had gathered, contained", with ر for و, and I translate it that way. اضاءت here is intransitive, "shone".

sentences.t: وَأَرْضُهَا مَفْرُوشَةٌ بِالرُّخَامِ الْمُجَزَّعِ
sentences.tr: wa-arḍuhā mafrūshatun bi-al-rukhāmi al-mujazzaʿi
sentences.l: And-its-floor spread with-the-marble the-veined.
sentences.i: and its floor was laid with veined marble.
sentences.n: المجزع is "streaked, variegated", said of marble with coloured veins.

sentences.t: وَفِي وَسَطِهَا نَسْقِيَةٌ وَفِي أَرْكَانِ تِلْكَ الْفَسْقِيَةِ طُيُورٌ بِالدُّرِّوَا لْجَوْهَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-fī wasaṭihā nasqiyatun wa-fī arkāni tilka al-fasqiyyati ṭuyūrun bi-al-durrawā ljawhari
sentences.l: And-in its-middle a-basin; and-in corners-of that the-fountain-basin, birds with-the-pearls and-the-jewel.
sentences.i: In the middle of it was a basin, and in the corners of that fountain were birds of pearls and jewels,
sentences.n: نسقية is printed here, and تلك الفسقية just after it; this is surely one word, فسقية, "a fountain basin", with the first letter misprinted, and I point each as printed. بالدروا لجوهر is printed with the و-ا of والجوهر attached to the previous word: read بالدر والجوهر, "with pearls and the jewel". I keep the split where the print puts it. بِـ here shows what the birds are made of or decked with.

sentences.t: مَفْرُوشَةٌ بِالْبُسُطِ وَالْحَرِيرِ الْمُلَوَّنِ وَالْمَرَاتِبِ
sentences.tr: mafrūshatun bi-al-busuṭi wa-al-ḥarīri al-mulawwani wa-al-marātibi
sentences.l: spread with-the-carpets and-the-silk the-coloured and-the-mattresses.
sentences.i: the whole hall spread with carpets, coloured silk, and mattresses.
sentences.n: مفروشة agrees with القاعة, the hall, not with the birds; the print has no punctuation to show this. I point البسط as the plural بُسُط, "carpets". المراتب are the mattresses or cushioned seats.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلْتُ جَلَسْتُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhaltu jalastu
sentences.l: So-when I-entered, I-sat.
sentences.i: When I went in, I sat down.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْ—احِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-—āḥi
sentences.l: And-reached Shahrazād the-morning, and-she-fell-silent from the-speech the-[gap]ā-ḥ.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: This is the closing formula of the night, in rhymed prose (الصباح / المباح). In this print the last word is broken, ال—اح, with a dash where the letters مب should be. I keep it as printed and read it as الْمُبَاحِ, "the permitted". Since the print gives only ال and اح, I point just those.
